id: DeliveryTask_AboveAndLeft class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: mName: "Two-Parent Child" mDescription: "Requires both the Above and Left parents at once (AND semantics)." mIcon: DeliveryTaskIcon mIsDisabled: false mPriority: 0 mTags: - KMods.EventOnly mAdaMessages: - AdaMessage_TaskComplete mToastIcon: DeliveryTaskIcon mToastText: "You completed the Two-Parent Child task." mCoordinate: X: -1 Y: 0 # Above -> (-1, -1): Right, Left -> (-2, 0): Above # multiple flags set in parallel mParentTask: - Above - Left bRequireAllParents: true # AND: both parents must be completed first bIsEndless: false mRewards: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C Amount: 100 mCosts: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C Amount: 40 - id: DeliveryTask_UnlockSuperIngot class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: mName: "Unlock: Pure Super Ingot" mDescription: "Force-unlocks the Pure Super Ingot schematic on completion." mIcon: DeliveryTaskIcon mIsDisabled: false mPriority: 0 mTags: - KMods.EventOnly mAdaMessages: - AdaMessage_TaskComplete mToastIcon: DeliveryTaskIcon mToastText: "Pure Super Ingot production unlocked!" mCoordinate: X: -1 Y: 1 # Above -> (-1, 0): AboveAndLeft mParentTask: Above bRequireAllParents: true bIsEndless: false # force-unlocked by HandleUnlock on completion mSchematics: - /Game/YourMod/Schematics/Schematic_PureSuperIngot.Schematic_PureSuperIngot_C mRewards: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C Amount: 500 mCosts: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C Amount: 100 Five nodes, four edges: Root has no parent (the tree's entry point), Above/Right each depend on Root alone, AboveAndLeft depends on both Above and Right at once (the multi-flag case), and UnlockSuperIngot depends on AboveAndLeft.

sections.heading: Instanced dependencies and unlocks
sections.text: Delivery-task data assets accept dedicated dependencies: and unlocks: lists alongside properties:. They append to mTaskDependencies and mUnlocks; generic property ops cannot construct these instanced subobjects. assets: - id: DeliveryTask_AboveAndLeft class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask dependencies: - class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematicPurchasedDependency properties: mSchematics: - Schematic_MyPrerequisite unlocks: - class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGUnlockGiveItem properties: mItemsToGive: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C Amount: 25 Known native paths automatically remap to Blueprint implementations; exact Blueprint paths remain valid. See Base-Game Unlock Classes and Availability Dependency Classes.

sections.heading: How completing a task unlocks more of the tree
sections.text: A node becomes available once its mParentTask requirement is satisfied: - bRequireAllParents: true (the default) every flagged parent must be completed first (AND). DeliveryTask_AboveAndLeft above needs both Above and Right done. - bRequireAllParents: false any one flagged parent completing is enough (OR). Useful for a node reachable from more than one earlier branch, whichever the player finishes first. - mRequiredParentCompletions: 1 (the default) completion count each marked parent must reach. Raise it for branches behind repeatable tasks; AND/OR semantics then compare parents against same threshold. - mTaskDependencies (an availability-dependency list, checked via AreTaskDependenciesMet) adds further gating on top of the parent-tree check itself a schematic purchase, a research unlock, whatever the dependency subclass checks. Parent completion and mTaskDependencies are independent gates: both must pass. For an endless node (bIsEndless: true), "unlocking more" also means more concurrent task slots: mMaxTasks caps how many of that node's rolled tasks can be active/queued at once (INDEX_NONE/-1 for uncapped), and mAmountMultiplierCurve / mAbsolutMaxItemAmount scale the reward amounts up as the player completes more rounds of it so the effective "how much can I get from this node" grows over time even though the node itself doesn't move in the tree.

sections.heading: Unlock example force-unlocking a schematic
sections.text: DeliveryTask_UnlockSuperIngot above is the unlock example: its mSchematics force-unlocks Schematic_PureSuperIngot via HandleUnlock on completion, regardless of whether the player could normally research or purchase it another way the same mechanism unlocks: / dependencies: use on schematics themselves, just triggered from a delivery-task completion instead. mRewards/ mCosts on that same node are the plain item grant/cost, independent of the schematic unlock.

pages.title: End-to-end pack
pages.description: Build one pack with an item, recipe, schematic, sink points, translation, a dynamic data asset, RRDA edits, and a safe id rename.

sections.heading: End-to-end pack
sections.text: The individual type pages (Items, Resources, Buildings, Unlocks, Recipes, Schematics, Research Trees, Sink Points, Game Tags, Localization, Data Assets) each explain one document type in isolation. This example shows how several types live together in one pack and reference each other without any include: juggling, because the stage order already handles it for you. A single pack folder holds every file below side by side, one document type per file, all under one pack root: <your-mod>/DataForge/ pack.yml super-ingot.item.yml super-ingot.recipe.yml super-ingot.schematic.yml super-ingot.sinkpoints.yml de.localization.yml cleaner.dataasset.yml faster-boilers.cdo.yml :::note Every file above is shown separately for clarity, but that's a choice, not a requirement. Any of them can be merged into one file with --- separators (see Multiple Documents Per File). For example, super-ingot.item.yml and super-ingot.sinkpoints.yml could just as well be a single super-ingot.yml with two type:-tagged documents, useful for small, self-contained additions where a whole folder of one-liners feels like overkill. This page keeps them split because the individual type pages link straight to their matching file. :::

sections.heading: pack.yml
sections.text: pack.yml is optional. A folder without one just forms an implicit pack named after its directory. Once you care about save compatibility across versions, though, you want one. Three fields matter here. ref is the stable pack reference embedded in every generated class path (/KDataForge/Gen/<ref>.Gen_<ref>_<Id>) that this pack produces. name is the human readable display name. version is an informational semver value used in conflict reports. This pack declares its ref up front, so the redirect added later has something stable to anchor to: ref: MyPack # the save-persistence contract generated classes embed this ref name: My Content Pack version: 1.0.0

sections.heading: The item
sections.text: An item document generates a brand-new ItemDescriptor subclass and sets its CDO properties in one step. super-ingot.item.yml parents a new item off the vanilla iron ingot and configures three things on it. It gets a localized display name using block key, ns, and source fields rather than a plain string, so the German translation below can target it. It also gets a description, and an SS_HUGE stack size, which is an EStackSize enum value rather than a plain count: # file: super-ingot.item.yml type: item items: - id: MySuperIngot parent: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties: mDisplayName: key: MySuperIngot_Name ns: MyPack source: Super Ingot mDescription: A far superior ingot. mStackSize: SS_HUGE # EStackSize enum, not a plain count This generates /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot. The path is deterministic and id-based, so every other file below can reference it safely regardless of load order.

sections.heading: The recipe
sections.text: A recipe document describes ingredients, products, craft duration, and which buildable(s) can craft it, all as CDO properties on a generated FGRecipe subclass. This one consumes 2 iron ingots, produces 1 of the item generated above, takes 4 seconds, and runs in a Smelter Mk.1: # file: super-ingot.recipe.yml type: recipe recipes: - id: Recipe_MySuperIngot properties: mDisplayName: Super Ingot mIngredients: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C Amount: 2 mProduct: - ItemClass: /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot Amount: 1 mManufactoringDuration: 4.0 mProducedIn: - /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/SmelterMk1/Build_SmelterMk1.Build_SmelterMk1_C No include: is needed here. Items always finishes before Recipes starts, so the product reference above just works.

sections.heading: The schematic (with an `FGUnlockRecipe` unlock)
sections.text: A schematic document generates a milestone and, through an inline unlocks: list, wires up what it grants. Here that is an FGUnlockRecipe unlock pointing back at the recipe generated above. Completing this schematic is what actually makes the recipe available to the player: # file: super-ingot.schematic.yml type: schematic schematics: - id: Schematic_MySuperIngot properties: mDisplayName: Super Ingot Smelting mTechTier: 2 mTimeToComplete: 60 mCost: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C Amount: 50 unlocks: - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockRecipe.BP_UnlockRecipe_C properties: mRecipes: - /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_Recipe_MySuperIngot register: true, which is the default, registers this schematic. From there, SML's auto-propagation takes over: the recipe and its items register right along with it.

sections.heading: Sink points for the item
sections.text: A sinkpoints document is a small standalone table of AWESOME Sink point values keyed by item class. This one gives the freshly generated ingot 8 points on the Default track: # file: super-ingot.sinkpoints.yml type: sinkpoints track: Default entries: - item: /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot points: 8 Remember that this one specifically needs a session restart to take effect. See Sink Points for why.

sections.heading: German translation
sections.text: A localization document maps translation keys (or exact source-text overrides) to translated strings for one namespace and culture. Here the culture is de, which prefix-matches so it also covers de-DE: # file: de.localization.yml type: localization namespace: MyPack culture: de # prefix-matched: also applies for de-DE entries: MySuperIngot_Name: 'Superbarren' KeyWithSource: source: 'Super Ingot Smelting' text: 'Superbarren-Verhüttung' # override by source text The item's mDisplayName used localized FText fields (key: MySuperIngot_Name, ns: MyPack, and source:), so the simple key entry above translates it directly. This one _is_ loaded at session start: you can iterate on translations without restarting.

sections.heading: Dynamic data asset: KAPI cleaner item
sections.text: A dataasset document creates a brand-new UPrimaryDataAsset instance (not a class) of any KAPI subclass and announces it to the asset registry. A conditions: block with hasMod: KAPI gates the whole document so it cleanly skips if KAPI isn't installed, rather than erroring: # file: cleaner.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: CleanerItem_MyFluid class: /Script/KAPI.KAPICleanerItemDescription # any UPrimaryDataAsset subclass properties: mProductionTime: 4.0 mInFluid: ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Water/Desc_Water.Desc_Water_C Amount: 1000 This creates a real PrimaryDataAsset instance and announces it to the asset registry. KDataForge then triggers KAPI's own rescan, so it picks the new asset up. See Data Assets for the full mechanism and every KAPI asset type it applies to.

sections.heading: Editing RefinedR&D data assets (RRDA)
sections.text: Existing data-asset instances from other mods are edited with a plain cdo document too, using allAssetsOfClass: to hit every instance of a class at once. This patch halves the cook time of every RefinedR&D boiler, whether it is RefinedPower's, FicsitFarming's, or anyone else's built on RefinedRDApi. It is gated the same way, behind a conditions: block with hasMod:: # file: faster-boilers.cdo.yml type: cdo conditions: hasMod: RefinedRDApi patches: - allAssetsOfClass: /Script/RefinedRDApi.RRDABoilerDataAsset properties: mDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.5 # every RefinedPower/FicsitFarming boiler produces twice as fast No RefinedRDApi dependency is needed in your .uplugin. The rescan that picks this up runs via reflection, gated purely by the hasMod condition.

sections.heading: Renaming an id later: `redirects:`
sections.text: Renaming the file super-ingot.item.yml is always safe. Renaming the id MySuperIngot, however, changes the generated class path, which would orphan any save that already has the item. Declare the rename in pack.yml instead: # pack.yml (version 2.0.0 of this pack) ref: MyPack name: My Content Pack version: 2.0.0 redirects: MySuperIngot: SuperIngotMk2 # OldId: NewId The class is now generated as Gen_MyPack_SuperIngotMk2, and FCoreRedirects resolves the old class path in existing saves to it. Items already in old saves load without warnings.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - Something in this pack didn't apply? /kdf report in chat prints every warning and error, along with the file and line that caused it. A broken file only skips itself: the rest of the pack still loads. - Renamed an id and now old saves complain? That's exactly what redirects: is for, as covered above. If you forgot to add one before shipping the rename, you can add it retroactively: it's read at load time, not baked into the save. - Ready to go deeper on one piece of this? Jump to the type page for whichever document you're extending: Items, Recipes, Schematics, Sink Points, Localization, or Data Assets.

pages.title: Adding KAPI data assets
pages.description: Copy-pasteable "type: dataasset" examples for air collectors, cleaners, modular miners, slug breeding, extractor and resource allow lists, and delivery-task nodes.

sections.heading: Adding KAPI data assets
sections.text: These type: dataasset examples create new instances for every KAPI data asset type. To edit *existing* instances through type: cdo, see Data Assets. Four of the five examples below use real property values from actual shipped Satisfactory Plus / KLib content, so the numbers are realistic, not placeholders. The fifth (extractor/resource allow-lists) is illustrative since no shipped instance of that type exists to read from.

sections.heading: UKAPIAirCollectorData: air collector production
sections.text: Each Air Collector resource is its own UKAPIAirCollectorData instance the DataAsset registers a new gas/resource the Air Collector can extract, it does not patch an existing one. See the full property reference for every field; the example below mirrors Satisfactory Plus's own shipped "Air Collector extract Toxic Air via Resource Nodes" asset. Note bUseHightBasesdProduction selects one of two mutually exclusive production models. here it's false, so mMaxHit/mProductionPerHit are the active fields and mProduceItemCountMin/Max/Base (the other model) are omitted entirely, not just left at defaults. # file: air-collector-toxic-air.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: AirCollector_ToxicAirNode class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIAirCollectorData properties: mRecipePrio: 100 mRangeToScan: 2500 bCheckNodes: true mTraceChannel: - ObjectTypeQuery1 - ObjectTypeQuery2 - ObjectTypeQuery9 - ObjectTypeQuery6 mItemClass: /KLib/Assets/Ressources/Raw/Gas/Desc_ToxicAir.Desc_ToxicAir_C mProductionTime: 6 bUseHightBasesdProduction: false mMaxHit: 2 mProductionPerHit: 6000

sections.heading: `UKAPICleanerItemDescription`: Filtrator (Cleaner) recipes
sections.text: A dataasset document targeting KAPICleanerItemDescription creates a brand-new Filtrator recipe: which input fluid it consumes, what it outputs, and any bonus items produced alongside the main conversion. See the full property reference for every field, including FKAPICleanerInfo. The example below reproduces Satisfactory Plus's own "Filtrator filter Wastewater" recipe: 6000 wastewater in, 4000 clean water out over 6 seconds, plus two bypass products (crushed zinc and crushed caterium) that come out independent of the main fluid conversion. mCleanerItemInfo is left out entirely here, it's optional, and this real recipe ships with no extra cleaner item required (mCleanerItemInfo.mProduceItem is None in the shipped asset). # file: filtrator-wastewater.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: CleanerItem_WasteWater class: /Script/KAPI.KAPICleanerItemDescription properties: bSkipUnlockCheck: false mProductionTime: 6 mInFluid: ItemClass: /KLib/Assets/Ressources/Raw/Fluids/Desc_Wastewater.Desc_Wastewater_C Amount: 6000 mOutFluid: ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Water/Desc_Water.Desc_Water_C Amount: 4000 mBypassProducts: - mProduceItem: /KLib/Assets/Parts/Production/Crushed/Desc_CrushedZinc.Desc_CrushedZinc_C mProductionTime: 12 mProduceAmount: 6 - mProduceItem: /KLib/Assets/Parts/Production/Crushed/Desc_CrushedCaterium.Desc_CrushedCaterium_C mProductionTime: 12 mProduceAmount: 6

sections.heading: UKAPIModularMinerDescription: modular miner ore entries
sections.text: Full property reference. Each UKAPIModularMinerDescription instance registers one raw-resource entry the KAPI modular miner can extract, its rarity/found flavor text, node screenshot, which attachment modules are required or blocked, and the minimum drill tier needed. The example below mirrors a real shipped Cryolite raw-ore entry: # file: modular-miner-cryolite.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: MM_Cryolite class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIModularMinerDescription properties: mRarityText: 'Common' mFoundText: 'Can be found in every biome.' mNodeScreenshot: /SatisfactoryPlus/AssetDatas/Miner/UI/TXUI_Wiki_ResourceNode_Cryolite.TXUI_Wiki_ResourceNode_Cryolite mIsFallbackDescriptor: false mNeededModules: - /KAPI/Attachments/ModularMiner/Attachment_MM_MiningHead.Attachment_MM_MiningHead_C mPreventModules: - /KLib/Assets/Buildings/ModularExtractor/Modules/Smelter/Build_SmelterModule.Build_SmelterModule_C mResourceClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/RawQuartz/Desc_RawQuartz.Desc_RawQuartz_C mDrillTier: 1 mFluidInfo and mModuleInformation are optional TMap fields (keyed by an item class and a waste-producer module class respectively) for entries that feed fluid or waste-producer modules, see the property reference for their map-key/value shapes. A resource entry that doesn't use either module type, like this one, works fine without them. mScannerTier is unused and left out entirely.

sections.heading: UKAPISugHatchingData: slug breeding & incubation
sections.text: Defines a slug species end to end: what it hatches from, how the incubator raises it, and its breeding-cycle behavior. See the full property reference for every field, including the fluid-incubator properties (mTankTier, mFluidConsume, mFluidClass, mFluidConsumeTime) left out below since bRequireFluid is false here. The example reproduces the shipped Red Slug breeder, trimmed to two mPossibleSlugs entries for readability. # file: kapi-slug-red.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: RedSlugBreeder class: /Script/KAPI.KAPISugHatchingData properties: mSlug: /KLib/Assets/Buildings/SlugHatching/Desc/Slugs/SlugDesc_Red.SlugDesc_Red_C mEgg: /KLib/Assets/Buildings/SlugHatching/Desc/Eggs/EggDesc_Red.EggDesc_Red_C mEggColor: R: 1 G: 1 B: 1 A: 1 mSlugTier: -1 mHatchDuration: 10 mPowerConsume: 0.1 mIncubatorTier: 1 bRequireFluid: false mPossibleSlugs: - mSlug: /KLib/Assets/Buildings/SlugHatching/Desc/Slugs/SlugDesc_Red.SlugDesc_Red_C mProductionCount: 1 mProbability: 100 mFixedChanceMultiplier: 0.1 bShouldUseFixedChance: true - mSlug: /KLib/Assets/Buildings/SlugHatching/Desc/Slugs/SlugDesc_Orange.SlugDesc_Orange_C mProductionCount: 1 mProbability: 0.38 mFixedChanceMultiplier: 1 bShouldUseFixedChance: true mProductionCountEggs: 1 mBreedingTime: 40 mDieTime: 100 mRequiredFood: /KLib/Assets/Parts/Production/Food/Desc_SnailFood_Tier_20.Desc_SnailFood_Tier_20_C mFoodConsumePerCycle: 2 mFoodDuration: 20 mComfortableWith: - /KLib/Assets/Buildings/SlugHatching/Desc/Slugs/SlugDesc_Orange.SlugDesc_Orange_C mMinHumidity: 0.8 mMaxHumidity: 0.85 mMinHeat: 80 mMaxHeat: 100 mDayTime: Any # EKAPISlugTime enum name (Any/Day/Night), not a raw number; Any is also the default

sections.heading: UKAPIExtractorAllowList: Registering new Extractors and Resources
sections.text: Unlike the other examples on this page, no shipped instance of this asset exists to read from the wiki data export has zero UKAPIExtractorAllowList entries. SF+ ships its own default allow-list as an existing default asset that mods normally type: cdo patch instead (see Data Assets); creating a brand new instance from scratch, as below, is mainly useful for a self-contained mod that wants its own allow-list rather than editing SF+'s. The values below are illustrative adjust the class paths to your own mod's classes. See Extractors → Properties for the full property reference. This is the same "hooking up a new resource type" scenario described on that reference page: a new custom extractor building needs to go in mAllowedExtractors before SF+ will treat it as a valid extractor, and a new resource descriptor needs to go in mAllowedResources before any extractor will recognize it as extractable: # file: my-extractor-allowlist.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: MyModExtractorAllowList class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIExtractorAllowList properties: mAllowedExtractors: - /Game/YourMod/Buildable/Build_YourExtractor.Build_YourExtractor_C mAllowedResources: - /Game/YourMod/Resource/Desc_YourResource.Desc_YourResource_C # mDisallowExtractors and mDisallowResources omitted no exclusions. mPriority: 0 mPriority defaults to 0; raise it only if another mod's allow/disallow list needs to be overridden for this class (see the priority note on the reference page).

sections.heading: `UKAPIDeliveryTask`: research-tree / delivery-task nodes
sections.text: UKAPIDeliveryTask places one node on a 2D coordinate grid and links it to a parent node (or several, at once) via mParentTask a bitmask property (EKAPIDeliveryTaskParent: Above/Left/Right/Bottom/AboveLeft/AboveRight/BelowLeft/BelowRight). Like UKAPIExtractorAllowList above, there's no shipped instance to read real values from this feature isn't part of Satisfactory Plus, it only needs KAPI + KPrivateCodeLib so the example below is illustrative. The interesting part is mParentTask accepting more than one flag at once. Use one scalar name for one parent or a YAML sequence for several. With WITH_METADATA, retained property metadata, and the enum already loaded, KDataForge resolves and ORs names or |-joined strings ("Above|Left"). This enum declares mask values: Above (1) and Left (2) combine to 3. Raw integer masks such as 3 are accepted by set only; append/prepend and remove require named flags. Stripped metadata or an unresolved enum leaves ordinary integer conversion without named bitmask forms or mutations. Shipping builds must retain metadata for these named examples. See Property Types for mask-value versus bit-index rules and width limits. bRequireAllParents then switches between AND (true, every flagged parent required; default) and OR (false, any one is enough) semantics. mRequiredParentCompletions defaults to 1 and requires that many completed runs from each marked parent. Values above 1 are intended for branches behind endless tasks and count completed runs, not queued repeats. See Value Forms for the full grammar. Every flag on mParentTask must resolve to a real sibling node at the matching coordinate offset (Above → the node directly above, Left → directly left, etc.) or the node is rejected at load time, so a small tree needs coordinates laid out to match: # file: showcase-delivery-task.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: DeliveryTask_Root class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: mCoordinate: X: 0 Y: 0 mName: "Root Task" - id: DeliveryTask_Child_Above class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: mCoordinate: X: 0 Y: 1 mName: "Single-Parent Child" mParentTask: Above bRequireAllParents: true - id: DeliveryTask_Child_Right class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: mCoordinate: X: 1 Y: 0 mName: "Sibling Child" mParentTask: Left # points back at (0, 0): the root bRequireAllParents: true - id: DeliveryTask_Child_AboveAndLeft class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: mCoordinate: X: 1 Y: 1 mName: "Two-Parent Child" # multiple flags set in parallel mParentTask: - Above # points to (1, 0) - Left # points to (0, 1); both nodes must exist in the tree bRequireAllParents: true # AND: both parents must be completed A one-time task (bIsEndless: false, the default) can also force-unlock a schematic and grant rewards on completion, via mSchematics/mRewards/mCosts: - id: DeliveryTask_UnlockSuperIngot class: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDeliveryTask properties: mCoordinate: X: 1 Y: 2 mName: "Unlock: Pure Super Ingot" mParentTask: Above bRequireAllParents: true # force-unlocked on completion mSchematics: - /Game/YourMod/Schematics/Schematic_PureSuperIngot.Schematic_PureSuperIngot_C mRewards: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C Amount: 500 mCosts: - ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C Amount: 100 The full property set (including the Endless-only fields mPoolElements/mTaskRewards/mMaxTasks/ mAmountMultiplierCurve/mAbsolutMaxItemAmount) is demonstrated in [KDataForge's own reference sample pack](/kdataforge/getting-started), showcase-delivery-task.dataasset.yml.

pages.title: Power and machines
pages.description: Change buildables, power use, manufacturing speed, generators, extractors, pipelines, storage, and live actors.

sections.heading: Power and machines
sections.text: Use these examples to patch stats on existing buildables, including power consumption, manufacturing speed, generator output, extraction rate, pipeline throughput, and storage capacity, through a plain type: cdo document. If you're instead looking to add a genuinely new building/buildable descriptor class to the build menu, that's a different mechanism. Type: building covers generation. This page never generates anything: it only patches CDOs. Buildable CDOs expose factory tuning: mPowerConsumption, mPowerConsumptionExponent, mManufacturingSpeed, significance/overclock settings, mDisplayName, mDescription. > ℹ️ Verify property names against your game version. The buildable examples on this page use > real FactoryGame properties, but game updates occasionally rename or move them. If a target: > path or property key doesn't resolve, nothing breaks. The load report tells you exactly which patch > failed (/kdf report, see Getting Started → Troubleshooting). Confirm the > effect in-game after every patch.

sections.heading: Combining an exact target with a subclass-wide target in one document
sections.text: A single cdo document can mix a precise, single-building target: with a native base-class target: that fans out via applyToSubclasses: true. Below, the Mk.1 Smelter gets its own power draw and speed tweaks by exact class path. A second patch entry reaches every resource node and deposit through their shared native base class AFGResourceNode, doubling the extraction multiplier for miners across the board, vanilla and modded alike, in one pass: type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/SmelterMk1/Build_SmelterMk1.Build_SmelterMk1_C properties: mPowerConsumption: $op: multiply value: 0.75 mManufacturingSpeed: $op: multiply value: 1.25 # Double the extraction yield of every resource node/deposit via the native base class: - target: /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceNode applyToSubclasses: true # FGResourceDeposit derives from FGResourceNode too properties: mExtractMultiplier: $op: multiply value: 2

sections.heading: Power generator output
sections.text: All fuel-burning generators (coal, fuel, biomass burner) derive from AFGBuildableGeneratorFuel. The produced megawatts live on the generator base as mPowerProduction: type: cdo patches: - target: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableGeneratorFuel applyToSubclasses: true # coal, fuel, biomass, modded fuel generators properties: mPowerProduction: $op: multiply value: 2 # double output; fuel burn rate scales with it Target a single generator class (e.g. Build_GeneratorCoal.Build_GeneratorCoal_C) instead when you don't want the subclass blast radius. See Targeting.

sections.heading: Extractor cycle speed
sections.text: mExtractCycleTime is the seconds per extraction cycle. This property lives on the miner buildable itself, not the resource node. Halving it doubles the output rate: type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/MinerMk1/Build_MinerMk1.Build_MinerMk1_C properties: mExtractCycleTime: $op: multiply value: 0.5

sections.heading: Pipeline flow limit
sections.text: Every pipeline mark derives from AFGBuildablePipeline. mFlowLimit is the throughput cap in m³/s (Mk.1 = 300 m³/min = 5 m³/s): type: cdo patches: - target: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildablePipeline applyToSubclasses: true # Mk.1 + Mk.2 + modded pipes properties: mFlowLimit: $op: multiply value: 2

sections.heading: Power storage capacity
sections.text: Power Storage buildables cap how many megawatt-hours they can bank before topping out. mPowerStoreCapacity is that ceiling. This patch omits $op: entirely, so it defaults to a plain set overwrite rather than a relative scale: type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/PowerStorage/Build_PowerStorageMk1.Build_PowerStorageMk1_C properties: mPowerStoreCapacity: 200 # MWh (vanilla: 100)

sections.heading: Drone station logistics
sections.text: AFGBuildableDroneStation is an ordinary buildable, so its per-trip cargo/fuel tuning is a plain cdo patch like anything else: type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/DroneStation/Build_DroneStation.Build_DroneStation_C properties: mTransferSpeed: $op: multiply value: 2 # faster cargo load/unload mStackTransferSize: 4 # items moved per transfer tick mTripPowerPerMeterCost: $op: multiply value: 0.5 # cheaper long-haul routes

sections.heading: Runtime actor patches (values that saves/archetypes would override)
sections.text: CDO edits only affect _newly built_ actors when the value is serialised into the save. Placed buildings keep their saved values. applyToSpawnedActors re-applies the ops to every instance the moment it spawns: type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/StorageContainerMk1/Build_StorageContainerMk1.Build_StorageContainerMk1_C applyToSpawnedActors: true # re-applied to every instance the moment it spawns applyToSubclasses: false # exact class only properties: mInventorySizeX: 12 mInventorySizeY: 8 All targeting modifiers are documented in Targeting. Belt speed, also a buildable patch but balance-flavored, lives in Balancing. To generate a brand-new building/buildable descriptor class instead of patching an existing one, see Type: building.

pages.title: Removed repeat-purchase unlocks
pages.description: Migrate an old KLib repeat-purchase reward pack to Delivery tasks.

sections.heading: Removed repeat-purchase unlocks
sections.text: The custom KLUnlockMaxRepeatPurchases unlock, its challenge Blueprint, and its purchase-count and level-dependent reward system have been removed. Existing YAML that references that class must be updated; enabling KLib no longer provides it. Use Delivery Task Trees to define repeatable tasks, completion-specific rewards, and cost growth. Remove the obsolete schematic unlock from your pack. Unused cost/reward curves can be removed once no other content references them.

pages.title: Unlocks catalog
pages.description: Find the relocated base-game FGUnlock catalog.

sections.heading: Unlocks catalog
sections.text: The Unlocks Catalog has been split into two pages: - The base-game FGUnlock catalog now lives at Base-Game Unlock Classes.

pages.title: Document types and features
pages.description: Understand each YAML document type and the mechanics shared across KDataForge packs.

sections.heading: Document types and features
sections.text: Use this section to understand how KDataForge packs work. Most YAML documents declare a type: that selects a handler and its load stage. Each document type has a page below. Shared concepts cover the property codec, all 25 patch operations, target selection, conditions, pack manifests, templates, settings, and reload behavior. For a procedure, use the How-to guides. For complete packs, use Examples. The Reference holds exact syntax, defaults, constraints, and public API contracts.

sections.heading: Patch mechanics
sections.text: type: cdo is the workhorse document that every other type either resembles or builds on internally. These pages cover the parts that make a patch a patch: what a value looks like, what an operation does to it, how a target is selected, when a document applies at all, and how the pieces fit together in one patch entry. - Property Types: every value shape the property codec accepts, including bool, all numeric widths, enums, strings, FText (plain and localized), object/class/soft references, all three struct forms, arrays, sets, maps, and gameplay tags. - Operations: what each of the 25 $op: values does and which property kinds accept it, covering numeric math and clamping, container mutation, string concatenation, array reordering, and cross-property copy/move. - Targeting: every way to select what a patch applies to, a class CDO, a single asset instance, every asset of a class, tag matching, subclass expansion, and spawned-actor propagation. - Conditions & Packs: conditions: for gating whether a document applies, pack.yml manifest fields, redirects: for safe id renames, and include: ordering between files in one pack. - Patching (type: cdo): how a patches: entry ties target selectors, modifiers, and a properties: mapping together, plus the current snapshot and restart boundaries. - Templates & Typed References: typed configuration and game-setting reads, string interpolation, and apply-time reflected property/function reads. - Pack Configuration: type: config definitions, player values, field controls, and when changed settings take effect. For condition syntax, see Configuration Expressions. - Category Ordering: assign categories and deterministic one-based menu order to items, recipes, schematics, and user settings. - Categories: create named category classes with optional icons.

sections.heading: Runtime registration
sections.text: Two document types register something into a global engine system rather than patching an object directly. Both are unusual enough about _when_ they take effect to deserve their own page. - Game Tags: registering new gameplay tags at runtime, how that registration survives the engine's tag-tree rebuilds, and why the GameTags stage always runs first. - Localization: new or overridden display text per namespace and culture, source-hash matching for overrides, and culture prefix-matching rules.

sections.heading: World and startup control
sections.text: These root types affect world content or react to world events without generating a class. Their multiplayer execution rules differ; check the linked page before shipping a pack. - Resources and Resource Nodes: type: resourcenode removes matching world nodes by effective resource descriptor and optional node type, with explicit save-persistence and occupied-node safeguards. - Resource Node Appearance: override node materials or hide selected mesh actors, including streamed and client-side instances. - Resource Node Placement: add nodes from explicit transforms or replace matching existing nodes. - Event Rules: run bounded server-side actions at world start or after schematic purchases, optionally once per save. - Sublevels: type: sublevel blocks selected RefinedRDLib or KBFL sublevel descriptor assets before their levels stream in. - Removing Content: remove: on recipe, schematic, and research documents takes registered content out of the game, by exact class or by filter rule, with the save implications of each kind and how they combine.

sections.heading: Content creation
sections.text: These seven types generate a class at runtime or register an existing class. They share the id/parent/properties shape and KDataForge's save-stable generated-class identity. - Items: generating new FGItemDescriptor classes, the parent/required-base rules, and the generated-class identity every other content-creation type shares. - Resources and Resource Nodes: generating FGResourceDescriptor classes, patching node actor classes, scanner unlocks, and removing matching world nodes with type: resourcenode. - Buildings: generating new building/buildable-descriptor classes, what a generated building actually is, and the hard limit on genuinely new meshes or components. - Unlocks: generating a standalone, reusable FGUnlock subclass, and why a schematic's own inline unlocks: list is what most packs actually want. - Recipes: generating new recipes, registering existing recipe classes, and how registration into SML's content registry actually happens. - Schematics: generating new schematics/milestones, registering existing ones, and the instanced unlocks: list that wires a recipe up to a schematic. - Research Trees: generating new M.A.M. research trees, registering existing ones, and why a schematic doesn't "point at" a tree the way a recipe points at a schematic.

sections.heading: Other content and assets
sections.text: These pages cover a narrow registry document, the general class handler, object-instance assets, imported audio, and Unreal curves. - Sink Points: setting AWESOME Sink point values for items, its registration timing, and why this is separate from Resource Nodes. - Custom Classes: generating a class of any kind from any parent (native or Blueprint), with optional registerAs: for the three registered kinds, the escape hatch beyond the preset types above. - Data Assets: editing every KAPI PrimaryDataAsset type, creating new instances with type: dataasset, loading 2D images with type: asset, and RefinedR&D (RRDA) integration. - Sounds: type: sound imports pack-relative PCM16 WAV, lossless FLAC, or Ogg Vorbis files as audio events for ADA messages and other consumers, including generated Audio settings. - Float and Vector Curves: creating or editing UCurveFloat and UCurveVector assets with key interpolation, tangents, defaults, and extrapolation.

sections.heading: Authoring tools
sections.text: - TypeScript scripting with KDataForgeJS: choose the KDataForgeJS workflow and open its focused guides for project setup, reflection, hooks and lifecycle, content authoring, and runtime limits. The built-in module also includes a 128-function helper library. - VS Code Extension & LSP: bind exported game data to a project for completions, hover, and diagnostics, or work with schema-only validation. - TypeScript Pack Modules and Libraries: organize one static pack graph into optional feature installers and vendored typed helpers. - Reflection Export: export the game's reflected types, defaults, settings, functions, and texture previews as a .kdfdata archive. If you know the YAML type:, open its page above. If you are starting from a goal, such as making a new item obtainable, follow the How-to guides instead.

pages.title: Actor instance selectors
pages.description: Select live actors by actor tag, world bounds, or production recipe, then patch or remove them.

sections.heading: Actor instance selectors
sections.text: Use actorSelector: inside a type: cdo patch to change selected actor instances without changing their class defaults. For example, change the power consumption of iron-ingot smelters inside a particular factory area while leaving other smelters alone. The same predicates can accompany an actorAction to destroy or dismantle selected actors instead of writing properties. Omit properties in that case. Predicates remain server-only, even though unfiltered lifecycle actions also support local non-replicated client actors. type: cdo patches: - target: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableManufacturer applyToSubclasses: true applyToSpawnedActors: true actorSelector: sphere: center: - 120000 - -40000 - 15000 radius: 25000 currentRecipe: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties: mPowerConsumption: $op: multiply value: 0.75 Replace the bounds with coordinates from your world. Coordinates and distances use Unreal world centimetres: 100 is one metre. The selector checks the actor origin, not its mesh or collision box. Use properties available on the target class in your game's reflection data. Property operations have the same constraints as ordinary CDO patches; changing a property does not automatically call a machine-specific setter or rebuild derived state.

sections.heading: Fields and matching
sections.text: At least one selector field is required. Every supplied field must match. | Field | Accepted value | Match | | tags | Non-empty string or non-empty list of non-empty strings | Actor has every listed ordinary AActor.Tags tag. | | sphere | Map with a three-number center sequence and a finite positive radius | Actor origin lies inside or on the sphere. | | box | Map with three-number min and max sequences | Actor origin lies inside or on the axis-aligned box. Each minimum must be smaller than its maximum. | | currentRecipe | Recipe class reference or non-empty list of recipe classes | Actor's current recipe equals any listed class. Subclasses do not match automatically. | tags uses ordinary actor tags, not gameplay tags. Tags must already exist on the instance; the selector does not add them. Tag names follow Unreal FName matching. Empty entries and None are rejected. Recipe references must resolve to FGRecipe subclasses. Actors without a compatible mCurrentRecipe class property, or without a selected recipe, do not match currentRecipe. Recipe classes must be available when the entry registers. If another document generates the recipe during this same load, add deferOneGameTick: true beside applyToSpawnedActors: true. This delays recipe resolution until after content generation, then visits existing actors too. This patch requires both actor tags and a box match: type: cdo patches: - target: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableManufacturer applyToSubclasses: true applyToSpawnedActors: true actorSelector: tags: - FactoryNorth - PowerBudget box: min: - 100000 - -50000 - 0 max: - 140000 - -10000 - 30000 properties: mPowerConsumption: 2

sections.heading: Required patch settings
sections.text: - target: must resolve to an actor class, or a non-empty list of actor classes. Direct object and asset targets are rejected. All targets must resolve before the entry is registered. - applyToSpawnedActors: true is required. - applyToSubclasses defaults to false; enable it when targeting a native base class. - properties: must contain the operations to apply. - allAssetsOfClass, ofClass, matchAssets, tagProperty, and the CDO/asset filters cannot be combined with actorSelector. Use separate patch entries for CDO changes. - Unknown selector and bounds fields, malformed vectors, non-finite numbers, empty lists, and invalid bounds are rejected. Inspect /kdf report for diagnostics.

sections.heading: When changes apply
sections.text: Selectors run for actors already present when the world starts, actors spawned afterwards, and actors present after /kdf reload. Instance matching waits until the actor has begun play, so construction and save restoration finish before tags, location, and recipe are read. This is a lifecycle selector, not continuous monitoring. Moving an actor into a region, adding a tag, or selecting a different recipe later does not automatically apply or remove a patch. Reload to re-evaluate existing actors. A freshly built machine without a selected recipe cannot match a recipe selector at spawn; select the recipe, then reload. Each matching entry is applied at most once per actor between reloads. Repeated visits do not compound multiply, append, or similar operations. Different entries can still apply to the same actor, in pack/document order. Reload restores KDataForge's captured property baselines before matching and applying the current entries again. Removing an entry therefore restores its captured values on surviving actors during reload; this can also overwrite gameplay changes made to those same properties since the snapshot. If deferOneGameTick: true is present, deferred registration also visits existing actors without repeating entries already applied to them. Starting another reload cancels deferred work from the previous load, so a removed or edited entry cannot run afterwards from an old queue.

sections.heading: Multiplayer
sections.text: Selected actor operations run on the authoritative host or dedicated server. Clients receive changes only through replication already provided by the target actor/property. A selector does not make an unreplicated property replicate or add a client RPC. Use identical packs on host and clients, and verify the chosen property in multiplayer when its client presentation matters. See Targeting for class and asset selection, and Operations for the property-operation syntax.

pages.title: Type: building
pages.description: Generate building descriptor classes from YAML and understand what generated buildings can and cannot do.

sections.heading: Type: building
sections.text: This is the Items stage, at priority 20, the last of the five generation types (class → unlock → item → resource → building). /kdf reload rescans the document, but generated building registration is frozen for the session, so changes need a restart. The entries key is buildings, and the default parent is /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildingDescriptor, which is also the required base class (or a subclass of it). Register-only mode (class:) is not supported here, use id: instead. Use a plain cdo patch to edit an _existing_ buildable's stats (see Power & Machines and Type: cdo). type: building is specifically for creating a new FGBuildingDescriptor-derived class: a genuinely new entry in the build menu, not a tweak to one that already exists.

sections.heading: Read this before you start: the hard constraint
sections.text: A generated class copies its parent's layout exactly: same components, same mesh slots, same everything except CDO default values. type: building is worth reaching for when you want, say, a recoloured or re-tuned variant of an existing buildable that needs its own separate build-menu entry. That way players can have both the original and the variant at once. It is not a way to add a new mesh, a new component, or genuinely new behaviour: a generated class has no new reflected properties and no new components beyond what the parent already defines. KDataForge is also 2D-only by design, so there's no way to bring in new meshes either. For a new mesh, new component, or new gameplay behaviour, you need actual C++/Blueprint content: type: building can't get you there.

sections.heading: Worked example: a recoloured storage variant
sections.text: A building document's buildings: entries follow the same id/parent/properties shape as every other generation type. id names the new descriptor, parent is the existing descriptor class it clones the layout from, and properties applies CDO overrides to the clone. Here a plain Storage Container Mk1 gets a recoloured, bigger-capacity variant of its own: # file: crimson-storage.building.yml type: building buildings: - id: MyCrimsonStorage parent: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/StorageContainerMk1/Build_StorageContainerMk1.Build_StorageContainerMk1_C properties: mDisplayName: Crimson Storage Container mInventorySizeX: 12 This generates /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_MyCrimsonStorage, a real, separate buildable class with its own build-menu entry, save data, and everything else a normal buildable has. It inherits the parent's mesh and behaviour wholesale.

sections.heading: Practical note: descriptor vs. buildable
sections.text: FactoryGame splits "the thing in your build menu" (UFGBuildingDescriptor, what this document generates) from "the thing placed in the world" (AFGBuildable*, the actor). Parenting a building entry off an existing descriptor (like Build_StorageContainerMk1 above, which is itself the descriptor tied to the buildable) is what makes the new descriptor spawn the same buildable actor with your CDO overrides. You're not generating a new AFGBuildable subclass, and for a simple variant you never need to. When you _do_ want a separate buildable class, with its own CDO defaults on the actor and its own save identity, generate one from an existing Build_*_C parent with type: class and point the descriptor's mBuildableClass at it. The full chain (buildable → descriptor → build recipe → production recipes → schematic → sinkpoints) is walked step by step in A Complete Building.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - The new building doesn't show up in the build menu at all: check /kdf report first. If the class generated successfully but you don't see it, this is very likely a build menu category or recipe registration question, not the building document itself. A building descriptor needs a recipe (see Type: recipe) that produces it, and a schematic that unlocks that recipe before it becomes buildable in a fresh game. - Stats didn't change: same rule as everywhere else. An unsupported op or a bad property key is a diagnostic, never a silent failure, and /kdf report tells you exactly which patch failed. - Want to bulk-tune a whole family of _existing_ buildings instead (all miners, all belts, all generators)? That's applyToSubclasses: on a plain cdo patch. See Targeting.

pages.title: Category ordering
pages.description: Assign menu categories and one-based display order to items, recipes, schematics, and user settings.

sections.heading: Category ordering
sections.text: type: category_reorder keeps category placement separate from general cdo patches. One document selects a content kind, assigns one main category and optional subcategory, then writes priorities from the order array: first entry gets 1, second gets 2, and so on. type: category_reorder subType: items category: /Game/MyMod/Categories/Cat_Pipelines.Cat_Pipelines_C subCategory: /Game/MyMod/Categories/SC_SpecialPipes.SC_SpecialPipes_C categoryPriority: 4 subCategoryPriority: 2 order: - /Game/MyMod/Pipes/Desc_PipeMk1.Desc_PipeMk1_C - /Game/MyMod/Pipes/Desc_PipeMk2.Desc_PipeMk2_C The handler runs in CDOChanges after ordinary cdo handlers. This makes the declared array the final category order even when another patch previously changed the same priority fields.

sections.heading: Supported subtypes
sections.text: | subType | order entries | Main category | Subcategory | Priority field | | items | UFGItemDescriptor class paths, including buildings and equipment | UFGCategory | optional UFGCategory | mMenuPriority | | recipe | UFGRecipe class paths, including customization recipes | UFGItemCategory | not supported | mManufacturingMenuPriority | | schematic | UFGSchematic class paths | UFGSchematicCategory | optional UFGSchematicCategory | mMenuPriority | | settings | UFGUserSetting asset paths | UFGUserSettingCategory | optional UFGUserSettingCategory | WidgetsToCreate[0].MenuPriority | items, recipe, and schematic entries are class paths and normally end in _C. settings entries are Primary Data Asset object paths and do not end in _C.

sections.heading: Settings preserve other placements
sections.text: A user setting can appear in more than one menu location. category_reorder updates only WidgetsToCreate[0].CategoryClass, optional SubCategoryClass, and MenuPriority. It does not replace the array, change later placements, or change SubOptionTo links. The setting must already have a WidgetsToCreate[0] entry. Use a general cdo object patch when creating a placement from scratch. type: category_reorder subType: settings category: /Game/MyMod/Settings/Cat_Gameplay.Cat_Gameplay_C subCategory: /Game/MyMod/Settings/SC_Logistics.SC_Logistics_C order: - /Game/MyMod/Settings/US_PipeHints.US_PipeHints - /Game/MyMod/Settings/US_AutoConnect.US_AutoConnect

sections.heading: Category priorities
sections.text: categoryPriority changes mMenuPriority on the main category class. subCategoryPriority does the same for subCategory and therefore requires that field. Both accept fractional values. Omitting subCategory leaves each target's existing subcategory unchanged. Supplying it replaces the subcategory list for items and schematics with one entry; settings update only the first menu placement. Recipes reject both subcategory fields because UFGRecipe has no equivalent property. Every order array must be non-empty and contain unique paths. Missing class targets are watched and applied if their class loads later. Settings are asset instances, so an unresolved settings path is reported as an error instead of becoming a class-load watch.

pages.title: Conditions and packs
pages.description: Control when documents apply, configure pack manifests, redirect ids, and order files with include:.

sections.heading: Conditions and packs
sections.text: Two mechanisms sit above the individual document types covered elsewhere in this section. The conditions: block decides whether a single document applies at all. The pack.yml manifest describes the folder of documents around it: a stable ref for save persistence, a load-order priority, and optional dependencies on other packs. Both are cross-cutting, so they work the same way no matter which document type: (cdo, item, gametag, …) they're attached to.

sections.heading: Conditions: gating whether a document applies at all
sections.text: A conditions: block lets a document skip itself when the environment doesn't match: a required mod isn't loaded, the game version is too old, or a class from another mod doesn't exist. It accepts one object or an array of objects. Keys inside each object are AND-combined; conditionBehaivor selects AND or OR across objects and defaults to AND. Ranges use SML's semver syntax (>=, ^, ~, exact versions, || unions). The example below exercises every supported key, including both the scalar and sequence forms of hasMod/hasClass: type: cdo conditions: gameVersion: '>=1.0.0' # semver range vs FactoryGame version hasMod: KAPI # single mod (loaded check) # hasMod: # sequence ALL must be loaded # - KAPI # - RefinedPower@>=4.0.0 # inline version constraint modVersion: # explicit version map form SML: '>=3.12.0' KAPI: '>=2026.0.0' hasClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableFrackingActivator # hasClass: # sequence ALL must exist # - /Game/FicsitFarming/Buildable/FarmPlot/Build_FarmPlot.Build_FarmPlot_C patches: - target: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableFrackingActivator properties: mDefaultPotentialExtractionPerMinute: $op: multiply value: 1.5 The map form above remains the compact form for ordinary positive conditions. Use an array of condition objects when some requirements must match and another must not match: conditionBehaivor: AND # optional; AND is the default conditions: - hasMod: - KAPI - KLib # both mods must be loaded - hasMod: IncompatibleMod # this object must NOT match ifNotMatch: true - hasMod: 'OptionalIntegration@^2.0.0' # reject only matching 2.x versions ifNotMatch: true Keys inside each object are AND-combined, then ifNotMatch: true negates that object's combined result. conditionBehaivor combines the resulting objects and accepts AND or OR (case-insensitive); it defaults to AND. Correctly spelled conditionBehavior is accepted as an alias. Therefore, the example applies only when KAPI and KLib are loaded, IncompatibleMod is absent, and OptionalIntegration is either absent or outside ^2.0.0. Inversion applies to the whole object, not each list entry. To reject several mods independently, put each hasMod check in its own object with ifNotMatch: true. Invalid keys, value types, or version ranges are configuration errors and are never converted into matches by inversion. Use OR when any one condition object may enable the document: conditionBehaivor: OR conditions: - hasMod: RefinedPower - hasMod: FicsitFarming This applies when RefinedPower, FicsitFarming, or both are loaded. ifNotMatch still runs per object before OR combines the results. Invalid behavior values or malformed condition objects always fail closed, even when another OR object matches. With an empty condition array, AND passes and OR does not. For configuration checks, config: accepts one expression string or a nonempty list of expressions that must all be true. At runtime, config: [] is an error: the affected pack, document, or list element is skipped, including when ifNotMatch: true or another matching OR branch is present. See Config Expressions for expression syntax. Failing conditions skip the document with an Info-severity diagnostic. However, /kdf report filters Info diagnostics out of its printed output entirely, so a condition skip is currently not visible there. The only signal is a lower-than-expected "document(s) applied" count. See Debugging a Pack That Won't Apply for the workaround.

sections.heading: pack.yml: the pack manifest
sections.text: A pack.yml at a detected pack root turns it into a named pack instead of the loader's fallback. The implicit ref and name come from the detected root's parent directory. The manifest gives a group of documents a stable identity across saves, a load-order priority relative to other packs, and dependency ordering. The fields below are read directly by the pack scanner: name and description accept either a plain string or a localized text map with ns, key, and source. Use keyed maps for translated pack labels. The native source remains the readable fallback in logs; ref stays the unchanged technical/save identity. Existing scalar manifests remain supported. The desktop manifest editor displays the source and preserves namespace/key when editing a keyed name or description. ref: MyOverhaul # stable ref the save-persistence and conflict-report contract name: My Overhaul Pack version: 2.1.0 priority: 200 # higher than default (100) → applies earlier in every stage enabled: true conditionBehaivor: AND # optional; controls condition-object aggregation dependencies: - KDFSample # packs that must load before this one conditions: # same grammar/evaluator as a document's conditions: see above hasMod: RefinedPower@>=4.0.0 dependencies: are hard ordering constraints. A pack is rejected if a dependency is missing, self-referential, or already invalid; that rejection propagates to transitive dependants. Packs in a dependency cycle are also rejected. The remaining packs are topologically ordered so every dependency runs first. Among packs whose dependencies are ready, priority descending is the tie-break, followed by ref ascending. priority defaults to 100.

sections.heading: pack.yml conditions: gating a whole pack
sections.text: pack.yml accepts the exact same conditions: map-or-array and evaluator as a document. Every key from Conditions: gating whether a document applies at all above (gameVersion, hasMod, modVersion, hasClass) plus condition arrays, ifNotMatch, and conditionBehaivor works here unchanged. It's evaluated **once, before any file in the pack is even read**. A failing pack is skipped entirely with a single Info-severity diagnostic naming the pack, instead of every document in it failing its own copy of the same condition: # file: pack.yml ref: MyRefinedPowerAddon name: My RefinedPower Addon version: 1.0.0 conditions: - hasMod: RefinedPower@>=4.0.0 - hasMod: LegacyRefinedPowerBridge ifNotMatch: true This whole pack loads only when RefinedPower 4.0+ is present and LegacyRefinedPowerBridge is not loaded. Use pack conditions for "this whole pack is a compat/addon layer for mod X" instead of repeating a conditions: block with hasMod: X at the top of every document. A document can still carry its own conditions: on top of the pack's. Pack and document gates must both pass; each gate uses its own conditionBehaivor value.

sections.heading: redirects: renaming generated-content ids
sections.text: Generated class names are id-based (Gen_<PackRef>_<Id>), so renaming an id would orphan save data. A redirects: entry in pack.yml feeds FCoreRedirects so old class paths in existing saves resolve to the renamed class. Renaming a _file_ never needs a redirect. Only id renames do: ref: MyOverhaul name: My Overhaul Pack version: 3.0.0 redirects: OldItemId: NewItemId # OldId: NewId Full worked example (rename MySuperIngot → SuperIngotMk2 across a save): End-to-End Pack → Renaming an id.

sections.heading: include: file ordering inside a pack
sections.text: Documents in the same stage use deterministic relative-path order unless include: adds an ordering constraint. List another file's path under include: (relative to the pack root) when this document must apply after it, even though both stay in the same stage: # file: overrides/late-tweaks.cdo.yml type: cdo include: - base/base-values.cdo.yml # relative to the pack root; applies first (same stage) patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply # multiplies the value base-values.cdo.yml already set value: 2.0

sections.heading: Tags registered elsewhere in the same pack
sections.text: A gametag document doesn't need include: ordering against the documents that use its tags. The GameTags stage always runs before every other stage, so a tag registered anywhere in a pack is already usable via matchTag: or tag-container ops in that same pack's cdo documents. The full syntax for registering tags, how registration survives the engine's tag-tree rebuilds, and worked examples of tagging content and then bulk-patching by tag all live on their own page: Type: gametag.

pages.title: Float and vector curves
pages.description: Create or edit UCurveFloat and UCurveVector assets with keys, interpolation, tangents, defaults, and extrapolation.

sections.heading: Float and vector curves
sections.text: type: curve creates or edits Unreal curve assets during the Assets stage. Set curveType: float for UCurveFloat or curveType: vector for UCurveVector. Every entry uses exactly one selector. - id: creates a runtime asset at /KDataForge/GenAssets/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> and announces it to the asset registry. - target: loads and edits an existing cooked curve by object path. A generated curve from the current pack can also be addressed by its bare id. The keys: list replaces all existing keys on that curve.

sections.heading: Float curves
sections.text: type: curve curveType: float curves: - id: DamageFalloff defaultValue: 0 preInfinityExtrap: constant postInfinityExtrap: linear isEventCurve: false keys: - time: 0 value: 1 interpMode: constant - time: 10 value: 0.5 interpMode: cubic tangentMode: user arriveTangent: -0.05 leaveTangent: -0.05 Reference generated curve from any object property: value: /KDataForge/GenAssets/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_DamageFalloff

sections.heading: Vector curves
sections.text: Vector values and tangent fields accept an X/Y/Z map or a three-number sequence. One key defines all three component curves at same time and with same interpolation metadata. type: curve curveType: vector curves: - id: CameraOffset defaultValue: X: 0 Y: 0 Z: 0 keys: - time: 0 value: X: 0 Y: 0 Z: 0 - time: 1 value: - 100 - 0 - 50 interpMode: cubic tangentMode: auto

sections.heading: Editing an existing curve
sections.text: type: curve curveType: float conditions: hasMod: SomeMod curves: - target: /SomeMod/Curves/Curve_ProductionRate.Curve_ProductionRate keys: - time: 0 value: 1 - time: 60 value: 2 target: must resolve to class selected by curveType. A float document cannot edit a UCurveVector, and a vector document cannot edit a UCurveFloat.

sections.heading: Key and curve fields
sections.text: | Field | Accepted values | Default | | time | finite number, unique within entry | required | | value | finite number for float, X/Y/Z value for vector | required | | interpMode | constant, linear, cubic | linear | | tangentMode | auto, smartAuto, user, break | auto | | tangentWeightMode | none, arrive, leave, both | none | | arriveTangent, leaveTangent | float or X/Y/Z value | 0 | | arriveTangentWeight, leaveTangentWeight | float or X/Y/Z value | 0 | Entry-level preInfinityExtrap and postInfinityExtrap accept none, constant, linear, cycle, cycleWithOffset, or oscillate. defaultValue uses same shape as key values. isEventCurve is valid only for float curves.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - Curve type mismatch: Confirm object path points to UCurveFloat or UCurveVector matching document curveType. - Duplicate time: Each entry can contain only one key per time. File order does not matter. KDataForge sorts keys before applying them. - Reference does not resolve: Generated curve assets have no _C suffix. Use exact /KDataForge/GenAssets/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> object path. - Existing keys disappeared: Replacement is intentional. Include every key that must remain. See YAML Schema for normative field grammar.

pages.title: Type: class
pages.description: Generate a class from any C++ or Blueprint parent and optionally register it with registerAs.

sections.heading: Type: class
sections.text: This type runs first in the Items stage at priority 50, ahead of unlock, item, resource, and building. Later generation types can therefore use a custom generated class as their parent, and recipe, schematic, and research can reference it. Changes load during session initialization, so restart after editing YAML. Its entries key is classes. There is no default parent, so every entry must set parent: explicitly. There is no required base class either: every parent works, whether native C++ or Blueprint. Register-only mode (class:) is not supported; use id: instead, and register existing classes via Type: recipe, schematic, or research. Use the preset types (item, resource, building, unlock, recipe, schematic, research) when one fits. They select the parent, stage priority, and registration. Use class for everything else: equipment descriptors, vehicle descriptors, custom category subclasses, FGUnlock subclasses, custom classes from other mods gated behind hasMod, reparented buildables, and any class kind without a KDataForge preset. type: class debug: true # optional log every applied op (see Getting Started → Debugging) classes: - id: MyCustomThing parent: /Script/FactoryGame.FGEquipmentDescriptor # ANY class: native C++ or /Game/...Thing_C registerAs: recipe # OPTIONAL: recipe | schematic | research queues SML content # registration for kinds that need it; omit for everything else properties: mDisplayName: My Equipment # cdo-style op entries applied to the new class's CDO Everything that holds for the preset generation types holds here too: - Same save-stable identity: package /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>, class Gen_<PackRef>_<Id>. Reference it elsewhere as /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id>. The global manifest, tombstone reconstruction, and redirects: in pack.yml all apply. - Layout-copy constraint: the generated class copies the parent's layout exactly, with no new reflected properties and no new components. All variation lives in the CDO defaults that properties: sets. - registerAs: is only for the three kinds SML's UModContentRegistry tracks: recipe, schematic, and research. If you generate one of those through class instead of the preset type, set it so registration is queued. Everything else, such as descriptors, categories, and unlocks, just needs to exist and be referenced.

sections.heading: Example 1: an equipment descriptor from a C++ parent
sections.text: # file: my-equipment.class.yml type: class classes: - id: Desc_MyGadget parent: /Script/FactoryGame.FGEquipmentDescriptor properties: mDisplayName: key: MyGadget_Name ns: MyPack source: Portable Gadget mStackSize: SS_ONE # equipment is conventionally non-stacking mEquipmentClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Equipment/JetPack/Equip_JetPack.Equip_JetPack_C The result is a real UFGEquipmentDescriptor subclass, usable in recipes, schematics, and sinkpoints like any other descriptor. Because of the layout-copy constraint, mEquipmentClass has to point at an existing equipment actor, here the jetpack. You are re-parametrising existing equipment behaviour, not writing new equipment logic.

sections.heading: Example 2: a build-menu / item category
sections.text: Use type: category for a named category with an optional icon. Use type: class when a category needs additional properties such as mMenuPriority: # file: my-category.class.yml type: class classes: - id: Cat_MyPackParts parent: /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemCategory properties: mDisplayName: key: Cat_MyPackParts_Name ns: MyPack source: MyPack Parts mMenuPriority: 999 Point generated items at it from the same pack. The Items stage guarantees the category class exists before any later stage references it. Within the stage, include: orders documents when one Items-stage document needs another: type: item include: - my-category.class.yml # the category must generate before this item references it items: - id: MySuperGadgetPart properties: mCategory: /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_Cat_MyPackParts

sections.heading: Example 3: a modded parent class, gated behind `hasMod`
sections.text: Any loaded mod's classes work as parents. Gate the document so it is skipped cleanly (Info diagnostic) when the mod is missing: # file: ff-crop.class.yml type: class conditions: hasMod: FicsitFarming classes: - id: Desc_MyCustomCrop parent: /Game/FicsitFarming/Descriptors/Crops/Desc_Berry.Desc_Berry_C # Blueprint parent properties: mDisplayName: My Custom Crop

sections.heading: `registerAs:` (generating a registered kind through `class`)
sections.text: If you generate a recipe, schematic, or research class via class, for example because you want a specific modded subclass as the parent, queue its registration with registerAs:. It does exactly what the preset type's default register: true does: type: class classes: - id: Recipe_MySpecial parent: /Game/SomeMod/Recipes/Recipe_SpecialBase.Recipe_SpecialBase_C registerAs: recipe # queued into UModContentRegistry before the freeze properties: mDisplayName: My Special Recipe

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - "parent is required": unlike the preset types, class has no default parent. Every entry needs an explicit parent:. - "My generated recipe/schematic never shows up": you generated it via class without registerAs:. Only the preset types register automatically. class registers nothing unless you ask. - Wanting new components, meshes, or logic: not possible. See the layout-copy constraint above and the honest scope callout in A Complete Building. - Preset-type pages for the ergonomic forms: Type: item, Type: recipe, Type: schematic, Type: building.

pages.title: Data assets
pages.description: Edit KAPI data assets, create UDataAsset instances, load 2D images, and integrate RefinedR&D assets.

sections.heading: Data assets
sections.text: Most of the reference pages nearby cover generated classes such as buildings, recipes, and schematics. Data assets are different: they are UDataAsset instances, meaning objects rather than classes. KDataForge accepts any UDataAsset subclass for type: dataasset. KAPI and many RefinedR&D assets are UPrimaryDataAsset subclasses, so consumer subsystems can discover them through the asset registry and rescan them after KDataForge creates or edits instances. KDataForge can both edit existing instances, using plain cdo documents just like any other object, and create brand-new ones with type: dataasset. Use dataasset when a mod needs a fresh instance rather than an edit to an existing one. This page also covers the other asset-stage document, type: asset, which loads 2D images from your pack folder into real textures that you can point icon properties at.

sections.heading: Native CDO helpers and Blueprint requirements
sections.text: Use type: dataasset to move a KBFL CDO helper's configuration into YAML while keeping its native helper class and Blueprint requirement classes installed. This preserves the native requirement predicates, OnModify, OnModified, deferred and OnFinishedAll callbacks. World helpers retain their native world registration and tick behavior. Specialized DataAsset, tag, category, cache and recipe-mover helpers also keep their native implementation. Create an asset of the original concrete helper class. Copy its settings, priority and complete mRequirements class list. For KBFLCDOOverwrite, also copy mNativeClass, targeting flags, property descriptors and the effective values inside mPropertyContainer. The container uses the existing instanced-object form with class and nested properties. KDataForge duplicates its class defaults, including inherited subobjects; abstract classes are supported for this helper container. For example, this standalone helper sets an iron descriptor's energy value: type: dataasset assets: - id: IronEnergyHelper class: /Script/KBFL.KBFLCDOOverwrite properties: mCallPrio: 100 mTargetClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreIron/Desc_OreIron.Desc_OreIron_C mNativeClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceDescriptor mManuelPropertiesOverwrite: - mPropertyName: mEnergyValue mPropertyType: Float mNumericBehavior: Replace mPropertyContainer: class: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreIron/Desc_OreIron.Desc_OreIron_C properties: mEnergyValue: 10 These assets are configured during the initial Assets stage and published to the asset registry only after their property operations succeed. A failed helper configuration is not published. Each helper must have a unique pack/id definition. KBFL discovers the generated instance through its normal startup pass; KDataForge does not call callbacks a second time. Restart required: once a generated native CDO helper is active, /kdf reload and automatic pack reload are refused before restoring properties. Restart after changing, disabling or removing such a pack. The in-game editor refuses live edits to native helpers and their owned subobjects. Desktop completion and property details mark helper settings as requiring restart. For migration, compare the complete helper, requirement callbacks, selected targets, priority and resulting runtime values before archiving its original asset. Keep required classes and referenced assets available. Generated assets have new object paths and primary-asset names: update any references to the original helper and check callbacks that inspect its identity. Equal native priorities still have undefined order; YAML does not resolve an existing conflict automatically. Remove the original active helper when activating its replacement to avoid duplicate callbacks.

sections.heading: Editing KAPI data assets
sections.text: KAPI is the biggest single consumer of PrimaryDataAsset instances in the mod ecosystem. It drives modular miners, cleaner buildings, air collectors, manufacturer tuning, slug breeding, extractor allow-lists, and tooltip injection entirely from data assets rather than code. This lets other mods, including KDataForge packs, retune all of it without touching KAPI's own source. Because they're ordinary UObject instances, KDataForge reaches them with the exact same three selectors documented in Targeting: 1. target: with the asset object path (note: no _C suffix, since these are instances, not classes). 2. allAssetsOfClass: to patch every asset of a given KAPI type at once. 3. matchTag: + ofClass: to select by gameplay tag. KAPI assets carry their tags on mTags and are read like any other IGameplayTagAssetInterface object, so tags match directly.

sections.heading: `UKAPIDataAssetBase`: common base properties
sections.text: Every KAPI data asset instance, whatever its concrete type, inherits the same handful of admin fields from UKAPIDataAssetBase. There's a display mName and mDescription (both FText, shown in whatever UI surfaces the asset), an mIcon (soft texture reference), a hard on/off switch mIsDisabled, a tie-break mPriority (int32, where higher wins when more than one asset could apply), and mTags (FGameplayTagContainer), the same field matchTag: reads. Because these five fields exist on every KAPI asset, a single patch document can disable one specific asset by path while also bulk-adjusting every asset carrying a particular tag: type: cdo conditions: hasMod: KAPI patches: # Disable one specific KAPI data asset by object path: - target: /KLib/Assets/MinerDescriptions/DA_MinerDesc_Iron.DA_MinerDesc_Iron properties: mIsDisabled: true # Bump priority on every KAPI asset tagged as event-only: - matchTag: KMods.EventOnly ofClass: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDataAssetBase properties: mPriority: $op: add value: 100

sections.heading: `UKAPIModularMinerDescription`: modular miner resources
sections.text: Each instance describes one resource variant that a KAPI modular miner can extract: which resource class it targets, what item it actually produces, which drill and scanner tiers and which modules are required or excluded, and its fluid coolant/byproduct behavior. The mResourceClass field is the asset's identity. Never set it to none, since KAPI hard-crashes on a null resource class (see the key-field warning below). Retuning throughput across every modular miner resource at once is a single allAssetsOfClass patch: type: cdo conditions: hasMod: KAPI patches: - allAssetsOfClass: /Script/KAPI.KAPIModularMinerDescription properties: mNormalFluidCountPerSecond: $op: multiply value: 1.5 Other properties on this type worth knowing about: mProductionItem, mDrillTier, mScannerTier, mNeededModules, mPreventModules, mModuleInformation, mFluidInfo, mTryProductionDynamic, mTrashItem, mIsFallbackDescriptor, mFoundText, mRarityText, mNodeScreenshot.

sections.heading: `UKAPICleanerItemDescription`: cleaner recipes
sections.text: This is effectively a recipe for KAPI's cleaner building: an input fluid, an optional item that gets consumed alongside it, a production time, and the item(s) produced in return. mInFluid is a struct rather than a class reference, so its nested ItemClass member is the actual key field. Keeping mInFluid.ItemClass valid matters exactly the same way mResourceClass does on a miner description. Multiplying mProductionTime and clamping the input fluid amount both work as ordinary numeric ops, including through the nested path: type: cdo conditions: hasMod: KAPI patches: - allAssetsOfClass: /Script/KAPI.KAPICleanerItemDescription properties: mProductionTime: $op: multiply value: 0.75 # nested struct member on an asset instance mInFluid.Amount: $op: max value: 1000 Other properties: mOutFluid, mNeedCleanItem, mProduceItem, mProduceAmount, mBypassProducts, mCleanerItemInfo.

sections.heading: `UKAPIAirCollectorData`: air collector production
sections.text: Air collectors harvest a resource passively over time from the surrounding air rather than from a node.
