It does not create or place a Resource Node: unlocks: - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockScannableResource.BP_UnlockScannableResource_C properties: mResourcePairsToAddToScanner: - ResourceDescriptor: MyCustomOre ResourceNodeType: Node ResourceNodeType accepts Node, FrackingSatellite, FrackingCore, Geyser, or Deposit. See Resources and Resource Nodes for descriptor generation, node actor patches, and placement limits.

sections.heading: Gating a schematic on prerequisites
sections.text: dependencies: is the mirror image of unlocks:, using the exact same instanced-object mechanism. Each entry creates a real instanced FGAvailabilityDependency subobject directly on the schematic's CDO, appended to mSchematicDependencies: type: schematic schematics: - id: Schematic_AdvancedSuperIngot properties: mDisplayName: Advanced Super Ingot dependencies: - class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematicPurchasedDependency properties: mSchematics: - /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_Schematic_MySuperIngot mRequireAllSchematicsToBePurchased: true That schematic won't be purchasable until Schematic_MySuperIngot is. Dependency entries use the same native-to-Blueprint remapping as unlock entries. See Availability Dependency Classes for every native and Blueprint class, abstract state, path, and field. Common choices: - FGSchematicNotPurchasedDependency: inverse of FGSchematicPurchasedDependency - FGItemPickedUpDependency: requires specific items to have been picked up - FGResearchTreeProgressionDependency: requires progress in a M.A.M. research tree - FGGamePhaseReachedDependency: requires a minimum Space Elevator game phase Two flags on the schematic itself control what happens while dependencies aren't met: mDependenciesBlocksSchematicAccess (block purchase, but don't hide the entry) and mHiddenUntilDependenciesMet (hide the schematic entirely until then). Set them via ordinary properties: alongside dependencies:.

sections.heading: Making a milestone (schematic) free
sections.text: Because properties: is ordinary op grammar, the usual tricks apply to an existing, registered schematic too. clear wipes an array, and a plain numeric value: overrides a duration without having to compute a relative offset: type: schematic schematics: - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_1-1.Schematic_1-1_C # register-only: editing a vanilla milestone properties: mCost: $op: clear # no item cost mTimeToComplete: 1 # 1-second freighter turnaround (This particular example edits an existing vanilla schematic. For a genuinely simpler one-off tweak like this, a plain cdo patch with target: works identically and doesn't need the register-only framing at all. See Balancing → Making a milestone free. Using class: here is only meaningful when you also want SML registration semantics applied, which a vanilla schematic that's already registered doesn't need.)

sections.heading: Removing schematics
sections.text: A type: schematic document accepts a top-level remove: sequence. Each entry is either a bare class reference (a full Unreal class path, a bare loaded class name, or a generated content id from this or another loaded KDataForge pack) or a filter map that removes every schematic passing the scope filters (matchName:, matchTag:, where:; the scope defaults to FGSchematic). Removal-only documents are valid, and remove: can also be mixed with normal schematics: entries: type: schematic remove: - /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_1-1.Schematic_1-1_C - Schematic_MyGeneratedMilestone - where: # every tier 8+ schematic path: mTechTier greaterOrEqual: 8 schematics: - id: Schematic_ReplacementMilestone properties: mDisplayName: Replacement Milestone A bare reference names the exact schematic class to remove; it does not remove subclasses. If a generated id is ambiguous across packs, KDataForge logs the same ambiguity diagnostic used for other short-id class references. Removals run after registrations, so an explicit remove: wins over a register: for the same class. The consolidated guide is Removing Content. Schematic removal is save-clean. KDataForge removes the class from SML's content registry before the schematic manager builds its per-session list, so uninstalling the pack brings the schematic back on the next load. Removal does not revoke purchases. An already-purchased schematic stays in the save and keeps re-applying its unlocks on load, including recipes it granted. To actually take away craftable content, pair schematic removal with recipe remove:.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - The schematic shows up but the recipe never unlocks: check that the unlocks: entry's class: actually resolves (/kdf report will show a failed patch if it doesn't) and that mRecipes points at the exact generated class path, with no _C suffix. - Two mods both try to unlock the same recipe: that's fine. FGUnlockRecipe instances are additive, and duplicate unlocks of an already-unlocked recipe are a no-op in the base game. - Want to unlock a recipe from a schematic you didn't generate (vanilla, another mod's, or your own from an earlier pack): unlocks: also works in register-only (class:) mode. See Adding a Recipe to an Existing Schematic. - A schematic with dependencies: is purchasable even though its prerequisite isn't met: dependencies: alone only registers the check; you also need mDependenciesBlocksSchematicAccess: true (block purchase until met) and/or mHiddenUntilDependenciesMet: true (hide the entry entirely) as ordinary properties: on the same schematic. - Full worked pack: End-to-End Pack ties an item + recipe + this schematic + sink points + localization together in one folder.

pages.title: Type: sinkpoints
pages.description: Set AWESOME Sink values, account for registration timing, and distinguish sink scoring from resource nodes.

sections.heading: Type: sinkpoints
sections.text: This document type runs in the SubsystemMods stage, after all content-generation stages. A session restart is required to pick up changes. Its entries key is entries, and the track: field accepts Default or Exploration, defaulting to Default. Each entry sets an item's AWESOME Sink point value. Registration timing is strict. type: sinkpoints track: Default # or Exploration entries: - item: /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot points: 8 - item: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C points: 100 overridden: 50 # optional a separate "overridden" point value some UI paths read - item: must resolve to an UFGItemDescriptor subclass. Both the bare generated-content id shortcut (e.g. item: MySuperIngot instead of the full /KDataForge/Gen/... path, see Generated Content Short Ids) and the bare class-name shortcut work here too (see Targeting → bare class name), though sticking to full paths in a published pack is still the safer habit. - points: is a plain integer. overridden: is optional, and it's only needed if you specifically want a distinct "overridden" points value separate from the base one. - One sinkpoints document builds one UDataTable and registers it against whichever track: you picked. Multiple documents, even across packs, just add more rows to the sink subsystem: they don't need to be merged into one file.

sections.heading: Many items at once: filter entries
sections.text: An entry may replace item: with an ofClass: scope (default /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor) plus the scope filters (matchName:, matchTag:, where:, …). Every loaded item descriptor class that passes the filters gets the entry's points: (and overridden:): type: sinkpoints entries: - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor where: path: mForm in: # every fluid and gas: not sinkable - RF_LIQUID - RF_GAS points: 0 - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor matchName: Desc_Nuclear* # everything nuclear is worth a fixed 500 points: 500 Filter entries expand against the descriptor classes loaded when the document applies, and the load report warns when a filter matched nothing. A later explicit item: row for the same descriptor in the same document wins, because rows are keyed by class name.

sections.heading: Registration timing and resource node boundary
sections.text: KDataForge queues sink point tables during initialization and registers them per world before SML's content registry freezes. /kdf reload rescans the YAML, but it cannot rewrite a frozen Sink table for the current world. Restart the session after changing sink point documents. Sink points only control item scoring in the AWESOME Sink. They do not place Resource Nodes, change purity, or grant scanner visibility. See Resources and Resource Nodes for those systems.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - Changed points do not appear: restart the session or dedicated server. - Points show as 0, or unchanged in-game: check that item: actually resolved (/kdf report lists a failed patch if the class path was wrong), and make sure you're looking at the right track: (Default vs. Exploration are separate tables). - Sink points for a freshly generated item are part of the combined pack in End-to-End Pack. - A resource still has no mineable node or scanner entry: Sink scoring is unrelated. Follow the descriptor, world-node, and scanner steps on the Resources page.

pages.title: Sounds
pages.description: Turn pack-relative PCM16 WAV, lossless FLAC, or Ogg Vorbis files into Wwise audio events for ADA messages and other audio consumers.

sections.heading: Sounds
sections.text: type: sound imports WAV, FLAC, or Ogg Vorbis files from your pack as generated UAkAudioEvent assets. Use it when an existing game or mod feature accepts an audio event, such as an ADA message's mAudioEvent. Importing an event does not play it or create a message trigger.

sections.heading: Declare sounds
sections.text: Place the audio file inside the directory containing your pack.yml: DataForge/ pack.yml # ref: MyPack welcome.sound.yml audio/ welcome.flac # file: welcome.sound.yml type: sound sounds: - id: AdaWelcome file: audio/welcome.flac name: Welcome voice line description: Volume of the ADA welcome message category: Voice subCategory: ADA sounds: must contain at least one entry. Every entry requires id and file; the four display fields are optional and must be non-empty strings when supplied. | Field | Meaning | | id | Stable event id. Start with an ASCII letter; remaining characters may be ASCII letters, digits, _, ., or -. | | file | WAV, FLAC or Ogg Vorbis path relative to the pack root, not the YAML file's directory. | | name | Sound setting label; defaults to <id> volume. Unused for ADA's shared native control. | | description | Sound setting help text; defaults to an explanation of playback volume. Unused for ADA's shared native control. | | category | Group label below the native Audio settings section. | | subCategory | Additional Audio group label. ADA selects the game's native Dialogue Volume instead of a separate sound slider. | Set subCategory: ADA on every ADA sound, as in the example above. This value is case-insensitive and trims surrounding whitespace. These events route through Satisfactory's native VO audio bus and use Options → Audio → Dialogue Volume, including changes made during playback. They do not create individual KDataForge volume sliders or a separate ADA volume control. Their category, name and description remain accepted metadata but do not create an Audio row. Other sounds keep their individual volume sliders, defaulting to 100%, where 0% mutes them. Their category and subCategory combine into one Audio subcategory; without either field, it is KDataForge sound events. These events route to the master audio bus. All volume controls appear only under Options → Audio, never in KDataForge pack configuration. Audio preferences are local to each player and are not synchronized by the host. There is no volume field. Existing individual ADA preferences are removed during Audio settings synchronization once an entry uses subCategory: ADA; stale per-message menu registrations are removed too. The existing native Dialogue Volume becomes authoritative. Other sounds' local Audio preferences retain their values. Older __sounds.*.volume entries in pack configuration files no longer affect playback; they can be removed.

sections.heading: Accepted audio
sections.text: - Little-endian RIFF/WAVE containing uncompressed 16-bit PCM, native lossless FLAC containing 16-bit PCM, or Ogg Vorbis (decoded to PCM16). - Mono or stereo, with a sample rate from 8,000 through 192,000 Hz. - A non-empty audio payload containing complete PCM frames; maximum 64 MiB for both the encoded file and decoded PCM. - A .wav, .flac or .ogg extension, matched without regard to case. - FLAC must declare its nonzero total frame count in STREAMINFO. Decoding verifies the declared frame count and PCM MD5 when supplied. MP3, Opus, Ogg FLAC, chained/multiplexed Ogg streams, 24-bit FLAC and floating-point WAV are unsupported. Export as PCM16 WAV, native 16-bit FLAC or Ogg Vorbis in your audio editor. Files and any symbolic links must resolve inside the pack directory; absolute paths and paths escaping the pack are rejected. Existing WAV packs continue to work. To reduce download size without changing audio, convert PCM16 WAV to FLAC without resampling, mixing channels or changing bit depth, then update only sounds[].file. Keep the sound ID and message references unchanged. FLAC is decoded to the same PCM for playback, so runtime audio memory does not shrink. FLAC packs require a KDataForge build with FLAC support; keep WAV when supporting older builds. The editor checks FLAC structure and format limits; the game importer also decodes frames and verifies the supplied PCM checksum. Ogg Vorbis is lossy and requires a KDataForge build with OGG support. For example: ffmpeg -i input.wav -c:a libvorbis -b:a 96k output.ogg Set sounds[].file to audio/output.ogg; keep the event ID unchanged. OGG reduces source/download size, but KDataForge decodes it to PCM16 and writes an uncompressed Wwise bank cache. Bank size and decoded audio memory do not shrink. Keep original WAV/FLAC masters. The editor checks Ogg structure and limits; the game also decodes audio. Current server packaging filters cover WAV/FLAC; OGG files may remain in server packages harmlessly unless the packaging filter also excludes .ogg. Generated events play once in 2D and route to the master bus, or the native VO bus for subCategory: ADA. This document type does not author loops or spatial attenuation.

sections.heading: Reference an event
sections.text: Inside the same pack, use the bare event id in an audio event property: type: dataasset assets: - id: WelcomeMessage class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGMessage properties: mAudioEvent: AdaWelcome This creates a message asset with an audio reference. A separate game or mod workflow must trigger that message. The full event object path for ref: MyPack is: /KDataForge/GenAssets/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_AdaWelcome Use the full path when referring to the event from another pack. Audio events are assets, so their paths have no _C suffix. Sound ids share the generated asset namespace with images, curves and data assets; choose distinct ids across those types. See Generated Content Short Ids for reference resolution.

sections.heading: Load stage and multiplayer
sections.text: Sounds run in the Assets stage, before dataasset documents resolve properties such as FGMessage.mAudioEvent, and before later CDO changes. File ordering does not require placing a sound YAML before a data asset YAML. Install the same pack definitions on every multiplayer client and the server. Every client, including a listen-server host, also needs the referenced audio files. Dedicated servers do not need WAV, FLAC or Ogg Vorbis files: they validate the relative path syntax and create placeholder events at the same generated asset paths, without opening audio files, creating bank caches or loading Wwise banks. Messages, subtitles and server-side triggers remain available. Audio contents and symbolic-link containment are checked on clients, where the audio files exist. Importing on the server does not transfer audio files to clients. The workspace's Alpakit PackagePlugin automatically excludes raw .wav and .flac files from dedicated-server staging for WindowsServer and LinuxServer. This also applies to the server directories inside merged bundles and direct server deployments; the Windows client directory retains its audio. No YAML conditions or extra pack settings are needed. Keep the sound YAML and its message references in server packages. When packaging with an older Alpakit, audio files can remain in server packages harmlessly; older KDataForge versions still require them during import. An Alpakit filter that excludes only .wav keeps .flac and .ogg files in dedicated-server packages. Extend custom filters to every source format you use to obtain the same server size savings; keep client audio and server YAML definitions.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - File cannot resolve: Check the path relative to pack.yml, filename case on Linux, and whether a symbolic link points outside the pack. - WAV rejected: Re-export as uncompressed PCM16 mono/stereo WAV within the rate and size limits above. Renaming an MP3 to .wav does not convert it. - FLAC rejected: Export native 16-bit FLAC with a known frame count, within both size limits. Re-export files with checksum failures; renaming another format does not convert it. - Generated event missing: Check for duplicate ids, including collisions with other generated assets, and confirm the sound document's conditions pass. - Bank cache cannot be written: The client must be able to write generated banks under FactoryGame/Content/KDataForgeRuntimeSounds/. - Wwise rejects the bank: Inspect LogAkAudio and LogWwiseFileHandler alongside KDataForge diagnostics. - Import succeeds but nothing plays: Confirm a consumer triggers the event and check the sound's volume setting and the game's master volume.

pages.title: Type: sublevel
pages.description: Prevent selected RefinedRDLib or KBFL sublevels from streaming into the world.

sections.heading: Type: sublevel
sections.text: Use type: sublevel when another mod declares optional world sublevels through RefinedRDLib or KBFL and a compatibility pack must stop selected sublevels from loading. The document runs in the CDOChanges stage during session initialization. It changes the provider's data assets in memory; it does not unload a level that has already streamed in. Restart the session after changing it. This handler is deliberately narrow. It supports these two asset families: | Provider | Asset class | Blocking action | | RefinedRDLib | /Script/RefinedRDLib.RRDLSublevelAsset | Makes the asset's map selector match no normal map | | KBFL | /Script/KBFL.KBFLSubLevelSpawning | Clears its sublevel list and disables the asset | Use an ordinary type: cdo document for any other asset class.

sections.heading: Block explicit assets
sections.text: block: must be a non-empty sequence. A scalar entry is an exact asset object path. Map entries accept target: as either one path or a sequence of paths: type: sublevel block: - /SomeMod/World/DA_OptionalSublevel.DA_OptionalSublevel - target: - /AnotherMod/World/DA_Nodes_A.DA_Nodes_A - /AnotherMod/World/DA_Nodes_B.DA_Nodes_B Exact targets use direct object loading, so they still work when the Asset Registry is not fully populated during early startup. A path that does not resolve produces a warning: the owning mod may be absent, or the object path may be wrong. In a map entry, target: must be one non-empty scalar reference or a non-empty list of them. An empty string, null, mapping, nested list or empty target list produces a source-line error and skips that whole block: entry, including its bulk or filter selectors. Other block entries still apply.

sections.heading: Block every asset of a provider class
sections.text: Use allAssetsOfClass: for a bulk compatibility rule: type: sublevel conditions: hasMod: RefinedRDLib block: - allAssetsOfClass: /Script/RefinedRDLib.RRDLSublevelAsset The scan includes derived asset classes. A map may combine target: and allAssetsOfClass:; all matches accumulate. The provider is an optional dependency: an unresolved bulk class produces an Info diagnostic instead of a hard dependency failure.

sections.heading: Block assets by filter
sections.text: To block only some of a provider's assets, give a map entry an ofClass: scope plus the scope filters (matchName:, matchTag:, where:). ofClass: is required here, sublevel assets have no default scope, and only asset instances are matched, never class defaults: type: sublevel conditions: hasMod: RefinedRDLib block: - ofClass: /Script/RefinedRDLib.RRDLSublevelAsset matchName: DA_Optional_* # by asset name - ofClass: /Script/KBFL.KBFLSubLevelSpawning where: path: mSubLevelArray isEmpty: false Filter entries expand against the asset registry when the document applies (same Asset Registry caveat as allAssetsOfClass:); the load report states how many assets a filter matched. :::note Bulk discovery depends on the Asset Registry. If an installed provider class resolves but the scan finds no assets during early startup, KDataForge reports that condition. List exact target: paths instead when the assets must always be blocked. :::

sections.heading: Boundaries
sections.text: - sublevel blocks only RefinedRDLib and KBFL descriptor assets. It does not target arbitrary Unreal streaming levels, persistent-map content, world-partition cells, or already loaded levels. - Missing or invalid entries do not discard valid entries in the same document. Each target reports its own diagnostic. - Changes are in-memory and session-scoped. Removing the YAML restores normal provider behavior on the next session; no save data or source asset is rewritten. - Every multiplayer process loads its own sublevels. Install the same pack on server and clients.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - Nothing was blocked: use the asset object's path, not the generated class path. Check /kdf report for an unresolved target or an empty Asset Registry scan. - Target is rejected as the wrong kind: only RRDLSublevelAsset and KBFLSubLevelSpawning instances are supported. Patch other asset types with type: cdo. - Level was already present: Sublevel blocking must run before that level streams in. Restart instead of expecting an in-session unload.

pages.title: Targeting
pages.description: Select class CDOs, asset instances, every asset of a class, subclasses, or spawned actors by class, tag, name, property, or recipe shape; reuse the filters in remove:, block:, and sinkpoints entries.

sections.heading: Targeting
sections.text: Every type: cdo patch needs at least one target selector. The current validator accepts multiple selectors and GatherTargets accumulates their matches, but one clear selector per patch is easier to reason about. The sections below cover every selector and the modifiers that widen a selection.

sections.heading: Class identity filters
sections.text: Filtered scopes accept classType: any (default), blueprint, or native. This tests Unreal's CLASS_CompiledFromBlueprint flag; it does not guess from class names. excludeClasses accepts one class reference or a non-empty list. Exact references exclude those classes while their subclasses remain eligible. Full class-path patterns starting with / also accept * and ? wildcards, matched case-insensitively against each candidate's own class path. For example, An excludeClasses list containing /KLib/* and /SatisfactoryPlus/* leaves those namespaces untouched while selecting other mods' recipes. A subclass outside an excluded namespace remains eligible; patterns do not expand through ancestry. Both filters also run for classes loaded later. type: cdo patches: - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor classType: blueprint matchAssets: false excludeClasses: - /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/SpaceElevatorParts/Desc_SpaceElevatorPart_1.Desc_SpaceElevatorPart_1_C where: path: mForm equals: RF_LIQUID properties: mForm: RF_GAS Combine with ofClass, or a recipe shortcut that supplies a scope. These scope filters do not narrow separately listed target or allAssetsOfClass selections. Other filters are AND-combined. For data-asset candidates they test the asset's class. Set matchAssets: false for CDOs only. Consequently, exclusion patterns match a data asset's class path, not its individual object path. Wildcard exclusions must start with /; a short pattern such as Recipe_* is rejected. Quote patterns in YAML, especially patterns containing * or ?. Explicit classType: any selects every class in an ofClass scope without another predicate.

sections.heading: `target:` class path: the class default object (CDO)
sections.text: The most common form. Blueprint asset classes use the _C suffix (auto-retried if forgotten); native classes use /Script/Module.Class: type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.5

sections.heading: `target:` bare class name: shortcut for the full class path
sections.text: Anywhere a class path is accepted, a bare class name (no / or .) resolves against every class currently loaded in memory, so you don't have to spell out the full asset path: type: cdo patches: - target: Desc_Water # same class as # /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Water/Desc_Water.Desc_Water_C properties: mResourceSinkPoints: 0 If the short name matches more than one loaded class, KDataForge logs an Error to LogKDataForge listing every match. It still applies the patch, using the first match sorted by full class path, so the result stays deterministic. Prefer the full class path in published packs to avoid relying on load order. This shortcut is meant for quick local tweaks.

sections.heading: `target:` generated-content id: shortcut for `/KDataForge/Gen/...`
sections.text: A bare id also resolves to a class your own pack generated, so you can target your own item/recipe/schematic/... content without spelling out /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_...: type: cdo debug: true patches: - target: MySuperIngot # same as /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot properties: mResourceSinkPoints: 50 This is checked before the bare class-name shortcut above, and works the same way everywhere a class or object reference is accepted, not just target:. See Generated Content Short Ids for the full write-up (resolution order, cross-pack matches, and which reference kinds support it).

sections.heading: `target:` object path: one asset instance
sections.text: The same key also accepts an object path (PrimaryDataAsset instances etc.) and patches that object directly. Instances have no _C suffix: they are objects, not classes. type: cdo conditions: hasMod: KAPI patches: - target: /KLib/Assets/MinerDescriptions/DA_MinerDesc_Iron.DA_MinerDesc_Iron properties: mIsDisabled: true

sections.heading: `target:` a sequence of paths: patch several targets in one entry
sections.text: target: also accepts a list of paths instead of a single scalar. Every entry is resolved the same way a scalar target: would be (class path, bare class name, generated-content id, or object path), and the same properties:/applyToSubclasses:/applyToSpawnedActors: apply to each one: type: cdo debug: true patches: - target: - MySuperIngot # generated-content id - /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronPlate/Desc_IronPlate.Desc_IronPlate_C properties: mResourceSinkPoints: 50 This is purely a convenience for "these unrelated targets happen to want the exact same properties: block", it does not widen a single class the way applyToSubclasses: does, and mixing target kinds (a class path alongside an object path) in one list is fine, each entry is resolved independently. Prefer applyToSubclasses: or matchTag: instead when the targets share a common base class or tag; reach for a target: list when they don't. An explicit target: must contain one non-empty scalar reference or a non-empty list of them. An empty string, null, mapping, nested list or empty target list produces a source-line error and skips the entire patch entry, including its other selectors. Valid entries in other patches still apply. KDF.ApplyToAssets uses the same check before changing editor assets. A well-formed reference that cannot resolve keeps the normal warning and runtime class-watch behavior.

sections.heading: `allAssetsOfClass:` every asset of a class
sections.text: Patches every asset of that class (and its subclasses) found in the asset registry. This is ideal for data-asset families: type: cdo conditions: hasMod: KAPI patches: - allAssetsOfClass: /Script/KAPI.KAPICleanerItemDescription properties: mProductionTime: $op: multiply value: 0.75

sections.heading: `ofClass:` scope + filters: select by tag, name, recipe shape, or property values
sections.text: The remaining selectors all work the same way: ofClass: names a scope (that class and every subclass of it, plus data-asset instances of it unless matchAssets: false), and one or more filters on the same patch entry pick the members of that scope to patch. Every filter present on an entry must pass, so the filters are AND-combined: | Filter | Matches when … | | matchTag: (+ tagProperty:) | the object carries every listed gameplay tag | | matchName: | the class name (or full path) matches any listed wildcard pattern | | producedIn: | a recipe's mProducedIn references any listed building class or a subclass of it | | ingredient: | a recipe's mIngredients[*].ItemClass references any listed item class or a subclass of it | | product: | a recipe's mProduct[*].ItemClass references any listed item class or a subclass of it | | where: | every clause holds; with whereMode: OR, any clause holds | The three recipe shortcuts (producedIn:, ingredient:, product:) default the scope to /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe when ofClass: is omitted, and any matchTag:, matchName: or where: on the same entry shares that default. Without a recipe shortcut those three require an explicit ofClass:. Set ofClass: anyway to narrow the scope to a mod's own recipe base class. Filters never narrow a target: or allAssetsOfClass: selector on the same entry, those still match everything they name. When no object in the scope passes, KDataForge logs one warning that repeats the filters it evaluated, so you can see which one was too strict.

sections.heading: `matchTag:` select by gameplay tag
sections.text: Selects everything in the scope that carries the tag(s). matchTag: accepts a scalar or a sequence, and when it's a sequence, all tags must match. Two optional keys are available: tagProperty: names the tag container property explicitly, and matchAssets: also matches data-asset instances (default true): type: cdo conditions: hasMod: KAPI patches: - matchTag: KMods.AlternateRecipe # scalar; use a block sequence for multiple tags ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe # required scope tagProperty: mGameplayTags # optional explicit tag container property matchAssets: true # also match data-asset instances (default true) properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.8 Register your own tags first using type: gametag. The GameTags stage always runs before everything else. Then match on them in the same pack: see Game Tags.

sections.heading: `matchName:` select by class name pattern
sections.text: Matches the class name against a wildcard pattern (* any run of characters, ? one character, case-insensitive). The trailing _C of Blueprint classes is optional in the pattern. When the pattern contains a /, it is matched against the full class path instead, which lets you select by content folder. A sequence matches when any pattern matches: type: cdo patches: - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe matchName: Recipe_Alternate_* # every vanilla alternate recipe, no tags needed properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.8 - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematic matchName: /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/* # by folder: the milestones properties: mTimeToComplete: $op: multiply value: 0.5 For data-asset instances the pattern is matched against the asset's own name and path, not its class.

sections.heading: `producedIn:` / `ingredient:` / `product:` recipe shortcuts
sections.text: The three shortcuts answer the questions pack authors ask most often about recipes, without spelling out a where: clause. Each accepts a class path (any form that target: accepts: full path, bare class name, or generated-content id) or a sequence of them, and a recipe matches when any entry is referenced or one of its subclasses is: type: cdo patches: # every recipe crafted in a Constructor is 25% faster - producedIn: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/ConstructorMk1/Build_ConstructorMk1.Build_ConstructorMk1_C properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.75 # every recipe crafted in ANY manufacturing building (Constructor, Assembler, Manufacturer, # Refinery, Blender, Particle Accelerator, modded machines deriving from the same base, …) - producedIn: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableManufacturer properties: mVariablePowerConsumptionFactor: $op: multiply value: 0.9 # every recipe that consumes Plastic OR Rubber - ingredient: - Desc_Plastic_C - Desc_Rubber_C properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.9 # every recipe that produces a Screw, but only when it is crafted in an Assembler - product: Desc_IronScrew_C producedIn: Build_AssemblerMk1_C properties: mProduct[0].Amount: $op: multiply value: 2 The subclass rule is what makes the native base classes useful as values: FGBuildableManufacturer covers every machine that derives from it, /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildGun covers every build-gun (buildable) recipe, and /Script/FactoryGame.FGWorkBench covers every hand-craftable recipe (the vanilla Craft Bench is BP_WorkBenchComponent_C, a subclass). A class that is not loaded yet when the patch runs is matched by exact path only (a warning tells you), the subclass rule needs the class resolved.

sections.heading: `where:` filter by property values
sections.text: where: compares reflected properties of every candidate in the scope. It takes one map, or a sequence of maps. Clauses use AND by default, so every clause must hold. Set sibling whereMode: OR to require any clause instead. whereMode accepts AND or OR case-insensitively and is invalid without where. Other filters on the same entry remain AND-combined with the final where result. Each map names a path: (the same property path grammar as properties:, plus [*] for "any element") and exactly one operator: | Operator | Applies to | Matches when … | | equals, notEquals | everything | the value equals the given YAML value (class references: the class or a subclass) | | lessThan, lessOrEqual, greaterThan, greaterOrEqual | numbers, enums (ordinal), booleans | numeric comparison | | contains, notContains | arrays, sets, tag containers, strings/names/text | an element equals the value (same rules as equals), the container has the tag, or the text contains the substring | | in, notIn | everything | any listed value matches: equals for a scalar leaf, contains for an array/set/tag container leaf | | matches | everything | the display text matches a wildcard pattern (*Alternate*); references use their path | | isEmpty: true/false | containers, text, references | the container/text is empty, or the reference is null | A candidate that does not have the property does not match. A comparison that cannot apply to the property's type (greaterThan on an array, [*] on a float, …) is reported once per patch entry as a warning naming the path. Remember that the scope class's own CDO is a candidate as well, and it only holds default values: isEmpty: true on mProducedIn matches FGRecipe itself, not just the orphaned Blueprint recipes you were thinking of. /kdf report lists every object a patch touched. type: cdo patches: # liquid OR gas descriptors get no sink points - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor whereMode: OR where: - path: mForm equals: RF_LIQUID - path: mForm equals: RF_GAS properties: mResourceSinkPoints: 0 # long recipes (more than 8 seconds) that use Iron Ingot get a bit faster - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe where: - path: mManufactoringDuration greaterThan: 8 - path: mIngredients[*].ItemClass # [*] = any element equals: Desc_IronIngot_C properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.8 # every schematic up to tier 3 completes instantly - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematic where: path: mTechTier # a single clause can be written as one map lessOrEqual: 3 properties: mTimeToComplete: 0 # liquids and gases never earn sink points (`in` = any of the listed values) - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor where: path: mForm in: - RF_LIQUID - RF_GAS properties: mResourceSinkPoints: 0 # recipes crafted in a Constructor OR an Assembler (`in` on an array = contains any) - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe where: path: mProducedIn in: - Build_ConstructorMk1_C - Build_AssemblerMk1_C properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.9 # recipes nobody can craft anywhere (empty mProducedIn) get the Craft Bench - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe where: path: mProducedIn isEmpty: true properties: mProducedIn: $op: append value: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/-Shared/WorkBench/BP_WorkBenchComponent.BP_WorkBenchComponent_C [*] may appear more than once in a path (mUnlocks[*].mRecipes[*]) and descends through struct members and object references alike; a where: clause with [*] matches when any element path satisfies the operator. [*] is read-only: a properties: op still has to address one concrete element (mIngredients[0].Amount). Inside a where: path a class reference reads through to its defaults: mProduct[0].ItemClass.mForm compares the produced item's form, and mUnlocks[*].mRecipes[*].mProducedIn on a schematic walks into every unlocked recipe's producer list (soft references are loaded on demand). This is a filter convenience only; properties: ops never write through a class reference. Filters and the lazy class watch: like applyToSubclasses:, every scope-filter patch keeps watching the session. A Blueprint recipe or item class that loads later (common for content the game only references on demand), or a native-parent class generated by KDF, is tested against the same filters once its class and CDO are initialized, and patched when it passes. A not-yet-resolved explicit class target is also watched by its exact path, including a generated class created in a later content stage. KDF does not force CDO creation during class allocation.

sections.heading: The same filters in `remove:`, `block:`, and `sinkpoints` entries
sections.text: The scope filters are not a cdo feature. Every document type that selects existing content takes the same keys in place of one exact reference, with a default scope that fits the type: | Document / key | Filter entry selects | Default ofClass: | Details | | type: recipe → remove: | recipes to take out of the game | FGRecipe | Removing Content | | type: schematic → remove: | schematics to take out of the game | FGSchematic | Removing Content | | type: research / mam → remove: | research trees to take out of the game | FGResearchTree | Removing Content | | type: resourcenode → remove: | resource descriptors whose placed nodes are purged | FGResourceDescriptor | Resources | | type: sublevel → block: | provider data assets to block | none, ofClass: required | Sublevels | | type: sinkpoints → entries: | item descriptors that receive the entry's points: | FGItemDescriptor | Sink Points | type: recipe remove: - producedIn: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/HadronCollider/Build_HadronCollider.Build_HadronCollider_C type: sinkpoints entries: - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor where: path: mForm in: - RF_LIQUID - RF_GAS points: 0 Recipe, schematic, and research removal rules are stored as predicates and re-checked against every class the game presents, so late-loading Blueprint content is covered. Resource-node, sublevel, and sink-point filters expand once, when the document applies, against what is loaded at that moment; the load report tells you how many matched.

sections.heading: `applyToSubclasses:` widen a class target to every derived class
sections.text: With a class target, applyToSubclasses: true also patches every derived class's CDO: type: cdo patches: - target: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableResourceExtractor applyToSubclasses: true # every miner, oil extractor, water pump, … properties: mExtractMultiplier: $op: min value: 2 > ⚠️ Wide blast radius. Subclass expansion covers _every_ derived class, including ones added > by other mods you may never have heard of. Prefer the most-derived class that still covers what > you mean. Use min/max/clamp/multiply rather than absolute set where possible, and check > /kdf report to see exactly which classes were patched.

sections.heading: `applyToSpawnedActors:` runtime actor patches
sections.text: For actor classes, saves and archetypes override CDO values on already-placed instances. Setting applyToSpawnedActors: true re-applies the ops to every instance the moment it spawns (world begin play and every later spawn): type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Buildable/Factory/StorageContainerMk1/Build_StorageContainerMk1.Build_StorageContainerMk1_C applyToSpawnedActors: true # re-applied to every instance the moment it spawns applyToSubclasses: false # exact class only properties: mInventorySizeX: 12 mInventorySizeY: 8 These instance writes are unconditional. They do not compare a value against the vanilla snapshot or preserve a value changed by a player or save. Resource Nodes are an important consequence of class-only actor matching. KDataForge cannot select one placed node by location, descriptor, purity, amount, or node type. See Resources and Resource Nodes.

sections.heading: Actor lifecycle actions
sections.text: Use actorAction to remove live actors rather than edit their class defaults: type: cdo patches: - target: /MyMod/Retired/Build_Prototype.Build_Prototype_C applyToSubclasses: true applyToSpawnedActors: true actorAction: dismantle target must name actor classes; a target list is supported. applyToSpawnedActors: true is required: actions cover existing actors and future spawns. applyToSubclasses defaults to false. Omit properties; an action and property operations require separate entries. CDO scope filters such as ofClass, allAssetsOfClass and where are not supported here. Optional actorSelector predicates use the existing server-only instance selection. Generated actor IDs are created after the CDOChanges stage. Add deferOneGameTick: true when targeting these IDs so registration runs after generation and BeginPlay. The action then uses its normal subsequent world timer tick; existing native or cooked actor classes do not need this extra registration delay. - destroy calls the actor's normal destruction function. - dismantle calls the game's dismantle interface on child dismantle actors, then the parent. Actors without that interface use normal destruction instead. Actions wait until the actor has begun play, then run on a subsequent world timer tick. Replicated actors are changed by their authority. Local, non-replicated client actors can also be removed locally; a client never removes a remote replicated actor through this action. Reload and world shutdown cancel pending callbacks. Removing or reloading the pack does not recreate actors already removed; destruction of saved or level-placed actors may persist in the save. Use a disposable save when first validating a removal pack. The visual CDO editor exposes Instance operation with property operations, destroy and dismantle choices. Remove existing property operations before choosing an action. Class reflection alone cannot preview live actor matches; Affected elements reports this selection as limited.

sections.heading: Player inventory remapping
sections.text: Use inventoryRemap to replace existing player inventory items and convert items added later: type: cdo patches: - target: /Script/FactoryGame.FGCharacterPlayer applyToSubclasses: true applyToSpawnedActors: true inventoryRemap: - from: /MyMod/Items/Desc_Old.Desc_Old_C to: /MyMod/Items/Desc_New.Desc_New_C multiplier: 10 Targets must be FGCharacterPlayer classes or subclasses. The explicit target and applyToSpawnedActors: true are required. applyToSubclasses defaults to false. Each entry names concrete item descriptor classes. multiplier defaults to 1 and must be an unquoted integer from 1 to 2147483647. Use a separate patch for property writes or actorAction; asset and class scope filters are unavailable for inventory remapping. Generated item IDs require deferOneGameTick: true so registration follows item generation. Conversions run on the server after the player and inventory are ready. They handle existing players and later spawns, then listen for item additions, removals and inventory expansion. The complete output must fit while original stacks still occupy their slots. Otherwise originals remain and conversion retries on later inventory changes. A quantity above the 32-bit item-count limit also leaves originals unchanged. Partial conversions are not allowed. Sources must be unique. A destination cannot also be a source: chained and cyclic conversions are unsupported. Runtime validation also rejects conflicting or chained rules from separate entries whose player target classes overlap. Conversions replace descriptor and count; per-item dynamic state is not transferred. Optional actorSelector predicates keep their normal server-only behavior. Reload unbinds previous callbacks and applies current rules; it does not turn already converted items back into their originals. In the visual CDO editor, choose Instance operation → Remap player inventory. Add conversions, choose source and output descriptors, then enter numeric multipliers. Existing conversion rows must be removed before switching operation modes. Affected elements reports live inventory selection as limited; exported class defaults do not describe player inventory contents.

sections.heading: Choosing a selector
sections.text: The selector keys cover targets from a single class to every actor in a class family. Use the table below to choose the narrowest useful selector: | I want to patch… | Selector | | One recipe / item / building class | target: class path | | One data-asset instance | target: object path (no _C) | | A handful of unrelated targets, same properties: | target: sequence of paths | | A whole data-asset family | allAssetsOfClass: | | Everything carrying a tag | matchTag: + ofClass: | | Every class whose name / folder matches a pattern | matchName: + ofClass: | | Every recipe crafted in a building (or building family) | producedIn: | | Every recipe consuming / producing an item (or item family) | ingredient: / product: | | Everything whose property values meet a condition | where: + ofClass: | | A base class and everything derived | class target: + applyToSubclasses: true | | Values on placed/spawning actors | + applyToSpawnedActors: true | Filters combine: producedIn: + ingredient: + where: on one entry select recipes that satisfy all three. Prefer the narrowest combination that still describes what you mean, and check /kdf report to see exactly which classes were patched.

pages.title: Templates and typed references
pages.description: Read configuration, game settings, reflected properties, and functions from YAML values.

sections.heading: Templates and typed references
sections.text: KDataForge supports two forms of value substitution: unquoted typed references such as cfg:balance.ironSpeed, and template tokens such as {cfg:balance.ironSpeed} inside strings. Configuration and game-setting reads run before document stages; reflected property reads and function calls run when a property operation applies.

sections.heading: Typed references
sections.text: A typed reference must occupy an entire plain, unquoted YAML scalar. Prefixes are case-sensitive. These forms are supported: | Form | Source | | cfg:<id> | A configuration field in the current pack | | cfg:<pack>:<id> | A configuration field in another pack | | session:<id> | An SML session setting, with an advanced-game-setting fallback | | ags:<id> | An advanced game setting | | option:<id> | A local game option | The replacement keeps its type: numbers and booleans become scalar values, strings become string values, and a configuration field with multiple enabled becomes a YAML sequence. The resolved type must suit the destination property or operation. For example, after defining the numeric configuration field balance.ironSpeed in your pack, use its value as a divisor: type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: divide value: cfg:balance.ironSpeed Writing value: 'cfg:balance.ironSpeed' keeps literal text. An unknown configuration id leaves the reference unresolved and produces a warning; it does not supply a default value.

sections.heading: Templates
sections.text: Use braces to insert a value into text: value: 'Smelts at {cfg:balance.ironSpeed}x speed.' The pre-pass recognizes {cfg:<id>}, {cfg:<pack>:<id>}, {session:<id>}, {ags:<id>} and {option:<id>}. Lists inserted into text are joined with , . Quote YAML values that start with { so YAML does not parse them as mappings. The pre-pass walks document scalar values, but skips map keys, values of id, type, include and ref, and everything inside conditions:. Conditions have their own expression rules; a template is not a replacement for a condition expression. Tokens can nest up to four levels. Values produced by substitution are not scanned again as new template source.

sections.heading: Game settings
sections.text: session: reads SML session settings, falling back to an advanced game setting with the same id. ags: reads advanced game settings directly. Both require a loaded world: documents that use them are deferred on the main menu and applied again when the setting changes. option: reads local game options, which are available on the main menu as well. Each provider supports both an unquoted typed reference and a braced text token. For example, ags:FG.GameRules.NoPower is a typed value, while 'No power: {ags:FG.GameRules.NoPower}' is text. Find actual ids and value types in your bound datapack's indexes/settings.json. Its other records are not readable through these prefixes. See Reflection Export: Settings index for the record fields. A setting's exported default describes its default, not its current value in a running save.

sections.heading: Providers
sections.text: Apply-time tokens use {provider:<target>:<member>}. A member can be a reflected property path or a permitted function call. They work in operation operands such as value, min and max, including nested struct members and sequence elements. | Provider | Target | | class | Any class, including a function library | | item | A class derived from UFGItemDescriptor | | resource | A class derived from UFGResourceDescriptor | | building | A class derived from AFGBuildable | | recipe | A class derived from UFGRecipe | | schematic | A class derived from UFGSchematic | | research | A class derived from UFGResearchTree | | category | A class derived from UFGCategory | | dataasset | A UDataAsset instance, by asset path or generated dataasset id | | asset | An asset instance by path | Class providers read the class default object (CDO), rather than a placed actor in the world. Use the matching provider for a specific class family; building rejects a class that does not derive from AFGBuildable. dataasset and asset read object instances.

sections.heading: Whole-token typed values
sections.text: An apply-time operand consisting of exactly one token keeps the result's type. It can copy a number, boolean or sequence instead of converting it into surrounding text. For example, this copies the Iron Ingot recipe's crafting duration: mManufactoringDuration: '{recipe:/Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C:mManufactoringDuration}' Adding surrounding text makes the result text instead. Quotes around the YAML string do not disable braced templates; they only disable the unbraced typed-reference form.

sections.heading: Calling functions
sections.text: Write arguments in parentheses after the function name. For example, this operation operand calls a math-library function: mProduct[0].Amount: '{class:/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary:Round(2.6)}' Arguments can include numbers, booleans, quoted strings, nested tokens and supported struct literals. Arguments follow the reflected declaration order. For example, {class:/Script/Engine.KismetMathLibrary:VSize(Vector{3, 4, 0})} passes a vector struct. Only permitted native functions can run. A function must return a value and be BlueprintPure or a non-static const member. Unsupported parameter or return types, output parameters, network functions, events, delegates and Exec functions are rejected. Non-static functions of actors, components and subsystems are also rejected; read their CDO properties instead. The editor uses exported function records to offer member completion, signatures and validation. Export with --functions to include those records; see Reflection Export: Functions. Static checks depend on the bound datapack and do not execute functions or read live settings.

sections.heading: Escaping
sections.text: A backslash immediately before a registered token's opening brace keeps it literal: value: 'Use \{cfg:balance.ironSpeed} to read the speed.' Single-quoted, plain and block YAML scalars take \{ as written. In a double-quoted YAML string, write \\{ so YAML produces one backslash. Each expansion phase removes only its own escapes. Unknown prefixes and unterminated tokens remain literal text.

pages.title: Type: unlock
pages.description: Generate a reusable FGUnlock subclass, or use a schematic's inline unlock list for ordinary recipe unlocks.

sections.heading: Type: unlock
sections.text: This document type sits in the Items stage at priority 40, after generic class (50) and ahead of item, resource, and building. That ordering lets later content reference generated unlock classes. It loads during session initialization, so a restart is needed after changes. Its entries key is unlocks. There is no default parent; provide a concrete FGUnlock subclass that derives from /Script/FactoryGame.FGUnlock. Register-only entries (class:) are not supported, so use id:. Most packs do not need this document type. To make a schematic unlock a recipe, use the schematic's inline unlocks: list. See Schematics → Instanced unlocks. That creates an unlock instance directly on the schematic's CDO with no separate class needed. type: unlock exists for a narrower case. You want one preconfigured unlock class, with baked-in default properties, that you intend to reference by class from multiple schematics, or hand off to another mod, without repeating the same property block every time. parent: can be any concrete FGUnlock subclass the base game ships. See the Base-Game Unlock Classes for the full list and their settable properties.

sections.heading: Worked example, a reusable "give starter items" unlock
sections.text: The pattern below generates a single FGUnlockInventorySlot subclass with its slot count baked in. Any schematic can then grant the exact same reward just by pointing at the generated class, instead of re-declaring the property every time: # file: starter-kit.unlock.yml type: unlock unlocks: - id: MyStarterKitUnlock parent: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockInventorySlot.BP_UnlockInventorySlot_C # any concrete FGUnlock subclass properties: mNumInventorySlotsToUnlock: 3 This generates /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_MyStarterKitUnlock, a class, not an instance. Reference it from a schematic exactly like any other unlock class: # file: some.schematic.yml type: schematic schematics: - id: Schematic_UsesStarterKit properties: mDisplayName: Starter Kit Schematic unlocks: - class: /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MyStarterKitUnlock

sections.heading: Why it has to run first
sections.text: Unlocks generate at priority 40, after generic class (50) and ahead of item (30), resource (25), and building (20). All five sit within the Items stage. This ordering exists specifically so that a schematic generated later in the same pack can reference the unlock class the moment it's created, with no include: gymnastics needed.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - "Why didn't my item unlock show up on the schematic?" Nine times out of ten this means you meant the schematic's inline unlocks: list (a FGUnlockRecipe/FGUnlockSchematic/etc. instance configured right where it's used), not a standalone generated class. See Type: schematic first. - Reusing one unlock class across many schematics and want to change a default later? Edit the type: unlock document's properties:. Every schematic referencing that generated class picks up the new CDO default the next time a fresh instance is created from it. Existing save data that already holds an old instance is unaffected, same as any other CDO-default change.

pages.title: Create your first pack
pages.description: Build one recipe patch, load it in game, and verify the result.

sections.heading: Create your first pack
sections.text: This tutorial creates a pack with one manifest and one patch. The patch halves the smelting time for iron ingots. You will then confirm that KDataForge found and applied it. You need KDataForge installed and permission to start a local game, host a game, or administer a dedicated server. If you only want to install someone else's pack, use the Player guide.

sections.heading: 1. Create the pack folder
sections.text: Create this folder under the mod or project that will ship the pack: <your-mod>/DataForge/ KDataForge searches up to six directory levels below the Unreal project directory, which is FactoryGame/ in a packaged game. A directory becomes a pack root when its name is DataForge, uses the legacy name data-editor, or directly contains pack.yml. These names are case-insensitive. KDataForge ignores heavy engine directories such as Content, Saved, Plugins, and Source. It also ignores Docs, Scripts, and directories whose names start with . during root discovery and document collection. Keep pack documents outside those directories. KDataForge Tools and linter use the same exclusions; direct validation of an excluded file can parse its YAML but reports root.ignored-directory because the runtime will not load it. Detected pack roots may nest. A YAML file belongs only to its deepest enclosing root, so a parent pack does not load the same file again.

sections.heading: 2. Add the manifest
sections.text: Create <your-mod>/DataForge/pack.yml: ref: MyFirstPack name: My First Pack version: 1.0.0 The manifest gives the pack a stable identity. KDataForge can load a root without pack.yml, but then it derives the pack ref and name from the parent directory. Moving that directory can change the identity. Declare ref before release because generated content and save persistence use it.

sections.heading: 3. Add the patch
sections.text: Create /DataForge/faster-smelting.cdo.yml: type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.5 A type: cdo document edits a class default object. This patch multiplies the iron-ingot recipe's manufacturing duration by 0.5. KDataForge reads every *.yml and *.yaml file below the pack root. A file may contain several documents separated by ---; each document then needs its own type:. In a single-document file, the suffix ..yml can supply the type, but an explicit type: takes precedence. See Multiple documents per file. Your pack now has this shape: /DataForge/ pack.yml faster-smelting.cdo.yml

sections.heading: 4. Load and verify the pack
sections.text: 1. Start the game and open a save. 2. Enter /kdf report in chat. 3. Find MyFirstPack and faster-smelting.cdo.yml in the report. 4. Check an iron-ingot recipe. Its smelting time should be half the original value. /kdf report lists detected packs and documents, applied operations, warnings, and errors. An error skips the affected file, document, or patch while loading continues. A warning reports a tolerated problem, such as an unknown root type or duplicate pack ref. Info diagnostics describe expected skips, such as a failed mod-version condition, and do not appear in /kdf report.

sections.heading: 5. Reload an edit
sections.text: After changing the YAML: 1. Save the file. 2. Run /kdf reload as the host or a dedicated-server administrator. You can run KDF.Reload in the host or server console instead. 3. Run /kdf report and check the result again. Reload works only after initial loading has finished. It restores captured property baselines, rescans the pack roots, and applies the current pack set in that process. It does not synchronize connected clients. Restart the session for frozen content registrations, irreversible world changes, and fields marked as cold or restart-bound. Packs that generate native CDO helper assets disable manual and automatic reload. Restart after changing, disabling, or removing one because its native callbacks and caches cannot be reset live.

sections.heading: Trace an applied operation
sections.text: Add debug: true to one document to log its operations: type: cdo debug: true patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.5 You can put debug: true in pack.yml to trace every document in that pack. For all packs, run KDF.Debug 1, use /kdf debug on, or launch the game with -KDFDebug. Global debug logging also includes operations made in the in-game editor. Each applied operation produces one line at Log verbosity: [KDF DEBUG] faster-smelting.cdo.yml: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C.mManufactoringDuration multiply : 2.000000 -> 1.000000 The line follows <file>: <target>.<property> <op> : <before> -> <after>. Packaged-game logs are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\FactoryGame\Saved\Logs\FactoryGame.log. Search for [KDF DEBUG]. You can also run /kdf editor to request the host-local editor window, browse live objects, edit properties, undo or redo changes, and export those changes as YAML. The command branch does not perform the reload/configuration host-permission check, but the editor still works only in the process that opens it.

sections.heading: Multiplayer check
sections.text: Install the same pack set and versions on the host or dedicated server and every client. Each process loads YAML independently. KDataForge does not compare checksums, reject mismatches, transfer pack files, or stream applied operations. Live changes made in /kdf editor remain in that process. Export them to YAML and distribute the updated pack when every player needs the same values.

sections.heading: If the result is missing
sections.text: | Symptom | Check | | KDataForge ignores the file | Add type: or rename a single-document file to <name>.<type>.yml. | | One document in a ----separated file is ignored | Add type: to that document. Filename inference works only for single-document files. | | The report says class not found | Use _C for a cooked Blueprint class, /Script/Module.Class for a native class, or /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> for a generated class. Generated classes do not use _C. An unambiguous short id: also works. | | The operation is rejected | Check the operation's supported property kinds in YAML schema and Operations. | | A data-asset instance is not found | Remove _C; object instances are not classes. See Targeting. | | A changed default does not affect placed buildings | A save or archetype can override the default. Use applyToSpawnedActors where appropriate; see Buildings. | For a longer diagnosis, follow Debug a pack that will not apply.

sections.heading: Continue authoring
sections.text: - Run Lint your pack before starting the game or sharing the pack. - Read Targeting before patching other classes or asset instances. - Follow Item, icon, recipe, and Tier 1 unlock to create a complete content chain. - Use Balancing or the end-to-end pack as larger examples. - Browse KPatchwork's public packs for maintained cross-mod compatibility examples.

pages.title: Lint your pack
pages.description: Run standalone KDataForge Linter or KPatchwork policy linter before starting game or opening pull request.

sections.heading: Lint your pack
sections.text: The standalone KDataForge Linter validates packs with bundled schemas. Pass the lint subcommand and a path: kdataforge-linter lint DataForge kdataforge-linter lint DataForge --format github kdataforge-linter lint DataForge --format json kdataforge-linter lint DataForge --allow-unknown-types Useful options include --schema-dir <dir> for extra schemas, --allow-schema-override when a custom schema intentionally replaces a bundled one, --allow-unknown-types for handler types that the linter does not know yet, --warnings-as-errors, and --format text|json|github. It also checks instanced FGUnlock and FGAvailabilityDependency references in schematics, research trees, and delivery-task data assets. Native classes with known Blueprint implementations, abstract classes without Blueprint variants, wrong-family references, and unknown class paths emit warnings only. They do not turn an otherwise valid pack into exit code 1 unless you enable --warnings-as-errors. Base-Game Unlock Classes, Mod Unlock Classes, and Availability Dependency Classes document bundled inventory.

sections.heading: KPatchwork policy schemas
sections.text: KPatchwork repository runs this same kdataforge-linter executable, pinned through its pyproject.toml and uv.lock. Repository-local schemas under ci/schemas override selected bundled schemas with KPatchwork policy, such as its required player-facing pack description. Its public DataForge directory also provides maintained examples of complete compatibility packs. Use their YAML as examples of pack organization and conditional integrations, while keeping the repository-specific policy fields described below separate from the runtime grammar. The linter is also the validation step used by KPatchwork's pull-request CI. It reports every issue it finds in one run: warnings are printed but do not fail the command, while errors produce exit code 1. Run KPatchwork's exact CI-equivalent command from its repository root: uv run --locked kdataforge-linter lint DataForge --schema-dir ci/schemas --allow-schema-override --format github

sections.heading: Get the linter
sections.text: Install uv and Git, then clone KPatchwork: git clone https://github.com/Satisfactory-KMods/KPatchwork.git cd KPatchwork KPatchwork currently requires Python 3.11 or newer. uv run --locked creates the required Python environment from the repository's lockfile, so you do not need to install PyYAML manually.

sections.heading: Choose the correct root
sections.text: The positional <path> after lint is the directory searched recursively for pack.yml files and YAML documents. Every manifest must be at least one directory below that path. For the standard standalone layout from Getting Started, pass <your-mod>, not its DataForge child: <your-mod>/ DataForge/ pack.yml faster-smelting.cdo.yml From the cloned KPatchwork directory, its pinned executable can also lint an external mod without the repository policy override: uv run --locked kdataforge-linter lint "<your-mod>" For a repository containing several nested packs, pass their common container instead: | Pack layout | <path> value | | <your-mod>/DataForge/pack.yml | <your-mod> | | <your-mod>/DataForge/<pack-name>/pack.yml | <your-mod>/DataForge | | KPatchwork/DataForge/<category>/<pack>/pack.yml | DataForge | The linter examines every .yml and .yaml below the selected root. Choose the narrowest root that still leaves at least one directory between the root and each pack.yml; otherwise unrelated YAML files may be reported as being outside a pack.

sections.heading: KPatchwork policy fields
sections.text: :::caution KPatchwork's policy linter requires a contributer field spelled exactly this way. This is repository ownership metadata, not a required KDataForge runtime manifest field. A standalone pack can be valid at runtime and still fail this policy check when the field is absent. The current standalone KDataForge Linter schema also validates contributer, so it may report the same field. Treat that as current linter policy, not runtime grammar. Standalone schemas accept an optional string description in pack.yml. KPatchwork's override requires it because CI uses the text on its generated mod page. KDataForge runtime ignores it. ::: When preparing a pack for KPatchwork, add your GitHub login or a non-empty list of co-maintainers: ref: MyTweaks name: My Tweaks version: 1.0.0 description: Explains player-facing compatibility changes supplied by this pack. contributer: - your-github-login KPatchwork CI uses this value for ownership checks as well as linting. Changing the field in that repository requires maintainer approval.

sections.heading: What current standalone linter checks
sections.text: The current linter checks: - YAML syntax, empty documents, and explicit type values in multi-document files; - pack manifests, semver-like versions, unique refs, dependencies, missing dependencies, and dependency cycles; - known document types and the filename-based <name>.<type>.yml convention; - conditions, patch selectors, property paths, operation names, and required operation arguments; - inline instances and generated IDs, including duplicate IDs within a pack; - generated classes, unlocks, items, resources, buildings, recipes, schematics, and research-tree mutations; - top-level remove: for recipe/schematic/research documents, including remove-only documents; - sublevel blocking documents and resourcenode removal documents; - float/vector curve keys, modes, finite values, and duplicate key times; - included files, image assets, data assets, localization entries, game tags, and sink-point entries; - symlinks, YAML outside a pack, and files that escape the selected root or pack directory. Unknown condition keys are warnings. Unknown document root types are warnings only when you pass --allow-unknown-types; otherwise the standalone linter reports them as errors because no schema was available. Structural problems, invalid values, missing files, and duplicate identities are errors.

sections.heading: Version notes
sections.text: Use a current standalone KDataForge Linter build when using newer runtime handlers. Current bundled schemas cover type: sublevel, type: resourcenode, and top-level remove: on type: recipe, type: schematic, and type: research, including remove-only documents. Older linter releases may report those documents as unknown root types or reject remove: as an unexpected field. In that case, update the linter before treating the diagnostic as authoritative. After linting, still verify in game with /kdf report; static schemas cannot prove runtime class resolution or another mod's installed content.

sections.heading: Bundled Rust CLI reports
sections.text: KDataForge Tools also bundles the current Rust validator used by its language server: kdf lint PATH --format json kdf lint PATH --format sarif kdf why PATH --format text kdf why PATH --format json --rule RULE_ID --line 12 JSON and SARIF share stable rule IDs, UTF-16 source ranges, explanation IDs, and structured evidence. why explains only evidence emitted by validation/reflection; missing evidence stays unknown. Exit codes are 0 success, 1 lint findings under selected warning policy, 2 usage/configuration, and 3 internal failure. This Rust CLI is separate from the historical standalone Python linter above. KPatchwork may pin an older standalone release until its lockfile is updated. Its ci/schemas directory overrides only repository-policy schemas; it does not add every newer runtime handler. Use a current standalone build when checking new KDataForge grammar outside KPatchwork CI.

sections.heading: Read the result
sections.text: A successful run prints the number of packs and documents it checked: lint passed: 1 pack(s), 1 YAML document(s) Errors include the file and the failed rule. Fix every error: line, then run the same command again: error: /path/to/pack.yml: version '1.0' is not semver-like error: /path/to/faster-smelting.cdo.yml: cdo.patches[0] requires properties The linter has no automatic-fix mode. Show current CLI options with: uv run --locked kdataforge-linter lint --help

sections.heading: Scripted packs
sections.text: The YAML linter checks documents only. If your pack also has TypeScript scripts, use the KDataForgeJS command line tool (@sf-kmods/kdataforgejs-cli) on the project folder: npx @sf-kmods/kdataforgejs-cli game-data npx @sf-kmods/kdataforgejs-cli sync npx @sf-kmods/kdataforgejs-cli format npx @sf-kmods/kdataforgejs-cli check npx @sf-kmods/kdataforgejs-cli lint npx @sf-kmods/kdataforgejs-cli validate game-data finds a Windows Steam/Epic or Linux Steam installation containing KDataForge and KDataForgeJS, loads the newest local save, waits for reflection export, exits the game, and imports .kdataforge/satisfactory.kdfdata plus generated declarations. DataForge/typescript/kdataforgejs/index.d.ts references smaller files grouped by symbol and Unreal path. They cover native and Blueprint classes present in the active export, including classes not named in the pack manifest. Pass --game-path <root-or-executable> to select an installation. Timeout is 15 minutes; --timeout <seconds> changes it. No console command or manual archive extraction is needed. sync derives imports, hashes, and reflected classes from source usage. format and lint use bundled Biome. check type-checks scripts against installed-game types. validate checks manifest, entry file, static imports, and import digests. These commands run without starting Satisfactory.

sections.heading: What static linting cannot prove
sections.text: The linter parses files without loading Unreal Engine or Satisfactory. It cannot prove that an asset or class path exists, that a reflected property has the expected runtime type, that another mod is installed, or that two otherwise valid packs produce the intended result together. After linting, start the game and use /kdf report to check runtime resolution and application. Use debug logging when you need the before/after value for each applied operation.

pages.title: Reference
pages.description: Look up exact YAML grammar, defaults, catalogs, APIs, and editor tools.

sections.heading: Reference
sections.text: Reference pages describe exact syntax and contracts. For a guided task, use the How-to guides. Use Authoring concepts for the underlying model and Document types and features for behavior specific to a document type.

sections.heading: Pack-author reference
sections.text: - Commands and console variables lists chat, runtime console, reflection, and Unreal Editor commands with permissions and process boundaries. - YAML schema defines pack manifests, document types, property paths, all 25 operations, conditions, and includes. - Configuration expressions defines config: operands, operators, evaluation, and diagnostics. Use it with Pack configuration and Templates and typed references. - Base-game unlock classes catalogs each base-game FGUnlock subclass, its path, properties, examples, and instantiation constraints. - Mod unlock classes catalogs unlock classes supplied by installed mods, including their Blueprint paths. - Availability dependency classes catalogs FGAvailabilityDependency classes, their abstract state, paths, and fields.

sections.heading: Authoring tools
sections.text: - VS Code extension and LSP covers .kdfdata import, project binding, reflection requirements, schema-only editing, and diagnostic status. - KDataForgeJS authoring in VS Code covers policy hover, capability analysis, typed completion, safe rename, forms, exports, and offline help. - KDataForgeJS runtime API covers hooks, lifecycle, structured values, DataTables, queries, overrides, and sandboxed YAML/JSON files. - KDataForgeJS SDK and CLI covers project updates and npm/pnpm multi-pack workspaces. - Reflection export defines export commands, options, archive contents, function and setting indexes, texture previews, validation, publication recovery, and reload classification.

sections.heading: Native developer reference
sections.text: - API design documents the public C++ contract in KDataForgeApi for third-party mods. - Template provider API documents native custom {prefix:body} values, phases, result states, registration, and diagnostics. - Blueprint configuration API documents pack and field queries, typed values, pending changes, apply/reset flows, events, and multiplayer writes. - Handler template provides a C++ implementation pattern for adding a YAML root type to KDataForge. - UE editor integration documents KDF.ApplyToAssets, which applies supported cdo patches to assets in Unreal Editor and marks their packages dirty. It does not run in the packaged game.

pages.title: API design
pages.description: Public C++ handler contract in KDataForgeApi and the KDataForge registration surface used by third-party mods.

sections.heading: API design
sections.text: Third-party handler types derive from KDataForgeApi. Handler registration calls UKDFSubsystem in the main KDataForge module, so a registering mod links both modules. Other implementation details may change between versions.

sections.heading: Stability guarantees
sections.text: IKDFDataEditorHandler, UKDFHandlerBase, FKDFNode, EKDFStage, EKDFOp, the context structs, and FKDFPatchRecord form the public handler contract. Additive changes are preferred. The main module exposes the registration and integration methods described below. The YAML schema is versioned through the documentation rather than C++ compatibility rules. Breaking schema changes belong in the changelog.

sections.heading: The `KDataForgeApi` contract
sections.text: Implement IKDFDataEditorHandler, or normally derive from UKDFHandlerBase, for one YAML root type. The interface is C++ only because UKDFDataEditorHandler declares CannotImplementInterfaceInBlueprint. class IKDFDataEditorHandler { virtual FName GetRootType() const = 0; virtual EKDFStage GetStage() const = 0; virtual int32 GetPriority() const; virtual bool ValidateDocument(const FKDFNode&, FKDFValidationContext&) = 0; virtual bool ApplyDocument(const FKDFNode&, FKDFApplyContext&) = 0; virtual bool ExportObject(UObject*, FKDFNode&, FKDFExportContext&); // optional virtual UClass* GetEditorPanelClass() const; // optional }; There is no RevertDocument virtual in the current interface. The framework parser handles raw YAML loading. ApplyDocument performs writes, ValidateDocument performs structural checks, ExportObject supports editor export, and GetEditorPanelClass can provide a custom panel.

sections.heading: `FKDFNode`, the document model
sections.text: Handlers receive an order-preserving map, sequence, and scalar tree rather than YAML text. Key helpers include Find, FindShared, GetString, GetBool, GetInt, GetFloat, their TryGet* variants, and the MakeMap, MakeSequence, and MakeScalar builders used by exporters.

sections.heading: Contexts
