sections.text: Contexts carry mGameInstance, mSourceFile, and a diagnostic sink with AddInfo, AddWarning, and AddError. Diagnostics are non-fatal. FKDFApplyContext adds bDryRun, mPatchRecord, and mAppliedOpCount. There is no bLiveReload flag in the current API. The same handler contexts are used during the initial pass and /kdf reload; a handler cannot distinguish those passes through a context flag.

sections.heading: Registration
sections.text: Register during your game instance module's CONSTRUCTION phase. Explicit subsystem initialization is required because SML can dispatch module lifecycle phases before custom GameInstance subsystems have been created. #include "Module/GameInstanceModuleManager.h" #include "Subsystems/KDFSubsystem.h" UGameInstanceModuleManager* Modules = GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UGameInstanceModuleManager>(); if (Modules != nullptr) { Modules->EnsureSubsystemInitialized(UKDFSubsystem::StaticClass()); if (UKDFSubsystem* KDF = UKDFSubsystem::Get(GetGameInstance())) { KDF->RegisterHandler(NewObject<UMyHandler>(KDF)); } } - Add KDataForgeApi for handler types and KDataForge for registration to your module dependencies. - The subsystem retains handler objects against garbage collection. - Registration after the initial load logs a warning. Matching documents can apply on the next successful /kdf reload or the next session. Register during CONSTRUCTION so the initial pass sees the handler and so cold registrations are available before world initialization. - Multiple handlers may claim the same root type. They all run in priority order.

sections.heading: Optional soft integration
sections.text: If you only want your mod's content to be editable, you do not need a custom handler. Reflected properties are already reachable through built-in cdo documents using target, allAssetsOfClass, and matchTag. Recommend a mod-presence condition: conditions: hasMod: YourModRef

sections.heading: Main-module surface
sections.text: Handler registration already links the main module. Handlers that generate content or integrate with the editor can also use these stable, additive entry points: | API | Purpose | | GetDynamicContent().GetOrCreateClass / GetOrCreateAsset | Create save-stable generated classes or UDataAsset instances | | QueueContentRegistration / QueueSinkTableRegistration | Queue per-world SML content registration before the freeze | | RegisterActorPatch / GetActorPatches / ClearActorPatches | Manage spawn-time FKDFActorPatch rules consumed by UKDFActorPatchSubsystem | | RegisterNodePurge / GetNodePurges / ClearNodePurges | Manage FKDFNodePurge rules consumed by UKDFResourceNodeSubsystem | | RegisterContentRemoval / GetContentRemovals / ClearContentRemovals | Manage exact-class FKDFContentRemoval rules for recipe, schematic, and research content | | MarkDataAssetsChanged | Request optional KAPI or RefinedRDApi consumer rescans after initial load | | ApplyEditorOp / RestorePropertyText | Apply editor writes and restore canonical property text for undo | | ExportObjectToYaml | Export an object to full or changes-only cdo YAML | | OnToggleEditorRequested() | Multicast hook used by the in-game editor UI | | FKDFPatchUtil::ApplyOpsToObject | Apply a parsed properties: sequence with pipeline semantics | | UKDFContentRemoveSubsystem | Apply recipe cleanup for one world and query exact removal rules/counts |

sections.heading: Runtime rule lifecycle
sections.text: The three Register* rule families above are retained on UKDFSubsystem for the GameInstance. Registering a rule with the same target class and source file replaces the previous rule. Clearing a rule array only stops later consumers; it does not undo actor writes, restore destroyed resource nodes, or put removed content back into an already-initialized manager. - RegisterActorPatch is normally driven by applyToSpawnedActors: true. At world begin play, UKDFActorPatchSubsystem applies matching rules to existing actors; its spawn delegate handles later actors. A rule registered after that initial sweep affects future spawns. Call ApplyPatchesToActor explicitly when a late integration also needs an existing actor updated. - RegisterNodePurge is normally driven by type: resourcenode. World initialization, actor-spawn, streamed-level, and deferred sweeps consume the rules. There is no public on-demand whole-world sweep, and destroyed level nodes can already have persistent vanilla save tombstones. - RegisterContentRemoval is normally driven by document-level remove:. Schematic and research filtering happens while RegisterQueuedContentForWorld drains the SML registry before its freeze. Recipe rules are different: native add hooks prevent later grants, and UKDFContentRemoveSubsystem::ApplyWorldRemovals can re-run its idempotent save-restored-recipe sweep when the rule set grows. Calling it late does not retroactively remove a schematic or research tree from a registry that already initialized. UKDFContentRemoveSubsystem::Get(WorldContext) exists only for Game and PIE worlds. Its IsRecipeRemoved and IsContentRemoved queries use exact class identity, not ancestry. GetAppliedRemovalCount reports resolvable rules seen by the last application pass, not the number of manager entries changed. WereRemovalsApplied becomes true after the first non-empty application pass and clearing the GameInstance rule list does not reset that per-world history flag. FKDFRecipeRemoval exposes lower-level HasAnyRemovalRules, IsRecipeRemoved, and the server-only SweepSaveRestoredRecipes helper. Normal integrations should use UKDFContentRemoveSubsystem so world timing and reporting stay centralized. Native recipe-add prevention is compiled for packaged runtime builds, not Unreal Editor PIE; PIE still exercises the initialization sweep. Treat unlisted implementation details in the main module as internal.

sections.heading: Versioning
sections.text: KDataForgeApi follows the mod's CI version. Handler ABI additions should be backwards compatible. Breaking schema changes must update the YAML Schema and the changelog.

sections.heading: Regenerate inventory
sections.text: Run Mods/GameFeatures/KDataForge/Tools/scan_instanced_class_catalog.py inside Unreal Python. It combines Asset Registry's transitive derived-class set and Blueprint ParentClass tags with native header metadata, then writes Saved/KDataForge/instanced-class-catalog.json by default. Set KDF_CLASS_CATALOG_OUTPUT to write a temp comparison file instead. The bundled KDataForge-Linter/src/kdataforge_linter/catalogs/instanced_classes.json snapshot already matches the current Unreal scan, so it does not need regeneration unless classes or Blueprint variants change.

sections.heading: Central Storage
sections.text: Three separate classes, one per axis. Combine as many as you need on one schematic: unlocks: - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockCentralStorageItemLimit.BP_UnlockCentralStorageItemLimit_C properties: mItemStackLimitIncrease: 5 - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockCentralStorageUploadSpeed.BP_UnlockCentralStorageUploadSpeed_C properties: mUploadSpeedPercentageDecrease: 10 # % faster upload (decreases UFGCentralStorageSettings::mDefaultTimeToUpload) - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockCentralStorageUploadSlots.BP_UnlockCentralStorageUploadSlots_C properties: mNumSlotsToUnlock: 1 | Class | Key property | What it does | | FGUnlockCentralStorageItemLimit | mItemStackLimitIncrease: int32 | More item stacks storable in Central Storage | | FGUnlockCentralStorageUploadSpeed | mUploadSpeedPercentageDecrease: float (Percent) | Faster central-storage uploads | | FGUnlockCentralStorageUploadSlots | mNumSlotsToUnlock: int32 | More concurrent upload queue slots |

sections.heading: Scanning and world interaction
sections.text: unlocks: - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockScannableResource.BP_UnlockScannableResource_C properties: mResourcePairsToAddToScanner: - ResourceDescriptor: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Bauxite/Desc_OreBauxite.Desc_OreBauxite_C ResourceNodeType: Node # Node | FrackingSatellite | FrackingCore | Geyser | Deposit - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockScannableObject.BP_UnlockScannableObject_C # Add mScannableObjects entries for world-object scan targets such as crates or POIs. | Class | Key property | What it does | | FGUnlockScannableResource | mResourcePairsToAddToScanner: TArray<FScannableResourcePair> (ResourceDescriptor + ResourceNodeType) | Grants Object Scanner detection for a resource | | FGUnlockScannableObject | mScannableObjects: TArray<FScannableObjectData> | Grants Object Scanner detection for non-resource world objects | | FGUnlockMap | _(no properties)_ | Unlocks the in-game map |

sections.heading: Customization and cosmetics
sections.text: unlocks: - class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGUnlockCustomization # Add mCustomizationUnlocks entries for outfits or skins. - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockEmote.BP_UnlockEmote_C properties: mEmotes: - /Game/FactoryGame/Emotes/Wave/Emote_Wave.Emote_Wave_C | Class | Key property | What it does | | FGUnlockCustomization | mCustomizationUnlocks: TArray<TSubclassOf<UFGPlayerCustomizationDesc>> | Player outfit/skin customization options | | FGUnlockCustomizer | _(no properties)_ | Unlocks the build-gun paint customizer feature itself | | FGUnlockEmote | mEmotes: TArray<TSubclassOf<UFGEmote>> | Grants emotes | | FGUnlockVisualizationMode | mVisualizationModes: TArray<TSubclassOf<UFGVisualizationModeDescriptor>> | Grants factory visualization modes (e.g. production/power overlays) |

sections.heading: Feature flags (no properties, presence alone unlocks the feature)
sections.text: These have no configurable properties at all; adding one to unlocks: is a bare class: entry: unlocks: - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockBuildOverclock.BP_UnlockBuildOverclock_C - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockBuildProductionBoost.BP_UnlockBuildProductionBoost_C - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockBuildEfficiency.BP_UnlockBuildEfficiency_C - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockCircuitDaisyChaining.BP_UnlockCircuitDaisyChaining_C | Class | What it does | | FGUnlockBuildOverclock | Unlocks overclocking (potential shards) on buildings | | FGUnlockBuildProductionBoost | Unlocks inserting production-boost shards into buildings | | FGUnlockBuildEfficiency | Unlocks the build-efficiency display on buildings | | FGUnlockCircuitDaisyChaining | Unlocks power-line daisy-chaining between poles |

sections.heading: Misc
sections.text: unlocks: - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockSAMIntensity.BP_UnlockSAMIntensity_C properties: mSAMIntensity: 2 - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockInfoOnly.BP_UnlockInfoOnly_C properties: mUnlockName: 'A cosmetic note' mUnlockDescription: 'Shown in the unlock UI grants nothing by itself.' | Class | Key property | What it does | | FGUnlockSAMIntensity | mSAMIntensity: int32 | Sets the intensity of SAM-node effects (e.g. VO) | | FGUnlockInfoOnly | mUnlockName/mUnlockDescription: FText, mUnlockIconBig/Small/Category: UTexture2D | Pure UI entry in the unlock list, grants no gameplay effect on its own | | FGUnlockCheckmark | _(inherits FGUnlockInfoOnly's fields)_ | Same as FGUnlockInfoOnly, plus tracks a per-player "seen/unlocked" checkmark in the save | | FGUnlockTape | mTapeUnlocks: TArray<TSubclassOf<UFGTapeData>> | Unlocks audio tapes in tape-player content | These classes plug into schematic instanced unlocks. Use Type: unlock to reuse one preconfigured unlock class across several schematics. Schematic dependencies: uses the equivalent instanced-array mechanism for mSchematicDependencies.

pages.title: Blueprint configuration API
pages.description: Query, edit, apply, synchronize, and observe KDataForge pack settings from Blueprint.

sections.heading: Blueprint configuration API
sections.text: UKDFConfigBlueprintLibrary exposes pack configuration to Blueprint. Use it when a mod needs its own settings screen or reacts to settings without using KDataForge's generated widgets. The API works with three main types: - FKDFPackInfo describes a pack and its configuration state. - UKDFConfigDescription describes one field and owns its current value state. - FKDFConfigApplyResult reports what happened when values were saved or synchronized. An empty PackRef means all packs for calls that accept a pack filter.

sections.heading: Query packs and fields
sections.text: | Blueprint node | Result | | Get All Pack Infos | Packs with at least one registered configuration field. Active packs use load order; skipped packs follow in ref order. | | Get Pack Info | One pack by ref, including packs without fields. Returns false when no matching ref exists. An active duplicate wins over inactive duplicates. | | Get Pack Config Descriptions | Map from category class to descriptions. Map order is undefined; descriptions inside each category use order, then field key. | | Get Sorted Config Categories | Category classes ordered by UFGCategory menu priority. | | Get Config Descriptions Flat | Fields ordered by category priority, then field order, then key. This is the usual source for a custom list UI. | | Get All Config Descriptions | Every non-stale field from every pack in registry order. | | Find Config Description | One field by the full <pack>:<id> key. | | Find Config Description By Id | One field by separate pack ref and id. | FKDFPackInfo supplies mRef, localized name and description, version, priority, icon, pack state, state reason, field count, pending-change state, and restart-required state. Dedicated servers do not decode pack icons. EKDFPackState distinguishes active packs from disabled manifests, duplicate refs, missing dependencies, dependency cycles, failed pack conditions, and skipped dependencies.

sections.heading: Read a field
sections.text: Every UKDFConfigDescription exposes identity, display metadata, type information, values, state, and source location. | Group | Getters | | Identity | Get Pack Ref, Get Id, Get Key | | Display | Get Display Name, Get Description Text, Get Tooltip, Has Tooltip, Get Category Class | | Shape | Get Apply Mode, Get Value Type, Is Array, Get Kind, Get Order | | Source | Get Source File, Get Source Line, Is Pack Active | | Values | Get Value, Get Effective Value, Get Default Value, Get Stored Value, Get Host Value | | Presentation | Get Value As String, Get Value As Display Text | | State | Is Dirty, Is Default, Is Restart Required, Is Restart Advised, Is Read Only, Is Host Override, Is Host Mismatch, Is Stale | The value slots have separate meanings: 1. Default comes from the field definition. 2. Stored comes from FactoryGame/Configs/Packs/<PackRef>.config.yml. 3. Pending contains an unsaved UI edit. 4. Host contains the multiplayer server override received by a client. 5. Effective is the value used by the currently loaded content. Get Value returns pending, host, or stored value in that order. A field can therefore display a new pending value while Get Effective Value still reports the value used by the current load. Reload keeps description object identity stable. A removed definition remains alive as stale but no longer appears in normal description lists. Do not keep stale descriptions in a settings panel.

sections.heading: Value types
sections.text: FKDFConfigValue stores a type, an array flag, and canonical text elements. Its EKDFConfigValueType is None, Bool, Int, Float, String, Text, Name, or Tag. Scalars contain one element. Fields with multiple: true use arrays and may contain any permitted number of elements. Canonical values use true or false for booleans, a whole decimal for integers, and fixed-point text without an exponent for floats. String-like values and gameplay tags keep their text. Comparison is case-sensitive. Use the Blueprint library helpers to build and read values: - Make Config Value Bool, Int, Float, String, Text, Name, or Tag - Make Config Value Array - Config Value To Bool, Int, Float, String, Text, or Tag - Config Values Equal FKDFConfigKeyedValue pairs a full <pack>:<id> key with a value. KDataForge uses this struct for configuration RPCs and replicated rows. The remaining supporting types are small value carriers: | Type | Values or fields | | EKDFConfigApplyMode | Cold, Hot | | EKDFConfigFieldKind | Text, Tag, Number, Slider, Boolean, Select, MultiSelect, List | | EKDFConfigNumberKind | Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, UInt8, Float, Double | | EKDFConfigTextKind | String, Text, Name | | FKDFConfigTooltip | Localized title and body text | | FKDFConfigOption | Typed value and localized label | | FKDFConfigDescriptionList | Description array used as the value in the category map |

sections.heading: Field-specific nodes
sections.text: Cast the base description when a UI needs constraints or a typed setter. | Description class | Field-specific Blueprint API | | KDFConfigTextDescription | Text kind, multiline flag, maximum length, string/text/name access, string and text setters | | KDFConfigTagDescription | Current tag, tag setter, tag root, selectable child tags | | KDFConfigNumberDescription | Number kind, integer flag, integer/float access, bounds, step, decimals | | KDFConfigSliderDescription | Normalized 0..1 value and normalized setter | | KDFConfigBooleanDescription | Boolean getter, setter, and toggle | | KDFConfigSelectDescription | Options, selected index, and index setter | | KDFConfigMultiSelectDescription | Per-option state, selected indices, and selection-count limits | | KDFConfigListDescription | Element access, add/set/remove operations, and list-count limits | All setters create a pending value. They return false with an error when the value is invalid or the field is read-only. Numeric setters clamp accepted values to the field's bounds.

sections.heading: Edit and apply values
sections.text: A custom settings screen normally follows this flow: Get Config Descriptions Flat (PackRef) -> For Each Description -> Read typed value and state -> Typed setter or Set Value -> Is Pack Config Dirty (PackRef) -> Apply Config Changes (PackRef) -> Inspect Config Apply Result Set Value accepts a complete FKDFConfigValue. Set Value From String parses one canonical scalar; for an array field it parses one element, so use Set Value to replace a complete array. Reset To Default and Reset Pack Config To Default stage default values. They do not write the file until Apply Config Changes runs. Discard Pending Change affects one description, while Discard Pending Config Changes discards a pack or every pack. Is Pack Config Dirty and Has Pending Config Changes are equivalent pack-level checks.

sections.heading: Interpret the apply result
sections.text: Apply Config Changes saves pending values that the caller may edit. Hot changes request a KDataForge reload. Cold changes remain saved and report that a restart is required. | Result field | Meaning | | bSaved | At least one value was written to a configuration file. | | bReloaded | A KDataForge reload ran during this call. | | bReloadScheduled | A reload was queued because another reload or debounce window was active. | | bRestartRequired | At least one saved cold value needs a restart. | | bPending | A dedicated-server administrator request was sent and has not returned yet. | | mRequestId | Correlates an administrator request with its later result. Local results use 0. | | mChangedKeys | Saved field keys. | | mRestartRequiredKeys | Cold fields that need a restart. | | mRestartAdvisedKeys | Hot fields that also feed a cold context or property. They work live, but a restart is advised. | | mErrors | Save, validation, permission, or reload errors. | Is Config Restart Required checks whether a pack, or any pack for an empty ref, currently has a saved cold change that differs from its effective value.

sections.heading: Reload or adopt values
sections.text: Reload Config From Disk re-reads stored value files. It keeps unsaved pending edits and reloads KDataForge when a hot stored value differs from the effective value. It does not write a file. Adopt Host Values is a multiplayer-client action. It writes the current host values into the client's local configuration files. Use it when the player wants the next standalone session to start with the server's settings.

sections.heading: Resolve templates and expressions
sections.text: Resolve Template String and Resolve Template Text expand the same {prefix:body} tokens used by pack documents. Both functions run pre-pass providers first, followed by apply-time providers. Pass the pack ref so pack-local cfg: references resolve in the expected scope. OutError is empty on success and combines provider failures with template diagnostics otherwise. The returned text still contains the best result produced by the two passes, so check OutError before using it as a validated value. Evaluate Config Expression evaluates the expression grammar used by conditions.config. The function return value reports whether parsing and evaluation succeeded. bOutResult contains the expression result only on success; OutError explains a parse or evaluation failure. See Templates and typed references and Configuration expressions for supported operands and prefixes.

sections.heading: Multiplayer roles and permissions
sections.text: Get Config Net Role returns one of these roles: | Role | Behavior | | Local | Standalone game. Edits write local files. | | ListenHost | Listen-server host. Edits write host files and synchronize effective values to clients. | | DedicatedServer | Server process. Files and server commands control values. | | RemoteClient | Client sees synchronized host values and cannot edit server configuration. | | RemoteAdmin | Authenticated dedicated-server administrator. Apply sends changes through a server RPC. | Use Can Local Player Edit Config before enabling controls. UKDFConfigDescription.Is Read Only uses the same permission state for one field. The server accepts configuration writes from the listen host and authenticated dedicated-server administrators. A plain remote client is read-only. The administrator RPC accepts at most 512 changes. Keys are limited to 256 characters. Each value can carry at most 64 elements, with at most 4,096 characters per element. The RPC validation rejects larger payloads before the permission and field checks run. The server replicates effective values, not pack files. A hot difference schedules a debounced reload on the client. A cold difference sets host-mismatch state and raises the mismatch event once per field and join. Synchronized values remain in memory and do not overwrite a client's local file unless the player calls Adopt Host Values. A synchronized value may contain at most 64 elements and 1,024 characters per element. The server skips an oversized field and logs a warning; clients keep their local value for that key. These replication limits are narrower than the administrator write-RPC limit.

sections.heading: Dedicated-server administrator results
sections.text: Apply Config Changes returns immediately for a remote administrator. That first result has bPending: true and a nonzero request id. The server validates permissions and values, saves the accepted changes, and reloads for hot fields. The final FKDFConfigApplyResult arrives through UKDFSubsystem.mOnConfigApplied with the same request id. Keep the Apply button in a pending state until the matching event arrives. Handle errors from the final result instead of treating the initial pending result as success.

sections.heading: Observe changes
sections.text: Bind these Blueprint events on UKDFSubsystem: | Event | When it fires | | On Config Applied | Local apply completion and final dedicated-server administrator response. Carries FKDFConfigApplyResult. | | On Pack Config Changed | A pack's values or state changed, including pending edits. Carries pack ref and dirty state. Load-time events are coalesced per pack. | | On Config Host Mismatch | A cold host value differs from the value this client loaded with. Fires once per key and join. | | On Reload Completed | A KDataForge reload finished. | Each description also exposes On Value Changed and On State Changed. KDataForge queues events while a load runs and broadcasts them afterward, so UI callbacks never observe a half-rebuilt registry.

sections.heading: Verify a custom screen
sections.text: 1. Query one pack and confirm its state, field count, and icon fallback. 2. Build rows from Get Config Descriptions Flat and reject stale descriptions. 3. Test one valid and one invalid setter. Display the returned error. 4. Stage a value, discard it, stage it again, and apply it. 5. Check hot, cold, restart-advised, and queued-reload results separately. 6. Join a listen server as a normal client and confirm the fields are read-only. 7. Test the administrator path on a dedicated server and match the final event by request id. 8. Leave the server and confirm local values return after host synchronization ends. For YAML field definitions and ready-made widgets, see Pack configuration. For the player-facing settings and multiplayer workflow, see Settings and multiplayer.

pages.title: Configuration expressions
pages.description: Syntax, operands, evaluation, and diagnostics for `config:` conditions.

sections.heading: Configuration expressions
sections.text: conditions.config tests pack settings and selected game settings. It accepts one expression string or a list in which all expressions must pass. The field works in pack.yml, documents, and list-entry conditions; it is not part of a type: config field definition.

sections.heading: Example
sections.text: type: cdo conditions: config: features.enableBonus && balance.ironSpeed >= 2 patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.9 Each expression in a config: list must pass: conditions: config: - features.enableBonus - balance.ironSpeed >= 2

sections.heading: Operands
sections.text: | Form | Value | | balance.ironSpeed | Field from this pack's configuration | | cfg:balance.ironSpeed | Same-pack field, with explicit prefix | | cfg:OtherPack:shared.level | Field from another pack | | session:Setting.Id | SML session setting | | ags:Setting.Id | Advanced game setting | | option:Setting.Id | Local game option | Configuration ids use dot-separated segments matching [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*. External pack references use letters, digits, _, ., and -. Settings ids are listed in a reflection export's settings index. Session and advanced game settings may be unavailable until a save is loaded.

sections.heading: Syntax and precedence
sections.text: or := and (|| and)* and := compare (&& compare)* compare := unary [comparison unary] # at most one comparison unary := ! unary | primary primary := (or) | [literal, ...] | literal | operand ! binds most tightly, followed by comparisons, &&, then ||. Parentheses change grouping. Comparisons are non-associative: write a < b && b < c, not a < b < c. Literals are true, false, signed decimal numbers, and single- or double-quoted strings. Lists contain literals only and must use one value type. Reserved words true, false, in, and contains cannot be bare configuration ids. Quote the whole YAML expression when it starts with !, since YAML otherwise reads it as a tag.

sections.heading: Operators
sections.text: | Operator | Meaning | | !value | Logical negation | | left && right | Both expressions must pass; short-circuits | | left || right | Either expression may pass; short-circuits | | ==, != | Compare same-typed numbers, strings, or booleans; lists cannot be compared | | <, <=, >, >= | Numeric comparisons | | list contains value | True when list contains value of matching type | | value in list | Same membership check with operands reversed | An expression used alone is converted to a condition: booleans keep their value, zero and empty strings/lists are false, and nonzero numbers and nonempty strings/lists are true. contains and in compare list elements by value.

sections.heading: Evaluation and diagnostics
sections.text: Inside each condition object, config: list entries are AND-combined with the object's other condition keys. conditionBehaivor combines condition objects and defaults to AND; OR allows any object to pass. ifNotMatch: true negates its condition object after evaluation. Expressions are evaluated before references and templates are expanded. cfg:, session:, ags:, and option: are expression operands here; {cfg:...} templates are not expanded inside conditions and are treated literally. Unknown ids, malformed syntax, and type mismatches produce diagnostics and make that condition object fail. A hot configuration field read by a load-time condition produces a warning because changing it requires the condition to be evaluated again.

pages.title: UE Editor integration
pages.description: Applying YAML cdo patches directly onto assets inside the Unreal Editor with KDF.ApplyToAssets, turning runtime patches into permanent asset edits (WITH_EDITOR builds only).

sections.heading: UE Editor integration
sections.text: Mod developers can apply YAML packs directly to Unreal Editor assets, then save those assets to make the changes permanent. For authoring YAML in the standalone desktop application, see VS Code Extension & LSP. > Editor builds only (WITH_EDITOR). None of this exists in the packaged game or on dedicated > servers. Players keep the runtime pipeline.

sections.heading: `KDF.ApplyToAssets [PathFilter]`
sections.text: KDF.ApplyToAssets is a console command available only in editor builds. Run it with no arguments to sweep every scanned pack, or pass a path prefix to restrict the sweep to one branch of the content tree: KDF.ApplyToAssets KDF.ApplyToAssets /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes It only touches documents that explicitly set type: cdo. It uses the same property-path parser and reflection operation engine (FKDFOpEngine::ApplyOp) as runtime, pointed at editor objects. Other document types (item, recipe, asset, …) are runtime concepts, and this command skips them. For each cdo patch, the optional PathFilter restricts application to targets whose path starts with the filter. For example, /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes applies only recipe patches and leaves everything else untouched. The target field resolves the same way it does elsewhere in cdo patches: a class path resolves to that class's CDO, and anything else is loaded as an object path. An invalid target: shape or a list containing an empty or non-scalar member skips the entire patch before any target is modified. The warning names the file and source line. Correct the target list and run the command again; valid targets in that same malformed list are not applied. Every modified package is marked dirty. For a Blueprint CDO, that is the generated class's outer package, so the standard editor save flow (Save All or source-control checkout) persists the changes. Your YAML pack has effectively become a set of permanent asset edits. Afterwards, a summary line is logged with the number of ops applied, assets touched, and packages marked dirty. :::caution This command is a narrow importer, not the runtime document dispatcher. It reads explicit target: paths and properties: only. It does not expand allAssetsOfClass or matchTag, and it does not reproduce applyToSubclasses, applyToSpawnedActors, actorAction, inventoryRemap, or deferOneGameTick. Document conditions and include: ordering are also not evaluated here. Write editor-import patches with explicit targets and review the dirty packages before saving. :::

sections.heading: Configuration and template pre-pass
sections.text: Before applying each file's cdo documents, the command loads pack configuration into a transient registry with file writes disabled. It runs the template pre-pass for typed references, pre-pass string tokens, and list-entry conditions. This does not make the command equivalent to the runtime dispatcher: top-level document conditions and runtime ordering remain outside this importer. World-dependent reads such as session: and ags: cannot resolve without a running world. Documents deferred for those reads are skipped with a warning. A list-entry condition evaluation error keeps the entry and emits a diagnostic, so inspect warnings and resulting assets before saving. The command never creates or rewrites player configuration value files.

sections.heading: In-game editor property categories
sections.text: The in-game /kdf editor groups reflected fields by their Unreal Category metadata. Categories are collapsed by default so large CDOs remain navigable. Reflected fields without CPF_Edit are placed in a separate Non-UPROPERTY / Internal category. Despite that UI label, they are still reflected FProperty fields; they lack the normal edit flag or category metadata. They remain available for inspection and editing through the same reflection operation pipeline. CDO exports include these non-edit reflected fields as well.

sections.heading: Runtime-only defer flag
sections.text: Set deferOneGameTick: true on a type: cdo patch when the base game initializes the target during startup and the patch must run after that initialization: type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Some/Class.Some_C deferOneGameTick: true properties: SomeProperty: 123 KDataForge waits for the matching world to enter BeginPlay, then applies the patch on the following game tick. The flag is deliberately a one-tick startup delay, not a general timer. KDF.ApplyToAssets ignores this flag and applies explicit targets immediately.

sections.heading: When to use which pipeline
sections.text: Both pipelines share the same operation engine and property-path resolution. Target discovery, conditions, timing, and runtime modifiers differ as described above: | | Runtime (players, packs) | Editor (KDF.ApplyToAssets) | | Changes live in | YAML, re-applied every session | The assets themselves, after saving | | Reversible | Usually on next session. resourcenode destruction can persist in saves; recipe removal self-heals on a later load without the pack | Via source control / not saving | | Audience | Players, pack authors | Mod developers cooking their own content | | Document types | All (item, recipe, asset, cdo, …) | Explicitly typed cdo with explicit target: only | | Diagnostics | debug: / KDF.Debug plus /kdf report | Command warnings and one summary log; no runtime patch report | See Resource Node removal before treating runtime YAML as reversible. Vanilla can retain destruction tombstones after that pack is removed.

sections.heading: Still open
sections.text: Asset/image import into the editor (bringing type: asset files in as real texture assets) and editor-side UI polish (search/filter/sort over patchable assets) are not implemented yet. Do not confuse this with the in-game editor (/kdf editor, opened from chat while playing). That is a separate, runtime-only tool for browsing and editing content live in a running session.

pages.title: Handler template
pages.description: Reference C++ implementation for creating a new document handler (worked RecipeHandler example).

sections.heading: Handler template
sections.text: A handler owns one YAML root type and runs in one fixed EKDFStage. It receives parsed FKDFNode documents and never sees raw YAML text directly. Third-party mods use handlers to give a new root type KDataForge validation, dry-run previews, diagnostics, and patch records. Every handler normally derives from UKDFHandlerBase, which lives in the KDataForgeApi module. Registration uses UKDFSubsystem from the main KDataForge module, so the registering mod links both. See Module Structure for why that module boundary exists and what else lives on either side of it. See API Design for the rest of the public contract surface.

sections.heading: Minimal skeleton
sections.text: A handler is normally two files: a header declaring the UCLASS and overrides, and a .cpp implementing them. The example below is a UMyRecipeHandler that owns a type: recipe document containing a recipes sequence. Start with the header: // MyRecipeHandler.h #pragma once #include "CoreMinimal.h" #include "KDFHandlerBase.h" #include "MyRecipeHandler.generated.h" UCLASS() class MYMOD_API UMyRecipeHandler : public UKDFHandlerBase { GENERATED_BODY() public: UMyRecipeHandler(); virtual bool ValidateDocument(const FKDFNode& Document, FKDFValidationContext& Context) override; virtual bool ApplyDocument(const FKDFNode& Document, FKDFApplyContext& Context) override; }; The constructor sets the three identity fields that UKDFHandlerBase exposes: mRootType, mStage, and mPriority. ValidateDocument does cheap structural checks before anything is written, and ApplyDocument does the actual work. Only ApplyDocument is mandatory. UKDFHandlerBase's default ValidateDocument returns true: // MyRecipeHandler.cpp #include "MyRecipeHandler.h" UMyRecipeHandler::UMyRecipeHandler() { mRootType = TEXT("recipe"); // matches `type: recipe` documents mStage = EKDFStage::Recipes; // fixed stage never reordered by priority mPriority = 0; // tie-break within (stage, root type); higher runs earlier } bool UMyRecipeHandler::ValidateDocument(const FKDFNode& Document, FKDFValidationContext& Context) { if (Document.Find(TEXT("recipes")) == nullptr) { Context.AddError(TEXT("recipe document requires a 'recipes' sequence")); return false; // skips ApplyDocument; never halts the load } return true; } bool UMyRecipeHandler::ApplyDocument(const FKDFNode& Document, FKDFApplyContext& Context) { const FKDFNode* Recipes = Document.Find(TEXT("recipes")); for (const TSharedRef<FKDFNode>& Recipe : Recipes->Sequence) { const FString Id = Recipe->GetString(TEXT("id"), FString()); if (Id.IsEmpty()) { Context.AddError(TEXT("recipe entry needs an 'id'"), Recipe->Line); continue; // per-entry problems are diagnostics, keep going } if (Context.bDryRun) { continue; // resolve/validate only no writes } // … create/modify the recipe class, write properties via FKDFOpEngine/FKDFValueCodec … ++Context.mAppliedOpCount; if (Context.mPatchRecord != nullptr) { FKDFOpRecord& Op = Context.mPatchRecord->mOps.AddDefaulted_GetRef(); Op.mTargetObjectPath = /* target path */ Id; Op.mOp = EKDFOp::Set; } } return Context.mAppliedOpCount > 0; } Stage order is fixed and shared across every handler, whether built-in or third-party. See Architecture for the full GameTags → Assets → Localization → CDOChanges → Items → Recipes → Buildings → … pipeline that your mStage slots into. mPriority only breaks ties between multiple handlers that share the same (stage, root type) pair. It never lets a handler jump into a different stage.

sections.heading: Registration (your mod's game instance module)
sections.text: A handler object is useless until KDataForge knows about it. Registration has a hard timing requirement: it must happen during the CONSTRUCTION lifecycle phase, because KDataForge's own RunInitialLoad() (scan, parse, validate, apply) runs at the later INITIALIZATION phase. Late registration misses the initial pass. Matching documents can run on a later /kdf reload, but cold registrations may still need the next session. Register from your own game-instance module's lifecycle dispatch: #include "Module/GameInstanceModuleManager.h" #include "Subsystems/KDFSubsystem.h" void UMyModGameInstanceModule::DispatchLifecycleEvent(ELifecyclePhase Phase) { Super::DispatchLifecycleEvent(Phase); if (Phase == ELifecyclePhase::CONSTRUCTION) // MUST be CONSTRUCTION — { // KDataForge applies at INITIALIZATION UGameInstanceModuleManager* Modules = GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UGameInstanceModuleManager>(); if (Modules != nullptr) { Modules->EnsureSubsystemInitialized(UKDFSubsystem::StaticClass()); if (UKDFSubsystem* KDF = UKDFSubsystem::Get(GetGameInstance())) { KDF->RegisterHandler(NewObject<UMyRecipeHandler>(KDF)); } } } } Add KDataForgeApi and KDataForge to your module dependencies. The explicit initialization is required because SML may dispatch lifecycle phases before custom GameInstance subsystems exist.

sections.heading: Contract checklist
sections.text: UKDFHandlerBase is forgiving about what you override, but diagnostics, dry-run preview, reports, and editor history depend on a few contracts. Run through these before shipping a handler: - [ ] mRootType is lowercase and unique to your mod, or intentionally shared: all handlers for a type run, priority-ordered. - [ ] Report diagnostics via Context.AddError/AddWarning/AddInfo. Never halt, and never call check() on user data. - [ ] Honor Context.bDryRun: resolve and validate, but do not write. - [ ] Record ops into Context.mPatchRecord. Reporting and editor history depend on it. - [ ] If you write CDO properties yourself, snapshot originals first via UKDFSubsystem::GetVanillaCache().RecordSnapshot(...) and retain patched objects via RetainObject(...). - [ ] Optional overrides are ExportObject for editor export and GetEditorPanelClass for a custom editor panel. The current interface has no RevertDocument hook.

pages.title: Mod unlock classes
pages.description: Every mod FGUnlock subclass, with abstract state, Blueprint path, exact field types, accepted values, nested structs, examples, and caveats.

sections.heading: Mod unlock classes
sections.text: KDataForge handles mod unlocks in schematic and delivery-task unlocks: lists like base-game classes. It resolves class:, creates the object on the schematic CDO with NewObject, applies properties:, and appends it to mUnlocks. Mod-provided classes need no special handling. Known native paths with Blueprint variants automatically remap; exact Blueprint paths also work. Catalog reflects mods loaded during Unreal scan. Use these in a schematic's instanced unlocks list or in a standalone type: unlock document. For base-game classes see Base-Game Unlock Classes. :::caution These classes exist only when provider mod is installed. Gate optional integrations with a hasMod condition; otherwise unresolved class is reported by /kdf report and skipped. :::

sections.heading: Deprecated KLib unlocks
sections.text: KLNetworkLevelUnlock carries no data of its own and only forces a Faxit tier recompute; use the KPCLFaxit*Unlock classes below instead. KLUnlockExtractorScanner is superseded by the base-game FGUnlockScannableResource. Both still exist because shipped schematic assets instance them, so do not use either in a new pack.

pages.title: Reflection Export
pages.description: Export runtime Unreal classes, structs, enums, defaults, functions, game settings, reload classification, Blueprint mappings, and asset indexes for KDataForge Tools and validation use.

sections.heading: Reflection Export
sections.text: KDataForge exports every reflected type loaded by the running game. The export also includes Blueprint-generated classes and the user-defined structs and enums found through the Asset Registry. The exporter works on the game thread in bounded slices and writes JSON in the background.

sections.heading: Run
sections.text: Wait until world begins play, then use console: KDF.DumpReflection Or chat: /kdf-reflection The two commands do not export the same amount: | Start | Options it uses | Result | | Console KDF.DumpReflection (bare) | none | Classes, structs, enums, defaults, Blueprint mappings, textures, the settings index and the cold-property catalog in the final ZIP. No functions, no data-asset or curve indexes and no flattened classes. | | Chat /kdf-reflection (bare) | --assets --functions --flattened --pack --image-max-dimension=1024 | The full profile: everything above plus functions, asset indexes and flattened classes. | | Launch argument -KDFReflectionAutoExport=<dir> | --assets --functions --flattened (and --image-max-dimension from -KDFReflectionAutoImageMaxDimension=<n> if given) | The same export, started automatically once a world has begun play. | For the data KDataForge Tools needs (function completion in templates, asset-by-class indexes, inherited properties) use the bare chat command, the auto export, or give the console command the options yourself: KDF.DumpReflection --assets --functions --flattened. The chat defaults apply only when you give no option at all; as soon as you pass one, exactly the options you passed are used. For KDataForgeJS projects, kdf game-data owns this lifecycle. It discovers a compatible Windows or Linux install, loads the newest local save, launches with -KDFReflectionAutoExport=<temporary-directory> -KDFReflectionAutoExit, waits for atomic publication, and imports the archive and generated declarations into the current project. -KDFReflectionAutoExit requests a clean game exit after the automatic export finishes; it has no effect on manual exports. The game emits typescript/kdataforgejs/kdataforge.generated.d.ts inside the temporary export. The CLI organizes that file under DataForge/typescript/kdataforgejs/: index.d.ts references runtime declarations, globals, alphabetic satisfactory/ groups, and Unreal-path paths/ groups. Pack authors use index.d.ts and do not edit generated files. Clients do nothing unless --force is supplied. Server or host is normal export location. Default directory is FactoryGame/KMods/ReflectionExport/. | Option | Meaning | | --out <dir> | Override output directory. | | --mounts /Game,/Plugin | Restrict Blueprint discovery to comma-separated mount points. | | --assets | Add asset-by-class indexes beyond textures; loading attempts still cover every selected registry asset. | | --asset-cap N | Limit assets recorded per class. | | --functions | Include reflected function signatures and flags (see Functions). | | --flattened | Write inherited-property view to classes.flat.ndjson. | | --image-max-dimension N | Largest exported texture side in pixels, 1 to 4096; default 1024. | | --used-textures[=true|false] | Select textures referenced by reflected non-widget class defaults; enabled by default. false selects all supported, portable texture candidates. | | --pack | Compatibility no-op; final ZIP is always written. | | --skip-widgets | Skip widget Blueprints; this is the default when omitted. | | --skip-widgets=true | Skip widget Blueprints, same as --skip-widgets. | | --skip-widgets=false | Include widget Blueprints, same as --widgets. | | --widgets | Shortcut that includes widget Blueprints. | | --budget-ms N | Game-thread budget per tick; default 8. | | --batch-size N | Blueprint load batch size; garbage collection runs between batches. | | --families name:path,... | Extend linter catalog families. | | --force | Allow local client export. | Progress appears in chat and LogKDFReflection. Run KDF.ValidateReflection [--out <dir>] after completion for runtime acceptance checks. Use the Python artifact validator for ZIP integrity, file parity, images, and schema validation; see Validation.

sections.heading: Output
sections.text: - manifest.json: runtime engine/build, platform, options, installed mods, counts, and failed loads. - classes.ndjson, structs.ndjson, enums.ndjson: path-sorted records with inline property data. - classes.flat.ndjson: optional inherited-property view. - indexes/subclasses.json, indexes/assets.json: class and registry lookup indexes. - indexes/settings.json: game settings that session:, ags: and option: references can read, see Settings index. - catalog/cold_properties.json: the cold-property catalog, see Reload classification. - indexes/textures.json: image path, format, dimensions, export method, or per-texture failure reason. - images/**: selected texture images as PNG, proportionally limited to the configured --image-max-dimension cap (default 1024 pixels per side). - nativeMapping.json: native-to-Blueprint and reverse mappings. - catalog/instanced_classes.json: linter family catalog. - schema/reflection.schema.json: draft 2020-12 schema. - <ISO-date>.kdfdata: mandatory ZIP bundle containing every output file. By default, texture selection recursively scans reflected non-widget class defaults. This retains descriptor, item, recipe, and schematic icons while excluding material-only maps, widget-only decoration, unreferenced helper textures, dynamic render/media textures, and transient runtime textures without a portable asset identity. Selected textures remain uncapped and appear in indexes/textures.json with Asset Registry tags, source and exported dimensions, resize state, image path, or explicit failure details. Every successful image is PNG. Cooked BC/BC7 data is decoded before writing; GPU readback supplies pixels when cooked CPU data is unavailable. Images exceeding the configured cap are proportionally downscaled or use a suitable cooked mip. The cap does not upscale images. Missing or unreadable higher mips can produce smaller output even when the source fits within the cap. Source/exported dimensions and resized record the result. Cooked-decode and GPU-readback fallbacks warn when using a lower mip than requested; the raw platformMipPng path does not. Unavailable textures remain indexed but produce no placeholder image. Each encoded PNG is limited to 4 MiB (4,194,304 bytes). Larger previews are not written; their texture metadata remains indexed with status: error, errorCode: encodedImageTooLarge, and an increased image error count. Reduce --image-max-dimension and rerun the export to retry. With --used-textures=false, selection expands to all supported, portable texture candidates, including candidates not referenced by those defaults. The manifest's options.usedTexturesOnly records that choice: true pairs with options.textureSelection: reflectedNonWidgetClassDefaults, and false with options.textureSelection: allPortableTextures. options.imageMaxDimension records the actual image cap; consumers should read it instead of assuming every export uses 1024. Current exports containing options.imageMaxDimension must include both options.usedTexturesOnly and options.textureSelection with the consistent pairing above. If either selection field is present, its partner is required too. Legacy schemaVersion: 1 exports may omit all three fields. Exporter attempts to load every previously unloaded registry asset under configured mounts with quiet/no-warn flags and bounded batches. Failed loads remain in manifest. Garbage collection runs through engine safe points, never directly from ticker-time export code. --assets adds indexes for data assets, curves, and other classes referenced by object properties; --asset-cap applies only to non-texture index classes, not loading coverage. Native constructors sometimes generate a fresh GUID, current timestamp, seed, transient object name, or uninitialized byte sequence. Exporter detects volatile reflected types and values, emits reflected zero value, and writes defaultVolatile: true. Result stays valid ImportText input and deterministic. Stable constructor defaults remain unchanged. Blueprint-authored member names are emitted lowercase because Unreal's case-preserving FName display casing depends on asset load order. Lookup remains case-insensitive. To import, run KDataForge: Switch datapack in VS Code, select generated .kdfdata, then bind the imported datapack to the project. KDataForge Tools validates manifest/schema, stores immutable archive copy, and exposes contents as datapack reflection section to editor and language server. See VS Code Extension & LSP for project binding, reflection requirements, and schema-only validation. Directory form is useful during editor/language-server development. Desktop import finds reflection data by manifest.json at the archive root, under reflection/, or under kdf/reflection/. These prefixes are case-sensitive. Exactly one supported location may contain a manifest, and classes.ndjson must be a file under that same prefix; class records at another prefix cannot fill the gap. Multiple supported reflection manifests are rejected.

sections.heading: Runtime export publication and recovery
sections.text: The runtime exporter first writes loose files and the ZIP into a sibling directory named .<output-name>.kdf-export-<id>.stage. Preparation failures leave existing output files unchanged. Publication then replaces generated files individually, retiring obsolete generated files and publishing the new .kdfdata archive last. Do not read, import, edit, or start another export into that destination until completion. The whole directory is not replaced atomically. Before publication, the exporter preserves affected existing files under .<output-name>.kdf-export-<id>.stage.backup/previous/. Its recovery.json records the absolute destination, new archive filename, previousFiles, newFiles, and newDirectories. Paths in these three lists are relative to destination. A publication error attempts rollback and reports whether it completed; the recovery directory remains available even after a completed rollback. After every new file, including the archive, has been published, the exporter writes a sibling .<output-name>.kdf-export-<id>.stage.backup.committed file containing the same journal. It removes that marker only after removing the backup directory. A retained marker therefore records completed publication, possibly with interrupted cleanup; it does not prove artifact validity or that every backup file remains available. If writing the marker fails, publication can still succeed with a warning and retained recovery directory. An absent marker does not prove that publication failed. A process crash can interrupt publication or rollback. There is no automatic restart recovery. If output is incomplete or its state is uncertain: 1. Stop the exporting game process and any other writer to that destination. Copy the destination, matching staging directory, recovery directory, and commit marker, if present, to a safe location. Keep these copies unchanged until recovery is verified. 2. Inspect the journal and logs to identify the transaction and its exact destination. Confirm that every listed relative path stays inside that destination and that no affected path traverses a symlink, junction, reparse point, or nested mount. Do not combine journals from different exports. 3. If a commit marker exists, validate the published output first (see Validation). A valid completed export needs cleanup only. Without a marker, also check logs and validate before deciding to roll back: the marker write itself may have failed after successful publication. 4. To restore the previous files, first check that every previousFiles entry exists under backup/previous/. If any is missing, stop; interrupted cleanup may have removed part of the backup. Recover from the safe copies or another known-good export instead of using a partial backup. 5. Remove only the destination files listed in newFiles, if present. Remove only empty directories listed in newDirectories, deepest first; preserve directories containing other files. Copy each previousFiles entry from backup/previous/ back to the same relative destination path, creating parent directories as needed and overwriting the affected file. Restore any previous .kdfdata archive last. Copy, rather than move, so recovery sources stay intact. 6. Check restored files against the saved previous/ bytes and verify that newFiles are absent. Validate a restored complete export with both validators below. If no previous complete export existed, verify the restored prior state and generate a fresh export into a new empty directory. Retain the journals, staging files, backup, marker, and safe copies until these checks succeed. These names belong to runtime export. The metadata-merge commandlet uses separate .<output-name>.kdf-merge-<id>.stage and .backup sibling directories and directory-move recovery, explained under Editor Metadata Supplement. Do not apply runtime recovery.json steps to a metadata-merge backup.

sections.heading: Functions
sections.text: With --functions (included in the chat default and the auto export) each class record in classes.ndjson gets a functions array. KDataForge Tools uses it to complete and check template function calls. | Field | Meaning | | name | The function name, lowercased so exports of different runs compare equal | | authoredName | The name with its authored letter case (GetItemName). Editors show this one. | | path | <ownerPath>:<name> | | ownerPath | The class that declares the function | | flags | The function flags, for example native, BlueprintPure, Const, Static, net and event flags | | params | Input parameters as property records, in declaration order | | return | The return value as a property record; absent when the function returns nothing | Property records use the same shape as class properties, including authoredName.

sections.heading: Integer bitmask metadata
sections.text: For integer properties with Bitmask and BitmaskEnum metadata, the exporter resolves only already-loaded enums. A full enum path must identify a loaded enum; a short name must uniquely match one. A resolved enum supplies its path, named options, and bitflags metadata. Plain integer bitmask properties also advertise bitmask operations and the named kdf.valueForm. A resolved enum with Bitflags metadata supplies bitmaskMode on both integer-bitmask and enum-backed property records: maskValues when UseEnumValuesAsMaskValuesInEditor metadata is present, and bitIndices otherwise. Consumers use that mode and exact option values to derive declared bits. Enum-backed properties keep enum import syntax; they do not get the pipe/sequence flag syntax or bitmask mutation operations used by plain integer BitmaskEnum properties. Without bitmaskMode, enum-backed properties use exact enum membership when complete option values are available. For plain integer bitmasks, an absent mode limits editor checks; runtime still requires a valid enum result and a value that fits the property. Missing metadata, an unloaded enum, or an ambiguous short name keeps the numeric fallback. Export does not load an enum merely to resolve this metadata. Runtime support requires WITH_METADATA and retained metadata; exported hints do not restore stripped runtime metadata. These hints describe available editor choices. Runtime value conversion still follows Property Types, including its mask-value, bit-index, and numeric forms.

sections.heading: Settings index
sections.text: indexes/settings.json lists the game settings that session:, ags: and option: references can read. It is written by every export. | Field | Meaning | | schemaVersion, engineVersion | Format and build | | counts | Number of settings per provider: session, ags, option, other | | settings | The records, sorted by provider, lowercase id and path | | unresolved | Setting assets that could not be indexed, with a reason (for example an empty id) | A record has: | Field | Meaning | | id | The setting id (StrId), exactly what follows the prefix in ags:<id> | | provider | session (SML session setting), ags (advanced game settings), option (local game options) or other (not readable by a prefix) | | path, class, source | The asset, its class, and which mod or the base game provides it | | displayName, tooltip | The texts shown in game | | valueType | bool, int, float, string, color or other | | default | The default value when it can be read | | range, displayRange | Slider or selection bounds; displayRange only when it differs | | options | Choices with value and label for an integer selector | | placements | Options-menu locations. Each entry contains category, optional subcategory and row priority; categories include class, display name and menu priority. | | sessionWide, dedicatedServerRelevant | Whether the setting is stored per session and whether a dedicated server uses it | | managerClass, mapWhitelist | The manager that owns the setting and, for session settings, the maps it is limited to | Active runtime-generated KDataForge sound sliders are included as option records with stable virtual paths and their Options → Audio placement. Dedicated servers do not create local Audio settings, so their exports omit these runtime-only records. The editor completes setting ids from this file and reports an unknown id as setting.unknown-id when the file exists.

sections.heading: Reload classification and cold-property catalog
sections.text: Every property declared directly by a class carries two extra fields under its kdf object: | Field | Meaning | | kdf.reload | hot, cold or newActors | | kdf.reloadReason | One sentence that says why, present when the classification comes from the catalog | - hot: a write applies live (an explicit allow-list entry). - cold: the game reads the property once or only when an object is created, so a live write does not change existing state. - newActors: the class default belongs to an actor or component, so only newly spawned actors see a write (the patch can set applyToSpawnedActors: true to include existing actors). Struct members, function parameters and container elements inherit the classification of the class property that contains them. The editor shows the classification next to path: completions and reports operations on cold or newActors properties as property.cold, see Reload classification. catalog/cold_properties.json is the catalog behind it: version, a description, and entries containing class, property, reload, reason, and verified. A class entry includes its subclasses and the property name is case-insensitive. verified: false marks an entry that is a reasonable assumption not yet checked in game.

sections.heading: Editor metadata supplement
sections.text: Packaged game may have WITH_METADATA disabled. Runtime records then contain metadataAvailable: false; export still succeeds. Generate metadata in modding editor: UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe FactoryGame.uproject -run=KDFReflectionMetaExport -out=C:\Temp\KDFMeta Merge supplement into separate copy with same native commandlet: UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe FactoryGame.uproject -run=KDFReflectionMetaExport ` -runtime=C:\Path\ReflectionExport ` -supplement=C:\Temp\KDFMeta\metadata.supplement.json ` -out=C:\Path\ReflectionMerged Merge records editor and game build per field and rebuilds mandatory ISO-named .kdfdata ZIP. The -runtime and -out directories must not overlap: they cannot be equal, and neither may contain the other. The -supplement file must be outside the -out directory, especially when using -force, which replaces an existing merge output directory. These path checks also apply without -force. On Windows and Linux, checks compare normalized paths and resolved physical paths, so symlink or junction aliases cannot bypass either restriction. Subsequent merge reads and writes use those resolved paths. The runtime directory and supplement file must exist. A new output path may have missing parent directories: the commandlet resolves its nearest existing directory ancestor and appends the missing components. Empty, inaccessible, dangling, or otherwise unresolvable paths are rejected before an existing output is replaced. Unsupported platforms reject the merge. The commandlet prepares a complete merged export and .kdfdata archive in a uniquely named sibling directory before replacing -out. Copy, metadata parsing, manifest, or archive errors during preparation leave an existing output untouched. The runtime manifest's generatedAt must be nonempty and contain no path separators because it supplies the archive filename. Keep the input and output directories unchanged until the commandlet finishes; do not run concurrent merges into the same output. With -force, the previous output moves to a uniquely named sibling backup before the prepared export moves into place. If publication fails, the commandlet tries to restore the backup. If restoration also fails, the error reports the backup path containing the previous output. Resolve any conflicting entry at -out, then move that backup directory back to -out. A successful merge removes its backup; a cleanup warning reports any backup retained for manual removal. Preparation failures also attempt to remove their staging directory and report its path if cleanup fails. These directory moves require same-filesystem rename support without replacing an existing entry. Linux requires renameat2 with RENAME_NOREPLACE; unsupported kernels or filesystems reject publication. Replacement uses two directory moves, so an interrupted process can leave -out absent with the previous export in a sibling .<output-name>.kdf-merge-<id>.backup directory. Inspect any matching .stage and .backup directories before recovering or deleting them; staging directories may contain incomplete exports. Before -force replaces an existing output directory, the commandlet inspects its contents without following link targets. Any nested symlink or Windows reparse point blocks replacement, even if its target is unrelated to the inputs. On Linux, mount points also block replacement, including bind mounts on the same filesystem and an output directory that is itself a mount point. The resolved output target must share its parent's mount ID, and every nested entry must share that same mount ID. Mount IDs must be readable through /proc/self/fdinfo; if they cannot be verified, replacement is rejected. Unreadable entries, failed directory enumeration, or more than 1,000,000 entries also block replacement. Unmount mounted entries, remove other blocked entries, or choose a new output directory, then retry. No Python merge script is packaged into mod or archive.

sections.heading: Validation
sections.text: Run both validators after export completes: | Validator | Checks | | In-game KDF.ValidateReflection [--out <dir>] | Required live FactoryGame reflection shapes, authored user-struct member names, and sampled default ExportText/ImportText round trips (up to three per property kind). Checks required file presence, exactly one .kdfdata file, the FGUnlockRecipe Blueprint mapping, and basic settings, icon, and cold-property index structure when present. | | Python validate_reflection_export.py <directory> | Exported reflection contracts and records against the emitted draft 2020-12 schema; texture PNG integrity, dimensions, selection options, image/index consistency, and supported optional index/catalog checks. Requires exactly one ISO-named .kdfdata ZIP, sorted entries, valid ZIP CRCs, every generated file in the ZIP, and byte-for-byte agreement between each packed entry and its loose file. Unrelated regular custom files outside images/ may remain outside the archive. Also checks numeric integer schemaVersion: 1 and mirrors the editor's archive inspection gates: source archive at most 2 GiB, at most 20,000 entries, at most 4 GiB expanded, manifest.json at most 1 MiB, and each PNG within the 4 MiB preview limit. | ZIP entries and indexed image paths must use safe relative paths contained within the export directory; traversal paths are rejected. The Python validator rejects symlinks and Windows reparse points anywhere in the loose export tree, including unrelated custom entries. Regular custom files outside images/ remain permitted outside the generated archive. The Python validator checks PNG signatures, chunk boundaries and CRCs, and supported non-interlaced pixel layouts with valid bit-depth and color-type combinations. It requires a single first IHDR, valid PLTE placement and size when present, a palette before indexed image data, contiguous IDAT chunks, and an empty final IEND with no trailing bytes. It also checks the decoded byte count, complete compressed stream, and row filter values. Chunk types must contain four ASCII letters with an uppercase third letter. Unsupported critical chunks are rejected; unknown ancillary chunks remain permitted. Invalid structure is rejected even when CRCs and dimensions match. Native acceptance PASS does not verify ZIP contents, loose/packed parity, image integrity, or schema conformance. Use the Python artifact/package validator before distributing or importing an artifact. The editor can compact source archives larger than 512 MiB and rejects installed output that still exceeds its 512 MiB cache cap. Python PASS does not predict compacted-cache success or prove every extension import gate. Confirm acceptance through KDataForge: Switch datapack in VS Code. The Python validator reads an export directory containing loose files and its .kdfdata archive; a standalone archive must first be extracted into a directory alongside that archive. Install Python dependency and validate one export from the modding workspace: python -m pip install jsonschema python Mods/GameFeatures/KDataForge/Tools/validate_reflection_export.py ` C:\Path\ReflectionExport For deterministic comparison, validate both exports with --compare: python Mods/GameFeatures/KDataForge/Tools/validate_reflection_export.py ` C:\Path\ReflectionExport --compare C:\Path\SecondReflectionExport Comparison hashes loose file paths and contents with SHA-256, excluding .kdfdata archives. It canonicalizes manifest.json and omits only its generatedAt field; other loose files are hashed as bytes. Each export must pass artifact validation before hashes are compared.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: - Blueprint load failures remain in manifest.json.failedLoads with reason. - Dedicated-server cooks or unsupported GPU formats may expose no readable pixels. Such records contain failure details instead of image bytes. - Per-class cap applies to non-texture classes. - All-mount exports can be large, especially with functions, flattened records, assets, or widgets. - Tick budget is checked between reflected records and Blueprint loads. One synchronous Asset Registry query, Blueprint load, garbage collection, or unusually large type can exceed budget by its own execution time because Unreal does not expose resumable versions of those operations. - Output determinism assumes identical game build, mod set, options, and registered content.

pages.title: Template provider API
pages.description: Register a native provider for custom `{prefix:body}` values in KDataForge documents.

sections.heading: Template provider API
sections.text: Use IKDFTemplateProvider when a native mod needs to expose values through custom template tokens. For example, a provider registered as acme receives the body of {acme:rate} and returns a typed value or localized FText. Pack authors do not need this API for KDataForge's built-in cfg, setting, class, item, recipe, or asset providers. Their syntax is documented in Templates and typed references.

sections.heading: Module and header
sections.text: The provider contract and registry are in the public KDataForgeApi module: #include "KDFTemplateProvider.h" Add KDataForgeApi to the module that owns the provider. A provider that only returns values from its own mod does not need to link the main KDataForge module.

sections.heading: Provider contract
sections.text: Implement three methods: class IKDFTemplateProvider { public: virtual FName GetPrefix() const = 0; virtual EKDFTemplatePhase GetPhase() const = 0; virtual FKDFTemplateResult Resolve(const FKDFTemplateRequest& Request) = 0; }; GetPrefix() returns the token prefix without the colon. A valid prefix starts with an ASCII letter and continues with ASCII letters, digits, or _. GetPhase() assigns the provider to one expansion phase: | Phase | When it runs | Use it for | | PrePass | Before KDataForge validates and applies document stages | Configuration or environment values that can change the document data passed to a handler | | ApplyTime | When a reflected property operation expands its operands | Values that need the final target, world state, or current apply-time context | A token is visible only in its provider's phase. Third-party prefixes support braced {prefix:body} tokens. The unquoted forms such as cfg:id are built-in typed references, not a general extension mechanism for third-party providers. Resolve() always runs on the game thread. The request contains: | Member | Meaning | | mBody | Text after prefix:. Nested tokens have already been substituted. | | mPackRef | Pack that owns the document. Use it when names are scoped to a pack. | | mGameInstance | Current game instance. | | mWorld | Current world, or nullptr when the initial pre-pass runs before a world exists. | Tokens can nest up to four levels. KDataForge does not scan a provider's returned value for more tokens.

sections.heading: Result contract
sections.text: Set mStatus on every result: | Status | Meaning | Runtime behavior | | Resolved | The provider returned a value. | Expansion continues. | | Unavailable | The source cannot answer yet, commonly because no world or session settings exist. | A pre-pass document can be deferred until world values are available. | | NotFound | The requested target or member does not exist. | The token remains unresolved and KDataForge reports it. | | Error | The request is malformed or the provider failed. | The token remains unresolved and mError explains the failure. | Return typed data in mValue with FKDFConfigValue::MakeScalar or MakeArray. A whole apply-time token can keep that type when KDataForge converts it for a destination property. Inside surrounding text, KDataForge converts the value to canonical text and joins arrays with , . Return a localized result in mText and set bHasText = true when the namespace and key must be preserved. Do not set both forms unless callers can use either representation consistently. Set bWorldBound = true when the result depends on the current world or session. KDataForge records world-bound reads so it can re-evaluate affected data after those values change. An Unavailable result is tracked as world-bound even if the provider does not set the flag. Fill mError for Unavailable, NotFound, and Error. Without it, KDataForge can only report a generic message containing the unresolved token.

sections.heading: Minimal provider
sections.text: This apply-time provider exposes {acme:rate} as a float: #include "KDFTemplateProvider.h" class FAcmeTemplateProvider final : public IKDFTemplateProvider { public: virtual FName GetPrefix() const override { return TEXT("acme"); } virtual EKDFTemplatePhase GetPhase() const override { return EKDFTemplatePhase::ApplyTime; } virtual FKDFTemplateResult Resolve(const FKDFTemplateRequest& Request) override { FKDFTemplateResult Result; if (!Request.mBody.Equals(TEXT("rate"), ESearchCase::CaseSensitive)) { Result.mStatus = EKDFTemplateStatus::NotFound; Result.mError = FString::Printf(TEXT("Unknown acme value '%s'"), *Request.mBody); return Result; } Result.mStatus = EKDFTemplateStatus::Resolved; Result.mValue = FKDFConfigValue::MakeScalar(EKDFConfigValueType::Float, TEXT("1.25")); return Result; } }; A pack can use the result as a typed operation value: properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: divide value: '{acme:rate}' Surrounding text converts it to text: value: 'Acme rate: {acme:rate}'

sections.heading: Register the provider
sections.text: Register during module startup and unregister during shutdown. Prefer RegisterWithSpelling(). Unreal's global FName table preserves the case of the first spelling it saw, so GetPrefix().ToString() may not reproduce the spelling your provider declared. void FAcmeModule::StartupModule() { mTemplateProvider = MakeShared<FAcmeTemplateProvider>(); bTemplateProviderRegistered = FKDFTemplateProviderRegistry::RegisterWithSpelling( mTemplateProvider.ToSharedRef(), TEXT("acme")); } void FAcmeModule::ShutdownModule() { if (bTemplateProviderRegistered) { FKDFTemplateProviderRegistry::Unregister(TEXT("acme")); bTemplateProviderRegistered = false; } mTemplateProvider.Reset(); } Document prefixes are case-sensitive. With the registration above, {acme:rate} resolves and {Acme:rate} does not. RegisterWithSpelling() also checks that the supplied spelling matches GetPrefix() when case is ignored. The registry is process-wide and thread-safe. The first registration for a prefix wins. These built-in families stay reserved even when their providers are temporarily unregistered: cfg, session, ags, option, class, item, resource, building, recipe, schematic, research, category, dataasset, and asset. A third-party registration cannot take one of those names. Check the Boolean return value and leave another provider registered when your call fails. Register() remains available, but derives the document spelling from GetPrefix().ToString(). Use it only when the FName casing issue cannot affect the prefix.

sections.heading: Diagnostics and verification
sections.text: KDataForge reports an unavailable pre-pass value as an informational deferral. Other unresolved pre-pass tokens produce warnings. An apply-time failure rejects the affected expansion or property operation with the provider's error text. Verify a provider with one document that covers each supported body: 1. Register it before KDataForge loads packs. 2. Use the exact registered spelling in a braced token. 3. Run /kdf report and confirm the document applied without an unresolved-template diagnostic. 4. Enable debug: true on the document and confirm the target property received the expected typed value. 5. Test Unavailable before a world exists if the provider reads world state, then load a save and confirm the deferred document applies. 6. Test a missing body and a malformed body. Confirm they return NotFound and Error with useful messages. 7. Repeat the checks in a dedicated-server build when the provider can run on a server. For the rest of native setup, see Integrate KDataForge and API design.

pages.title: VS Code Extension & LSP
pages.description: Install KDataForge Tools for completion, diagnostics, linting, Codex and typed KDataForgeJS authoring.

sections.heading: VS Code Extension & LSP
sections.text: KDataForge Tools adds KDataForge authoring support to VS Code. Extension ID: kmods.kdataforge. It bundles the Rust language server, project linter, Codex class browser, KDataForgeJS declarations, snippets and Explorer actions. No separate editor application is needed.

sections.heading: Install
sections.text: Install KDataForge Tools from VS Code Marketplace after the first public release, or install a platform-specific .vsix produced by the release workflow. Windows x64 and Linux x64 packages carry matching native sidecars. Remote workspaces run those sidecars on the workspace host. The extension requires a trusted filesystem workspace. Virtual and untrusted workspaces cannot run the native validators or create project files.

sections.heading: YAML language support
sections.text: Open a KDataForge project or any workspace containing DataForge/pack.yml. The extension provides: - schema and semantic diagnostics; - context-sensitive completion and hover; - go to definition, references and rename; - file, pack and project lint commands; - Codex search and class-reference insertion; - context actions for new KDataForge documents. The language server and CLI linter share the same validation core. A successful schema check does not prove that runtime classes, assets or functions exist when reflection data is unavailable. For properties:, completion and hover understand both the ordered path/value list and the shorter mapping form. In a mapping, the property name is the key, a plain value performs set, and $op selects another operation. This also works in nested instanced-object properties: blocks: properties: mDisplayNameOverride: false mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.5 Start a mapping with the kdf-properties-map YAML snippet, insert one operation with kdf-property-op, or add a nested recipe unlock with kdf-unlock-recipe-map. With a matching reflection datapack, completion can suggest property names and value types. See YAML Schema for the exact syntax and the $op ambiguity rule.

sections.heading: Import and bind game data
