sections.text: 1. Start a Satisfactory world with KDataForge and the mods your pack targets. After the world begins play, run: KDF.DumpReflection --assets --functions --flattened 2. Find the ISO-named .kdfdata archive under FactoryGame/KMods/ReflectionExport/, or the chosen --out directory. See Reflection Export for options and validation. 3. Run KDataForge: Switch datapack from the Command Palette and select or import the archive. 4. Confirm the effective datapack before relying on reflected completion or Codex results. Use an export matching the game build and installed mods. Missing or failed export records remain unknown; they are not proof that game content does not exist.

sections.heading: Schema-only mode
sections.text: Without usable game data, YAML schema and project validation remain available. Schema-only mode cannot establish whether a reflected class, property, function or asset exists. Reflection-dependent results state that limitation instead of treating missing metadata as success. For complete reflection-aware support, export classes with --flattened, functions with --functions, and non-texture assets with --assets.

sections.heading: KDataForgeJS projects
sections.text: Right-click a folder in Explorer and choose KDataForgeJS: Create Project Here. Generated projects receive the SDK bundled with the extension immediately, so TypeScript completion works before npm install. Available authoring actions: - KDataForgeJS: Create Script creates a typed handler without replacing existing files. - KDataForgeJS: Refresh Built-in SDK refreshes only the extension-managed SDK package. - kdf-handler, kdf-meta and kdf-item insert typed snippets. - TypeScript hover and CodeLens explain capabilities, authority, lifecycle, quotas, and unknown policy facts without granting rights. - Content/class/file completion, guarded rename, verified reflection quick fixes, content forms, JSON/SARIF export, diagnostic explanations, and offline docs search are available from standard VS Code providers and the Command Palette. See KDataForgeJS Authoring in VS Code for limits and safe-refusal cases, and KDataForgeJS Runtime API for the runtime contracts shown by hover. Generated package.json files retain @sf-kmods/kdataforgejs and @sf-kmods/kdataforgejs-cli development dependencies. Install them when you need kdf check, kdf lint, kdf sync, kdf format or kdf validate outside VS Code.

sections.heading: Other LSP clients
sections.text: The kdf-language-server binary speaks LSP over stdio. A host can supply initializationOptions.kdf.datapackPath with a .kdfdata path; an empty string selects schema-only validation. The same setting is accepted through workspace/didChangeConfiguration. For applying YAML permanently to Unreal asset packages, see UE Editor Integration.

pages.title: YAML schema
pages.description: Complete grammar for packs, document types, property paths, all 25 operations, conditions, and includes.

sections.heading: YAML schema
sections.text: > This is the normative schema. Every construct is implemented and covered by an example in > Examples.

sections.heading: File discovery
sections.text: - Author root: <your-mod>/DataForge/. - Author glob: <your-mod>/DataForge/**/*.yml (and *.yaml). - Scanner root: the Unreal project directory, which is FactoryGame/ in a packaged game. - Up to six levels below the project root, a directory is a pack root when it is named DataForge, uses the legacy name data-editor, or directly contains pack.yml. Names are case-insensitive. Root discovery prunes Content, Saved, Intermediate, Binaries, DerivedDataCache, Plugins, Source, and Config. - Roots may nest. Each YAML file belongs only to its deepest enclosing root. - All *.yml / *.yaml files under a pack root are parsed as documents. A file normally holds one document, but may hold several separated by --- lines. See Multiple Documents Per File below. - Malformed YAML produces an Error and that file is skipped. The rest of the load continues.

sections.heading: Pack manifest (`pack.yml`)
sections.text: Optional, at the pack root. Files without a manifest form an implicit pack whose ref and name come from the detected root's parent directory. Prefer an explicit stable ref; moving the root can otherwise change its implicit identity. ref: MyBalancePack # stable pack reference (save-persistence contract) required if present name: My Balance Pack # display name (default: ref) description: Rebalances early-game production. # string or localized FText map icon: icons/my-pack.png # UTexture2D object path or pack-relative image version: 1.2.0 # semver, informational + used by conflict reports priority: 100 # higher applies earlier within each stage (default 100) enabled: true # false disables the whole pack (default true) debug: false # true logs every applied op from every document in this pack (see Debug Logging) dependencies: # pack refs that must load before this pack - SomeOtherPack redirects: # id renames for generated content (see Content Creation) OldId: NewId # old save class paths resolve to the renamed class (FCoreRedirects) conditions: hasMod: - KAPI - KLib # optional same grammar as a document's `conditions:` (see # Conditions); gates every document in the pack (AND) conditions: on the manifest is evaluated once, before any file in the pack is even read, a failing pack is skipped entirely with one Info diagnostic, instead of every document failing its own copy of the same condition. Use it for "this whole pack is a compat layer for mod X" instead of repeating a conditions: block with hasMod: X at the top of every document. dependencies: are topological constraints. Missing or self-referential dependencies reject the pack, and invalidity propagates to transitive dependants. Dependency cycles are rejected. Among packs whose dependencies are ready, higher priority runs first and ref ascending breaks ties. redirects: maps old generated-content ids to new ones. Generated class names are id-based (Gen_<PackRef>_<Id>), so renaming an id would orphan save data. A redirect entry feeds FCoreRedirects so class paths in existing saves resolve to the renamed class. Renaming a _file_ never needs a redirect. Only id renames do. name and description accept a plain string or localized text with key, ns, and source. icon accepts a cooked UTexture2D object path beginning with /, or a pack-relative PNG, JPG, JPEG, TGA, or BMP file inside the pack directory. Relative icons are limited to 16 MiB and 4096 by 4096 pixels. Dedicated servers skip icon loading.

sections.heading: Script entries (`scripts:`)
sections.text: A pack can carry TypeScript scripts next to its YAML documents (see TypeScript scripting with KDataForgeJS). Each script is one entry under scripts:. Three keys are enough: scripts: - language: kmods.typescript languageVersion: 1 entry: scripts/main.ts | Key | Default | Meaning | | language | required | Script language. kmods.typescript is the only one available. | | languageVersion | 1 | Version of the language contract. | | entry | required | Entry file, pack-relative. KDataForgeJS only accepts scripts/main.ts. | | realm | any | Where the script runs: any, server or client. | | network | any | Network mode: any, standalone or networked. | | authority | any | Authority requirement: any, required or forbidden. | | reflectionClasses | none | Optional. Extra classes to allow, as full class paths (up to 64). classes is an alias. | | imports | none | Optional. Files the script may read with ctx.import, each with key, kind, path and sha256. | You don't set an ID or a list of capabilities here. KDataForge derives the script identity from the pack ref and the entry path, and capabilities come from defineMeta in the script. The classes a script uses are read from its satisfactory imports, so reflectionClasses is only needed when two Blueprints share a name or when a class should be allowed that the code doesn't import. Authoring capabilities (items, recipes, documents, dynamic classes) need realm: any and authority: any. An invalid entry is skipped with a diagnostic; the rest of the pack still loads.

sections.heading: Document structure
sections.text: Every document is a YAML map with a root type: type: cdo # required (or use the `<name>.<type>.yml` filename convention) debug: true # optional log every applied op from this document (see Debug Logging) conditions: ? ... # optional see Conditions include: # optional same-pack files that must apply BEFORE this one - base-values.cdo.yml # … type-specific content priority: belongs to pack.yml, not individual documents. A document-level value is ignored by runtime and rejected by current standalone schemas. Within one pack, include dependencies apply first and remaining documents use deterministic relative-file order. Root type detection order: type: key → filename convention (iron.recipe.yml → recipe). Unknown types warn once and are skipped (they may belong to a handler from another mod or a later phase).

sections.heading: Multiple documents per file
sections.text: A file can hold more than one document by separating them with a --- line (the same convention Kubernetes multi-manifest YAML files use). This lets a small, self-contained pack live in one file instead of several: type: item items: - id: MySuperIngot parent: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties: mDisplayName: Super Ingot mResourceSinkPoints: 100 --- type: sinkpoints track: Default entries: - item: /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MySuperIngot points: 100 - Every document still runs through the normal pipeline independently, with its own debug:, conditions:, and include:, staged and ordered exactly like a document from a separate file. - The <name>.<type>.yml filename convention only applies to single-document files. A file's name can't encode more than one type, so once a file holds multiple documents, every one of them must set its own type: key. A document with no type: in a multi-document file is skipped with a warning rather than falling back to the filename. - Diagnostics identify documents as file.yml[0], file.yml[1], … (zero-based, source order) so a warning always points at the right one. - include: file.yml (referencing a multi-document file by its bare name) waits for all of that file's documents to apply first. You don't need to know (or reference) how many documents it was split into. - A stray trailing --- with nothing after it produces a harmless empty document and is silently ignored. You don't need to trim it.

sections.heading: Root types
sections.text: Most root types are dispatched to a stage-specific handler. Configuration definitions are read before staged document application. The table lists every built-in type, when it runs, and the page with its full grammar and worked examples: | Type | Stage | Detailed page | | config | Configuration | Pack Configuration | | gametag | GameTags | Game Tags | | asset | Assets | Data Assets | | sound | Assets | Sounds | | dataasset | Assets | Data Assets | | curve | Assets | Float and Vector Curves | | localization | Localization | Localization | | cdo | CDOChanges | Patching (type: cdo) | | category | CDOChanges | Categories | | category_reorder | CDOChanges | Category Ordering | | sublevel | CDOChanges | Sublevels | | item | Items | Items | | resource | Items | Resources | | building | Items | Buildings | | unlock | Items | Unlocks | | class | Items | Custom Classes | | recipe | Recipes | Recipes | | schematic | Schematics | Schematics | | research / mam | Research | Research Trees | | sinkpoints | SubsystemMods | Sink Points | | resourcenode | SubsystemMods | Resources | | eventrule | RuntimePatches | Event Rules | | custom (third-party) | handler-declared | registered via RegisterHandler, no page, it's yours | > category generates classes in CDOChanges. Other class generation types (item, > resource, building, unlock, and the generic class) run in the Items stage, priority-ordered > (class → unlock → item → resource → building), so > later stages (recipe, schematic, research) can reference every generated class.

sections.heading: Property patches (`type: cdo`)
sections.text: Use actorSelector: with explicit actor targets and applyToSpawnedActors: true for instance-only tag, sphere, box and current-recipe selection. These entries never modify class defaults and cannot combine with asset/class scope filters. Alternatively, actorAction: destroy | dismantle removes matching live actors. It requires explicit actor targets and applyToSpawnedActors: true; omit properties. The action runs after BeginPlay on a subsequent timer tick, is authority-only (including local non-replicated actors), and supports optional server-only actorSelector predicates. Reload cancels pending actions but does not restore destroyed actors. inventoryRemap: replaces player inventory contents at startup and on inventory changes. Explicit FGCharacterPlayer targets and applyToSpawnedActors: true are required; omit properties and actorAction. Each entry contains item classes from, to and optional positive integer multiplier (default 1). Sources must be unique and cannot also be destinations. Conversion runs only when complete output fits; otherwise original items remain. This is a server-only operation. A cdo document patches properties on something that already exists: a class's default object, a live UObject such as a UDataAsset instance, or every asset matching a class/tag scan. It does not generate new content. One or more target selectors pick what gets patched, and one or more properties: ops describe the write: type: cdo patches: - # ---- one or more target selectors are required; matches accumulate ---- target: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Smelter/Recipe_IngotIron.Recipe_IngotIron_C # class path → patches the class default object # object path → patches that object directly (`UDataAsset` instances etc.) # a sequence of either → every entry resolved and patched independently # AND/OR: allAssetsOfClass: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDataAssetBase # every asset of that class (and subclasses) found in the asset registry # AND/OR an `ofClass:` scope narrowed by one or more filters (all filters must pass): ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe # the scope: this class, its subclasses, its assets # required for matchTag / matchName / where; producedIn / ingredient / product default # to /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe when omitted matchTag: KMods.AlternateRecipe # scalar or sequence (all must match) tagProperty: mGameplayTags # optional explicit tag container property matchAssets: true # also match data-asset instances (default true) classType: blueprint # any (default), blueprint, native; real class flags, not class names excludeClasses: # exact classes only; descendants remain eligible - /Game/Example/Excluded.Excluded_C matchName: Recipe_Alternate_* # wildcard on the class name (full path when it contains '/'); # scalar or sequence (any may match) producedIn: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableManufacturer # recipes whose mProducedIn # references this class or a subclass; scalar or sequence (any may match) ingredient: Desc_IronIngot_C # recipes with this item (or a subclass) in mIngredients product: Desc_IronPlate_C # recipes with this item (or a subclass) in mProduct whereMode: AND # optional; AND default, OR means any clause may hold where: # one map, or a non-empty sequence of maps - path: mManufactoringDuration # property path; `[*]` = any element (read-only) greaterThan: 4 # exactly one operator per clause: # equals | notEquals | lessThan | lessOrEqual | greaterThan | greaterOrEqual # contains | notContains | in [any of] | notIn [any of] | matches (wildcard) | isEmpty (true/false) # ---- modifiers ---- applyToSubclasses: false # class targets: also patch every derived class CDO applyToSpawnedActors: false # actor classes: re-apply ops to every spawning instance deferOneGameTick: false # wait until one game tick after BeginPlay before resolving/applying # ---- the ops ---- properties: # see Property Paths mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply # see Operations (default: set) value: 0.5 An explicit target: accepts one non-empty scalar reference or a non-empty list of them. An empty or non-scalar member invalidates the entire patch entry, with a source-line diagnostic; other selectors on that entry do not bypass the error. See target lists.

sections.heading: Actor-instance selection and actions
sections.text: An actorSelector requires explicit actor-class target values and applyToSpawnedActors: true. At least one field is required, and every supplied field must match: | Field | Value | | tags | Non-empty actor tag, or non-empty list; the actor needs every tag | | sphere | Map with a three-number center sequence and a positive radius | | box | Map with three-number min and max sequences; every minimum must be below its maximum | | currentRecipe | Recipe class, or non-empty list; any exact class may match | Selectors are evaluated after actor begin play for existing actors, later spawns, and actors present after reload. They are lifecycle checks, not continuous queries. Changing an actor's location, tags, or recipe does not re-evaluate it until reload. Full timing, multiplayer, and diagnostics: Actor Instance Selectors. Use actorAction: destroy or actorAction: dismantle instead of properties to remove matching actors. dismantle uses the normal dismantle path where supported. Reload cancels pending actions but cannot restore an actor already removed. Use inventoryRemap instead of properties to convert player inventory stacks; each entry requires from and to item classes and accepts a positive integer multiplier that defaults to 1. Source items must be unique and cannot also be destinations. The complete action and inventory contracts are under Targeting and Player Inventory Remapping.

sections.heading: Sublevel blocking (`type: sublevel`)
sections.text: A sublevel document blocks RefinedRDLib or KBFL sublevel descriptor assets during the CDOChanges stage. block: must be a non-empty sequence. Each entry is an exact asset object path, or a map with target: (scalar or sequence), allAssetsOfClass:, and/or an ofClass: scope with filters (matchTag:, matchName:, where:; assets only, ofClass: is required): type: sublevel block: - /SomeMod/World/DA_OptionalSublevel.DA_OptionalSublevel - target: - /AnotherMod/World/DA_Nodes_A.DA_Nodes_A - /AnotherMod/World/DA_Nodes_B.DA_Nodes_B - allAssetsOfClass: /Script/RefinedRDLib.RRDLSublevelAsset - ofClass: /Script/RefinedRDLib.RRDLSublevelAsset matchName: DA_Optional_* Exact paths use direct object loading. Bulk class scans include derived classes but depend on the Asset Registry being populated. Other asset families warn and must be patched through type: cdo. The provider mods are optional soft integrations. Full behavior and diagnostics: Sublevels.

sections.heading: Pack settings (`type: config`)
sections.text: A config document defines typed settings for its pack. Its filename must end in .config.yml or .config.yaml; configuration definitions are collected separately from ordinary documents. KDataForge stores player values in FactoryGame/Configs/Packs/<PackRef>.config.yml; the authored document contains definitions, not saved values. A pack that defines settings needs a stable ref of at most 50 characters. type: config category: /Script/FactoryGame.FGCategory fields: - id: balance.duration type: number valueType: float name: Production duration description: Recipe duration in seconds used by this pack. default: 1 min: 0.25 max: 4 step: 0.25 display: slider apply: hot fields must be a non-empty sequence. Each field requires id, type, name, description, and default. Set category on the document or on every field. Field IDs are case-insensitively unique within the pack, use dotted ASCII identifiers, and cannot exceed 200 characters. One ID cannot also be another ID's dotted prefix. | Field type | Accepted valueType | Default | Multiple values | | text | string, text, name, tag | string | multiple: true | | number | int8, int16, int32, int64, uint8, float, double | int32 | multiple: true | | boolean | bool, uint8 | bool | No | | select | Every text and number type above, plus bool | string | multiple: true | Common optional fields are tooltip, order, multiple, and apply. apply defaults to cold; hot requests a content reload after a saved value changes. Number fields accept min, max, step, decimals, and display: input | slider. Text fields accept maxLength, multiline, and tagRoot. Lists use minCount and maxCount; multi-selects use minSelected and maxSelected. Select fields require non-empty options entries with value and label. Configuration definitions cannot use config: conditions. Other documents read values through cfg:<id> or cfg:<PackRef>:<id>. For the exact identifier grammar, localized display-text forms, constraint interactions, cleanup rules, generated UI, and hot/cold behavior, use Pack Configuration. That page is the canonical contract for type: config fields.

sections.heading: Category ordering (`type: category_reorder`)
sections.text: category_reorder assigns a category and one-based menu order after ordinary CDO patches have run: type: category_reorder subType: items category: /Game/MyMod/Categories/Cat_Pipelines.Cat_Pipelines_C subCategory: /Game/MyMod/Categories/SC_SpecialPipes.SC_SpecialPipes_C categoryPriority: 4 subCategoryPriority: 2 order: - /Game/MyMod/Pipes/Desc_PipeMk1.Desc_PipeMk1_C - /Game/MyMod/Pipes/Desc_PipeMk2.Desc_PipeMk2_C subType, category, and a non-empty order sequence are required. Every order entry must be unique. categoryPriority and subCategoryPriority accept fractional values. The latter requires subCategory. | subType | order values | subCategory | | items | UFGItemDescriptor class paths | Optional UFGCategory | | recipe | UFGRecipe class paths | Rejected | | schematic | UFGSchematic class paths | Optional UFGSchematicCategory | | settings | UFGUserSetting asset paths | Optional UFGUserSettingCategory | Class targets may load later; unresolved settings assets are immediate errors. See Category Ordering for the exact properties changed for each subtype and the rules for settings with several menu placements.

sections.heading: Runtime sounds (`type: sound`)
sections.text: A sound document creates generated UAkAudioEvent assets from pack-relative audio files: type: sound sounds: - id: AdaWelcome file: audio/welcome.flac name: Welcome voice line description: Volume of the ADA welcome message category: Voice subCategory: ADA sounds must be a non-empty sequence. Each entry requires a stable id and file. IDs start with an ASCII letter and continue with ASCII letters, digits, _, ., or -. file is relative to the pack root and must remain inside it. Supported inputs are PCM16 WAV, native lossless 16-bit FLAC, and Ogg Vorbis; audio must be mono or stereo at 8,000 through 192,000 Hz. Encoded and decoded data are each limited to 64 MiB. name, description, category, and subCategory are optional non-empty strings. Setting subCategory: ADA uses Satisfactory's Dialogue Volume and does not create an individual slider. Other sounds receive local Audio settings; no volume document field exists. Generated event path: /KDataForge/GenAssets/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id>. Sound IDs share this asset namespace with images, curves, and data assets. See Sounds for format checks, dedicated-server behavior, Wwise bank caching, and troubleshooting.

sections.heading: Event rules (`type: eventrule`)
sections.text: Event rules register bounded, server-side reactions to world startup or schematic purchases: type: eventrule rules: - id: progression-followup event: schematicPurchased schematic: /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_1-1.Schematic_1-1_C once: true requiresSchematics: - /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_0-1.Schematic_0-1_C actions: - unlockSchematic: /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_2-3.Schematic_2-3_C - log: Follow-up schematic granted. | Field | Required | Contract | | rules | Yes | 1 to 256 rules per document | | id | Yes | 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, ., _, or -; case-insensitively unique in the pack | | event | Yes | worldReady or schematicPurchased | | schematic | No | Concrete schematic filter, valid only with schematicPurchased | | once | No | Defaults to true; successful completion is stored in the save by pack ref and rule ID | | requiresSchematics | No | Up to 64 schematic classes; all must already be purchased | | actions | Yes | 1 to 32 maps containing exactly one unlockSchematic or log action | log accepts nonblank text up to 2,048 characters. The full document is rejected when any rule is invalid or when IDs collide. worldReady does not fire again after /kdf reload; reloaded purchase rules handle only later purchases. See Event Rules for cascade limits, grant failure behavior, once-per-save persistence, and reload timing.

sections.heading: Property paths
sections.text: properties: accepts an ordered list of path/value operations or a shorter mapping. In the mapping, each key is a property path and its value performs set by default: properties: mDisplayNameOverride: true mDisplayName: Compressed Power Shard mIngredients: - ItemClass: /Game/Example/Desc_Item.Desc_Item_C Amount: 4 mSomeStruct: X: 1 Y: 2 For another operation, place $op directly inside that property's value. The remaining keys are the same arguments as in the list form (value, index, where, from, etc.): properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.5 mIngredients: $op: append value: ItemClass: /Game/Example/Desc_Item.Desc_Item_C Amount: 4 Only $op marks an operation. A struct containing ordinary fields named op or value remains a plain struct value. If a struct itself contains $op, wrap it as an indented mapping with $op: set and put the literal struct beneath value:. Property mappings also work inside instanced-object properties: blocks, including nested struct values. Mapping keys execute in source order; use the list form when the same path needs multiple operations, because a YAML mapping cannot repeat a key. The existing list form remains supported. An individual $op mapping cannot carry conditions:. To gate one property, put conditions: on its containing patch entry, or use a conditional operation in the list form. In a properties: mapping, the quoted key '@tagContainers': selects all top-level FGameplayTagContainer fields on each actual target, including inherited fields and fields declared by late-loaded subclasses. It supports set (default), append, prepend, remove and clear. No matching fields is a no-op. It does not select nested fields and is invalid in where, from, templates and single-property read/edit APIs. See tag-container selection. A property mapping key (or path: in the ordered list form) addresses a single property or a nested member reached through arrays, sets, maps, or object references. It uses a small path grammar shared by every operation below: Segment(.Segment)* Segment = Name([<int>] | ["key"] | [key])* | Example | Meaning | | mManufactoringDuration | plain property | | mIngredients[0].Amount | struct member of array element 0 | | mSomeMap["Iron"].Value | struct member of map value for key Iron | | mSomeSet[2] | third element of a set (logical order) | | mMeshComponent.RelativeScale3D | dereference through an object-typed member (components, subobjects) | | mIngredients[*].ItemClass | any element (cdo where: filters only, never in properties: ops) | Blueprint-defined properties match on their authored name (case-insensitive), so mangled BP names never appear in YAML.

sections.heading: Operations
sections.text: $op: values in mapping form (op: in list form) and their argument keys. Full worked examples: Operations. | Op | Applies to | Arguments | | set (default) | everything | value | | add, subtract, multiply, divide, min, max | numeric | value | | clamp | numeric | min, max | | append | array, set, map, string/name/text, tag container, bitmask | value (map for map; scalar or sequence otherwise) | | append_unique | array | value (one element or sequence); append only missing values, preserving existing duplicates | | update_where | array of structs | where, value; optional whereMode: AND|OR (default AND) | | replace_refs | reflected property subtree | from, value; recursively replace matching object/class references | | prepend | array, set, string/name/text, tag container, bitmask | value (scalar or sequence) | | insert | array | index, value | | remove | array (by value), set (by value), map (by key), tag container, bitmask | value | | remove_at | array | index | | clear | array, set, map, string/name/text, tag container, bitmask | none | | swap | array | index, with | | replace | array | index, value | | duplicate | array | index | | sort, reverse | array | none | | unique | array (set: no-op) | none | | copy, move | everything | from (property path on the same object; move clears the source) | Unsupported op×type combinations are diagnostics at load time, never silent no-ops.

sections.heading: Special-cased properties
sections.text: A few properties need more than a plain reflected write. KDataForge handles them automatically: - FGameplayTagContainer: accepts set/append/prepend/remove/clear with plain tag names (no native-struct text form needed). - mStackSize (any FGItemDescriptor-derived target): this is an EStackSize enum (SS_ONE/SS_SMALL/SS_MEDIUM/SS_BIG/SS_HUGE/SS_FLUID), not a plain integer. Set it with an enum value name like any other enum property. The engine also caches item stack sizes, so writing the property alone would not change anything in-game. This is why KBFL ships a dedicated UKBFLCDOItemStackSize helper. Any op that writes mStackSize also resets the descriptor's cached stack size (mCachedStackSize), so the change takes effect out of the box. There are two caveats. Inventories that already contain the item may need the item re-added (or a game reload) before slots reflect the new limit. Also, if you use KBFL's own CDO assets for stack sizes, don't patch the same descriptor from both sides. Example with the full caveat: Balancing → Items.

sections.heading: Value forms by property type
sections.text: Each reflected property type accepts its own YAML shape when used as an operation's value: (or min/max/with argument). The table below is the authoritative mapping from UE property type to accepted YAML form: | Property type | YAML form | | bool | true / false / yes / no / on / off / 1 / 0 | | int32, int64, uint*, uint8 | integer scalar | | float, double | number scalar | | enum | value name (RF_SOLID, EResourceForm::RF_SOLID) or numeric value (must be a valid ordinal, rejected otherwise) | | bitmask (int32/etc. with meta=(Bitmask, BitmaskEnum=...)) | one flag name (Above), a YAML sequence of names, an "Above|Left" string, or, for set only, a nonnegative unsigned decimal mask bounded by the property width. Named forms require available property metadata and a loaded enum, supporting declared mask values and bit indices. Export emits a name sequence. append/prepend OR-add flags, remove clears bits, and clear writes zero. See rules below. | | FString, FName | string scalar | | FText | string scalar, null (empty), localized mapping with key, ns, and source, or StringTable reference with stringTable and key; both table fields must be non-empty and must not mix with ns or source | | object reference | full object path; a bare generated-content id (e.g. SuperIngotIcon for a dataasset/asset entry, see Generated Content Short Ids); ""/none → null | | class reference | class path (/Script/Module.Class or /Game/....Asset_C; _C auto-retried), or a bare generated-content id (e.g. MySuperIngot for an item/resource/building/class/... entry, see Generated Content Short Ids), or, as a last resort, a bare class name (Desc_Water) resolved by name against every class currently loaded in memory; ambiguous bare-name forms log an error (LogKDataForge, listing every match) and use the first match (sorted by full class path), so prefer full paths in published packs when it matters | | TSoftObjectPtr / TSoftClassPtr | path string (not loaded) | | struct | native text form ("(X=1,Y=2,Z=3)"), block map with named fields, or block positional sequence | | FGameplayTag | tag name string | | FGameplayTagContainer | sequence of tag names | | TArray | sequence | | TSet | sequence | | TMap | map (keys converted via the key property type) | | nested structs | nested maps, any depth | For bitmasks whose enum has Bitflags metadata, available enum metadata distinguishes declared mask values (UseEnumValuesAsMaskValuesInEditor=true) from bit indices. Named bit indices 0..63 map to 1 << index and must fit the property width: 0..7, 0..15, 0..31, or 0..63 for 8-, 16-, 32-, or 64-bit properties, including signed properties. Plain integer bitmask handling requires WITH_METADATA, property Bitmask and BitmaskEnum metadata, and the referenced enum already loaded. If metadata is stripped or the enum cannot be resolved, conversion falls back to ordinary integer rules, including normal signed ranges; named bitmask forms and mutation operations are unavailable. Shipping builds must retain that metadata to use these forms. Enum-backed properties follow their separate enum conversion path: set one enum name or numeric value, with Bitflags values limited to declared bits. Pipe-joined names, sequences of flag names, and bitmask mutation operations are not supported for enum-backed properties. Reflection exports bitmaskMode for resolved enums with Bitflags metadata, including enum-backed property records, so editor validation can check their declared bits. Raw masks are accepted by set only; append/prepend and remove require named flags. Raw masks must contain only declared bits when the enum has Bitflags metadata; otherwise the resulting value must match a valid enum value. Both forms must fit the property width. Recognized signed bitmask properties accept the full unsigned bit pattern (0..4294967295 for int32, 0..18446744073709551615 for int64). Named flags must also fit that width. Negative enum values and declared mask values using bit 63 are unsupported because UEnum stores signed int64 values; bit-index 63 remains supported. Ordinary integer properties retain their normal signed ranges. See Property Types for examples and high-bit behavior.

sections.heading: Gameplay tag registration (`type: gametag`)
sections.text: A gametag document registers new FGameplayTag names with the engine's gameplay tag tree before any other document type runs. This matters because tags referenced from cdo targeting (matchTag:) or from a FGameplayTagContainer property write must already exist to resolve: type: gametag tags: - tag: MyPack.Machines.Special # map form with comment comment: Marks special machines - MyPack.Simple # scalar shorthand Tags are registered at runtime by appending to the gameplay-tag settings list in memory, never written to config files, with a tag-tree rebuild when needed. This is the only runtime channel that survives the engine's own tree reconstructs. Register tags before using them in cdo documents: the GameTags stage always runs first.

sections.heading: Content creation (`item`, `resource`, `building`, `recipe`, `schematic`, `research`, `unlock`)
sections.text: These seven root types generate new classes at runtime. All share the same entry grammar. Only the plural list key and the default parent differ: type: item # or resource / building / recipe / schematic / research / unlock items: # plural key per type see table below - id: MySuperIngot # required stable id, the save-persistence contract parent: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C # optional properties: # identical op entries to cdo patches, applied to the new class's CDO mDisplayName: Super Ingot mStackSize: SS_HUGE # EStackSize enum, not a plain integer see Special-cased properties | Type | Plural key | Default parent | | item | items | /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor | | resource | resources | /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceDescriptor | | building | buildings | /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildingDescriptor | | recipe | recipes | /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe | | schematic | schematics | /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematic | | research | research | /Script/FactoryGame.FGResearchTree | | unlock | unlocks | none: a concrete FGUnlock subclass must be given as parent |

sections.heading: Generated class identity (save-persistence contract)
sections.text: - Classes live in package /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef> and are named Gen_<PackRef>_<Id>: deterministic and id-based, never derived from file paths or load order. - Reference a generated class elsewhere (recipes, unlocks, sinkpoints, other YAML) as /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> with no _C suffix. - The id is the contract. Renaming a file is safe. Renaming an id needs a pack redirect (redirects: in pack.yml). - Classes are created during GameInstance INITIALIZATION strictly before any save loads, so save class-path resolution finds them in memory. - Constraint: generated classes have the parent's layout, with no new reflected properties or components. All variation lives in CDO defaults (which is exactly what properties: sets).

sections.heading: Generated content short IDs
sections.text: Anywhere a class or object reference is accepted (parent:, properties: values, target:, item: on sinkpoints, class:, …), a bare id (just the id: a document gave the content, e.g. MySuperIngot) resolves in addition to the full /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> path. Both forms always work; use whichever reads better: type: item items: - id: PureSuperIngot parent: SuperIngot # short id same as /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_SuperIngot - Resolution order: the id is looked up in the current document's own pack first (the common case: most references are to something the same pack just generated). If it isn't there, every pack's generated content is searched; a match in exactly one other pack still resolves. Matches in more than one pack log an error (LogKDataForge, listing every match) and apply to the first match (sorted by full path), the same ambiguity handling as the bare class-name shortcut above. Qualify with the full path to remove any ambiguity or to reference another pack's content unambiguously. - Covers both generated classes (item/resource/building/recipe/schematic/research/ unlock/class) and generated asset instances (dataasset/asset, e.g. an icon's id in mSmallIcon: SuperIngotIcon instead of /KDataForge/GenAssets/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_SuperIngotIcon). - Only tried for name-only input (no / and no . at all). Anything that looks like a path is always treated as a path, never as an id. - Works everywhere a class/object reference is resolved: properties: values, target:, allAssetsOfClass:, ofClass:, parent:, register-only class:, item: on sinkpoints, and spawn-time actor patches (applyToSpawnedActors: true) re-applied to newly spawned actors.

sections.heading: Registration (`recipe`, `schematic`, `research`)
sections.text: type: recipe recipes: - id: Recipe_MySuperIngot register: true # default omit unless you want registration off properties: mManufactoringDuration: 4

sections.heading: Removing registered content (`recipe`, `schematic`, `research`)
sections.text: These three document types also accept a document-level remove: sequence. It may be the whole document or appear beside the normal entries list. An entry is either a bare class reference (full path, bare class name, or generated-content short id) that removes exactly that class, or a **filter map** using the scope filters: matchTag:, matchName:, producedIn:, ingredient:, product:, where:, and optional ofClass:. This removes every class of the type passing all of them: type: schematic remove: - /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Progression/Schematic_1-1.Schematic_1-1_C - Schematic_ObsoleteFromAnotherPack - where: # filter map: ofClass defaults to FGSchematic here path: mTechTier greaterOrEqual: 8 # Optional: registration/generation entries can coexist. Explicit removal runs after registration. schematics: - id: Schematic_Replacement - Only recipe, schematic, and research (including type: mam) support this key. item, resource, building, unlock, and class do not have a live registry-removal path. - A bare reference matches by exact class; removing a parent does not remove its subclasses. A filter map's ofClass: defaults to FGRecipe / FGSchematic / FGResearchTree and must stay within that base; a map without any filter key is an error. - Filter rules are stored as predicates and evaluated against every class of the kind the game presents (recipes: on every grant; schematics/research: at world registration), so classes that load later are still caught. - Schematic and research-tree removal is save-clean and reverses on the next session after the pack is removed. Existing purchase/unlock state is not revoked. - Recipe removal prevents future adds and sweeps recipes restored from the server save. The available-recipe list is saved, but it self-heals on a later load without the pack when purchased schematics reapply their unlocks. - Removing a schematic does not remove recipes it already granted. Pair schematic and recipe removal rules when the content itself must become unavailable. See Removing Content for the consolidated guide, and Recipes, Schematics, and Research Trees for kind-specific notes. - register: true (default) queues the class for per-world registration into SML's UModContentRegistry, before the registry freezes at world begin play. Auto-propagation applies: registering a schematic registers its recipes. Recipes register their items. - Register-only mode: use class: instead of id: to register an existing class without generating one: type: schematic schematics: - class: /Game/SomeMod/Schematics/Schematic_Hidden.Schematic_Hidden_C # register, don't generate

sections.heading: Nodes: placing a schematic in a research tree
sections.text: A research entry modifies its visual M.A.M. graph directly. addNodes: appends node instances; it does not update or deduplicate an existing node with the same schematic. A usable node normally supplies the displayed schematic: and a coordinate:. parents: creates prerequisite relationships; with autoPath: true on the research entry, KDataForge also creates straight roads for those relationships: type: research research: - id: MyResearchTree autoPath: true addNodes: - schematic: Schematic_First coordinate: X: 0 Y: 0 - schematic: Schematic_Second coordinate: X: 2 Y: 0 parents: - schematic: Schematic_First - schematic: accepts a generated short id or a full UFGSchematic class path. - coordinate: is a block map with numeric X: and Y: fields. Supply it for a node that participates in graph relationships or roads. - parents:, nodesToUnhide:, and unhiddenBy: are optional. Each reference may name another node's schematic: or a literal coordinate. References may point forward or backward within the same addNodes: list, or to a node already present on the target tree. - autoPath: defaults to false. When enabled, each resolved parents: relationship gets a straight, two-point visual road. Leave it off and provide childrenAndRoads: on the parent for a bent or otherwise custom route. - class: optionally selects a UFGResearchTreeNode subclass; properties: applies ordinary property operations to that node. A convenience field missing from a custom node logs a warning and is skipped rather than failing the whole document. A custom road uses a child coordinate and every point along the path. childrenAndRoads: can be one a block map with key and points fields, or a sequence of those maps when a node has multiple children: addNodes: - schematic: Schematic_First coordinate: X: 0 Y: 0 childrenAndRoads: - key: X: 2 Y: 0 points: - X: 0 Y: 0 - X: 0 Y: 1 - X: 2 Y: 1 - X: 2 Y: 0 - key: X: 0 Y: 2 points: - X: 0 Y: 0 - X: 0 Y: 2 Use tree-entry-level removeNodes: to remove nodes by schematic class or short id. Each selector may be a scalar (Schematic_Obsolete) or a block map with schematic: Schematic_Obsolete. KDataForge performs all removals before appending the same entry's addNodes: list and removes every surviving Parents, NodesToUnhide, UnhiddenBy, and ChildrenAndRoads reference to each removed coordinate. The same entry may remove one node and add another; autoPath: applies to additions: research: - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Schematics/Research/Mycelia_RS/ResearchTree_Mycelia.ResearchTree_Mycelia_C register: false autoPath: true removeNodes: - Schematic_Obsolete addNodes: - schematic: Schematic_Replacement coordinate: X: 3 Y: 1 parents: - schematic: Schematic_ExistingParent autoPath: is a sibling of addNodes: on the research entry and generates straight roads for its resolved parents: relationships. To move a node, select and re-add the same schematic with its new coordinate. nodes: remains a legacy alias. If both keys exist, addNodes: wins and KDataForge warns that nodes: was ignored.

sections.heading: Instanced dependencies on research trees
sections.text: Research entries accept unlockDependencies: and visibilityDependencies:. Both use the block maps containing class: and properties: in the instanced FGAvailabilityDependency shape; they append to mUnlockDependencies and mVisibilityDependencies, respectively. research: - id: MyResearchTree unlockDependencies: - class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematicPurchasedDependency properties: mSchematics: - Schematic_MyPrerequisite visibilityDependencies: - class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGGamePhaseReachedDependency properties: mGamePhase: EGP_EarlyGame

sections.heading: Instanced unlocks on schematics (`unlocks:`)
sections.text: Schematic entries accept an unlocks: list. Each entry creates an instanced FGUnlock subobject on the schematic's CDO. This works with every concrete FGUnlock subclass shipped by the base game, including FGUnlockRecipe; see the Base-Game Unlock Classes for the full list: type: schematic schematics: - id: Schematic_MySuperIngot properties: mDisplayName: My Super Ingot unlocks: - class: /Game/FactoryGame/Unlocks/BP_UnlockRecipe.BP_UnlockRecipe_C properties: mRecipes: - /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_Recipe_MySuperIngot Known native FactoryGame/KMods class paths automatically remap to their Blueprint implementation. Exact Blueprint paths remain valid. Concrete native classes without Blueprints stay native; abstract classes without concrete variants cannot be instanced.

sections.heading: Schematic shortcut unlocks
sections.text: In addition to generic unlocks:, schematic entries accept recipes: (sequence of UFGRecipe classes), schematics: (sequence of UFGSchematic classes), positive-integer handSlots: and inventorySlots:, and scannableResources: (sequence of block maps containing resource: and nodeType:, with nodeType: Node by default). Each shortcut creates the corresponding normal FGUnlock instance; class references resolve exactly like every other generated, vanilla, or mod class reference.

sections.heading: Instanced dependencies on schematics (`dependencies:`)
sections.text: Schematic entries also accept a dependencies: list (the same instanced-object mechanism as unlocks:), targeting mSchematicDependencies instead of mUnlocks. Each entry creates an instanced FGAvailabilityDependency subobject on the schematic's CDO: type: schematic schematics: - id: Schematic_AdvancedSuperIngot properties: mDisplayName: Advanced Super Ingot dependencies: - class: /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematicPurchasedDependency properties: mSchematics: - /KDataForge/Gen/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_Schematic_MySuperIngot mRequireAllSchematicsToBePurchased: true Pair it with mDependenciesBlocksSchematicAccess/mHiddenUntilDependenciesMet (ordinary properties:) to control whether the schematic is merely blocked from purchase or hidden entirely until the dependency is met. See Type: schematic → Gating a schematic on prerequisites for the full worked example and other FGAvailabilityDependency subclasses worth knowing about.

sections.heading: Generic class generation (`type: class`)
sections.text: The seven preset types above are the recommended, ergonomic forms. class is the **escape hatch for everything else: it generates a new class from any** parent, whether native C++ (/Script/Module.Class) or Blueprint (/Game/....Thing_C). Examples include equipment descriptors, vehicle descriptors, item/schematic categories, FGUnlock subclasses, other mods' classes gated behind hasMod, reparented buildables, and more. type: class debug: true # optional (see Debug Logging) classes: - id: MyCustomThing parent: /Script/FactoryGame.FGEquipmentDescriptor # ANY class: native C++ or /Game/...Thing_C registerAs: recipe # OPTIONAL: recipe | schematic | research queues SML content # registration for kinds that need it; omit for everything else properties: mDisplayName: My Equipment # cdo-style op entries applied to the new class's CDO - Same save-stable identity as the preset kinds: /KDataForge/Gen/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id>. Manifest, tombstones, and redirects: all apply identically. - Runs in the Items stage (same as item/resource/building/unlock), so recipe, schematic, and research documents can reference the generated classes. - registerAs: queues the class into SML's UModContentRegistry like the corresponding preset type would. It's only needed for the three registered kinds. Everything else just needs to exist. - The constraint stays: generated classes copy the parent's layout, with no new reflected properties or components. All variation is CDO defaults. Worked examples (equipment descriptor, category, modded parent behind hasMod) live at Custom Classes. For reparenting a buildable as part of a complete building, see A Complete Building.

sections.heading: 2D image assets (`type: asset`)
sections.text: Loads image files from the pack and turns them into real, referenceable UTexture2D assets: type: asset assets: - id: MyIcon file: icons/my-icon.png # relative to the pack root; png / jpg / tga / bmp - Decoded at load into a transient UTexture2D at /KDataForge/GenAssets/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> and announced to the asset registry. - Reference it from any properties: entry like any other object path: value: /KDataForge/GenAssets/MyPack.Gen_MyPack_MyIcon. - Image files are decoded during the next GameInstance initialization after they change. - 2D only: no FBX/glTF, ever, by design. DDS and WAV image formats aren't supported yet (PNG/JPG/TGA/BMP are). Icon usage example (item mSmallIcon / mPersistentBigIcon): Data Assets → 2D image assets.

sections.heading: Dynamic DataAsset instances (`type: dataasset`)
sections.text: Creates real UDataAsset instances (not classes) at runtime, using package /KDataForge/GenAssets/<PackRef> and name Gen_<PackRef>_<Id>. It announces them to the asset registry so scanning subsystems can find them. UPrimaryDataAsset subclasses are the common consumer-facing case, but the runtime validator accepts any UDataAsset subclass. type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: CleanerItem_MyFluid class: /Script/KAPI.KAPICleanerItemDescription # any UDataAsset subclass properties: mProductionTime: 4.0 mInFluid: ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Water/Desc_Water.Desc_Water_C Amount: 1000 After the initial load, KDataForge automatically triggers consumer rescans when data assets were modified or added: - KAPI: called via reflection only when the KAPI mod is loaded, no hard dependency needed. - RefinedRDApi: called via reflection only when the RefinedRDApi mod is loaded, with no dependency needed. It covers RefinedPower / FicsitFarming boiler/cooler/heater/turbine/generator/dirt data assets. Existing data assets (KAPI's, RRDA's, any mod's) are already editable via cdo documents (target: object path, allAssetsOfClass:, matchTag:). The dataasset type is only for creating new instances. Data-asset entries may also contain unlocks: and dependencies: lists. They append instanced objects to mUnlocks and mTaskDependencies when selected class exposes those arrays. This is intended for UKAPIDeliveryTask; incompatible classes report missing array at runtime. Entry shape and native-to-Blueprint remapping match schematic lists.

sections.heading: Float and vector curve assets (`type: curve`)
sections.text: Creates new or edits existing UCurveFloat and UCurveVector assets. keys: replaces complete key set on each entry. type: curve curveType: float # float | vector curves: - id: DamageFalloff # exactly one of id or target # target: /Game/Curves/Curve_Damage.Curve_Damage defaultValue: 0 # vector defaults use X/Y/Z fields in a block mapping preInfinityExtrap: constant postInfinityExtrap: linear isEventCurve: false # float only keys: - time: 0 value: 1 # vectors also accept block X/Y/Z fields or block sequence items interpMode: cubic # constant | linear | cubic tangentMode: auto # auto | smartAuto | user | break tangentWeightMode: none # none | arrive | leave | both arriveTangent: 0 leaveTangent: 0 arriveTangentWeight: 0 leaveTangentWeight: 0 preInfinityExtrap and postInfinityExtrap accept none, constant, linear, cycle, cycleWithOffset, or oscillate. Times must be finite and unique within one entry. Vector values and tangent fields accept an X/Y/Z map or three-number sequence. Generated curves use object path /KDataForge/GenAssets/<PackRef>.Gen_<PackRef>_<Id> and have no _C suffix. See Float and Vector Curves for full examples and troubleshooting.

sections.heading: AWESOME Sink point values (`type: sinkpoints`)
sections.text: A sinkpoints document sets the AWESOME Sink point value for one or more items on a named track. The FGResourceSinkSubsystem consults this whenever it looks up how many points an item is worth: type: sinkpoints track: Default # Default | Exploration entries: - item: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C points: 100 overridden: 50 # optional - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGItemDescriptor # filter form instead of `item:` — every loaded where: # item descriptor passing the filters gets these points path: mForm in: - RF_LIQUID - RF_GAS points: 0 An entry names one item:, or replaces it with an ofClass: scope (default FGItemDescriptor) plus filters (matchTag:, matchName:, where:, …). Filter entries expand against the item descriptor classes loaded when the document applies. Not live-reloadable (registry freeze): sinkpoint changes need a session restart.

sections.heading: Resource nodes (`type: resourcenode`)
sections.text: A resourcenode document requires at least one non-empty remove:, add: or replace: sequence. add creates or reuses an ordinary resource node. replace requires an existing ordinary node in range and changes that actor in place. Positions and distances use Unreal centimetres; rotations use pitch, yaw, and roll in degrees. type: resourcenode add: - id: northern-iron resource: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreIron/Desc_OreIron.Desc_OreIron_C position: - 10000 - 20000 - 1200 purity: Pure checkRange: 500 reuseExisting: true allowToMove: true replace: - id: nearby-copper resource: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreCopper/Desc_OreCopper.Desc_OreCopper_C fromResource: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreIron/Desc_OreIron.Desc_OreIron_C position: - 30000 - 20000 - 1200 checkRange: 500 allowToMove: false Stable id values are required and must be unique across every add and replace entry in the pack. Both forms require resource and a finite three-number position. Their shared optional fields are rotation, purity, checkRange, allowToMove, fromResource, mesh, material, and materials. material and materials are mutually exclusive. checkRange defaults to 500 and must be greater than zero and no more than 100000. add also accepts reuseExisting (default true), preventOverlap (default false), and overlapClass (default FGResourceNodeBase). replace accepts radius as an alias for checkRange, but not together with it. An addition defaults to Normal purity; replacement and reuse preserve the existing purity when it is omitted. Placement and replacement support ordinary nodes only. Occupied nodes, unresolved extractor links, and nodes with saved randomization overrides are preserved. For save ownership, restoration, actor replication, node meshes, overlap checks, and reload limits, see Resource Node Placement. That page is the canonical contract for add and replace entries. Within remove:, a scalar is shorthand for a map with only resource:. Valid entries still apply when another entry reports an error: type: resourcenode remove: - /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Uranium/Desc_OreUranium.Desc_OreUranium_C - resource: MyGeneratedResource nodeTypes: - Node - FrackingCore allowOccupied: false removeFromScanner: true - ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGResourceDescriptor # filter form instead of `resource:` matchName: Desc_OreUranium* # every loaded descriptor passing the filters nodeTypes: - Node - resource: must resolve to a UFGResourceDescriptor class. Generated-content short ids work. Alternatively an entry carries an ofClass: scope (default FGResourceDescriptor) plus filters (matchTag:, matchName:, where:, …) and applies its options to every loaded descriptor class that passes. - nodeTypes: is optional. Omitted or empty means all types; accepted values are Node, FrackingSatellite, FrackingCore, Geyser, and Deposit, with or without the EResourceNodeType:: prefix. - allowOccupied: defaults to false. The default skips and warns about node groups used by an extractor. true can invalidate an extractor's node reference. - removeFromScanner: defaults to true. It also strips vanilla scanner pairs and matching KAPI allow-list data, then refreshes scanner/radar caches. :::danger Vanilla can persist level-placed node destruction in the save. Deleting the YAML does not reliably restore those actors. Back up the save and read the full persistence and deferred-pass limitations under Resources and Resource Nodes. ::: The same document type accepts visuals, hideMeshes, and meshActorsPerTick for node appearance: type: resourcenode visuals: - resource: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/OreIron/Desc_OreIron.Desc_OreIron_C materials: - slot: 0 material: /MyMod/Materials/MI_Node.MI_Node hideMeshes: - /MyMod/ResourceNodes/SM_OldNode.SM_OldNode meshActorsPerTick: 1 Each visual entry requires one exact resource descriptor and a non-empty materials list. Material records require a unique zero-based slot from 0 through 63 and a material or material-instance object path. hideMeshes contains exact static-mesh object paths. meshActorsPerTick defaults to 1, accepts 1 through 1024, and requires visuals or hideMeshes in the document. Full precedence, streaming, client, and restoration behavior: Resource Node Appearance.

sections.heading: Runtime text entries (`type: localization`)
sections.text: A localization document injects or overrides FText string table entries at runtime. It is scoped to a namespace and optionally a single culture, and it needs no separate localization asset shipped: type: localization namespace: MyPack culture: de # optional; prefix-matched against current language; omit = all entries: SimpleKey: 'Übersetzter Text' KeyWithSource: source: 'Original English' text: 'Deutscher Text' # override existing texts - culture: is prefix-matched against the current language (de matches de-DE). Omitting it applies the entries for every language. - The scalar form sets the text for namespace/key. A block map with source and text fields overrides existing texts by their original source string. - Localization documents apply during GameInstance initialization. Restart the session after edits.

sections.heading: Debug logging
sections.text: Every applied op can be traced. Three levels, from narrow to global: | Level | How | Effect | | Document | debug: true top-level key in any document type | Every applied op from that document logs | | Pack | debug: true in pack.yml | Every applied op from every document of the pack logs | | Global | console variable KDF.Debug 1 (or launch arg -KDFDebug) | Everything logs, including editor-originated ops | Log lines go to the game log at Log verbosity, one per applied op: [KDF DEBUG] <file>: <target path>.<property path> <op> : <pre value> -> <post value> Walkthrough (where the log file lives, reading the lines): Create your first pack: trace an operation.

sections.heading: Conditions
sections.text: Condition objects use AND by default; conditionBehaivor: OR opts into alternatives. A failing combined result skips the document with an Info diagnostic. conditions: gameVersion: '>=416000.0.0' # semver range vs the game version, reported as <changelist>.0.0 # (SML convention) gate on the game's build changelist, e.g. the # CL from the game's main menu / `>=491125.0.0` for the SML baseline hasMod: KAPI # scalar… # hasMod may instead use a block sequence; `Ref@<range>` pins a version modVersion: # explicit map form for version constraints SML: '>=3.12.0' hasClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableFrackingActivator # hasClass may instead use a block sequence conditions: may also be an array of condition objects. Within each object, condition keys are AND-combined first; ifNotMatch: true then negates that object. Top-level conditionBehaivor combines the object results using AND or OR (case-insensitive) and defaults to AND. Correctly spelled conditionBehavior is accepted as an alias. ifNotMatch defaults to false. conditionBehaivor: AND # optional; default conditions: - hasMod: - KAPI - KLib # require both - hasMod: IncompatibleMod # require this mod to be absent ifNotMatch: true - modVersion: # reject this version range if mod is loaded OptionalIntegration: '^2.0.0' ifNotMatch: true An inverted hasMod: Mod@<range> object matches when the mod is absent or its loaded version does not satisfy <range>. Inversion never hides malformed condition keys, types, or version ranges. Because inversion applies to the entire object, use separate inverted objects when excluding multiple mods independently. conditionBehaivor: OR conditions: - hasMod: RefinedPower - hasMod: FicsitFarming OR passes when at least one object matches; AND requires every object. Each object is evaluated and optionally inverted before aggregation. Invalid behavior values or malformed condition objects fail closed even if another OR branch matches. An empty array passes under AND and fails under OR. The config: condition accepts one expression string or a nonempty list of expression strings; every expression in the list must be true. At runtime, config: [] is an error and skips the affected pack, document, or list element. Neither ifNotMatch: true nor another matching OR branch hides this error. This requirement does not change the empty outer conditions: [] behavior above. Version ranges use SML's semver syntax: >=1.2.3, ^3.12.0, ~1.2.0, exact 1.2.3, unions with ||.

sections.heading: Dependency ordering (`include:`)
sections.text: include: lists relative file paths (same pack) whose documents must apply before this one within the same stage. It is ordering, not textual inclusion. Cycles fall back to path order with a warning.

sections.heading: Determinism
sections.text: Apply order is deterministic: dependency-aware pack topology (priority descending and ref ascending among ready packs) → stage → handler (priority descending, root type ascending) → same-stage include: constraints → relative path. KDataForge does not negotiate a multiplayer pack checksum or stream general operations between peers. See Architecture.

pages.title: How-to guides
pages.description: Complete a specific KDataForge authoring, integration, maintenance, or debugging task.

sections.heading: How-to guides
sections.text: These guides assume you have completed Create your first pack. Each guide starts from a goal, provides the required files and YAML, and ends with a result you can check. Use Authoring concepts for the underlying model, Document types and features for a capability, or Reference for an exact field or default.

sections.heading: Create content
sections.text: - Create an item, icon, recipe, and Tier 1 unlock builds a common first content chain and makes it obtainable in a new save. - Create a research tree generates the tree, places MAM schematics in its node graph, and shows how to extend or prune its branches. - Add a recipe to an existing schematic adds an unlock to a vanilla schematic, another mod's schematic, or one from an earlier pack version.

sections.heading: Integrate and balance
sections.text: - Balance content by tag registers a gameplay tag and edits every matching target with one patch. - Build a conditional multi-mod pack adds content only when a required mod version or class is present, without a hard dependency. - Edit another mod's data assets patches existing KAPI or RefinedR&D PrimaryDataAsset instances without generating replacements.

sections.heading: Prepare and maintain a release
sections.text: - Localize your pack adds translated text and safely overrides existing vanilla or mod strings. - Rename generated content safely separates file renames from identity changes and shows where redirects: can preserve saves. - Turn live edits into a shareable pack exports changes from /kdf editor and verifies that they survive a restart.

sections.heading: Diagnose a failure
sections.text: - Debug a pack that will not apply checks discovery, parsing, conditions, targets, operations, reload limits, and logs in order. For complete packs that combine several document types, continue to Examples.

pages.title: Build a conditional multi-mod integration pack
pages.description: Adding bonus content only when another mod (or a specific version of it, or just one of its classes) is present, without a hard dependency and without breaking the load for players who don't have it.

sections.heading: Build a conditional multi-mod integration pack
sections.text: This tutorial builds a pack that adds content when another mod is installed, such as a KAPI data asset, a buildable patch, or a bonus recipe. Players without that mod should receive no errors, warnings, or crashes. Conditions & Packs documents each condition key; this page shows how those keys behave together in an optional integration.

sections.heading: The core idea
sections.text: conditions: is a top-level key accepted by every document type, including cdo, item, dataasset, schematic, and more. It accepts one condition object or an array of condition objects. Keys in an object are AND-combined. An object's optional ifNotMatch: true field negates that object's combined result. Top-level conditionBehaivor: AND|OR combines array objects and defaults to AND. type: cdo conditions: hasMod: KAPI patches: - target: /Script/KAPI.KAPIDataAssetBase # ... If the combined condition result fails, KDFConditionEvaluator::Evaluate returns false for that document. The document is dropped before its handler ever runs, so no properties:, no patches:, nothing inside it is touched. The loader records a single Info-severity diagnostic (Skipped by conditions: <reason>) and moves on to the next document. Nothing else in the pack, or in any other pack, is affected. This is the entire mechanism behind optional integration: write the bonus content as if the other mod is always there, then gate the whole document on a condition that's false when it isn't.

sections.heading: `hasMod:` scalar, sequence, and version-pinned forms
sections.text: conditions: hasMod: KAPI # scalar one mod, any version --- conditions: hasMod: - KAPI - RefinedPower # sequence ALL must be loaded --- conditions: hasMod: RefinedPower@>=4.0.0 # inline version pin, one mod reference --- conditions: hasMod: - KAPI - "RefinedPower@>=4.0.0" # mix plain refs and pinned refs in one sequence Straight from the evaluator: a scalar value becomes a one-element list, and a sequence becomes a list of strings. Each entry is checked independently: for a sequence, every entry must pass or the whole condition, and therefore the whole document, fails. For each entry, everything before the first @ is the mod reference, trimmed of surrounding whitespace. Everything after @, if present, is parsed as an SML semver range (>=1.2.3, ^1.2.0, ~1.2.0, exact 1.2.3, || unions, see Conditions & Packs) and checked against that mod's actual loaded version. No @ means the mod just needs to be loaded, any version. hasMod calls UModLoadingLibrary::GetLoadedModInfo(ModReference, …). The reference has to match the mod's actual plugin reference or id exactly, case-sensitive, not a display name.

sections.heading: Requiring mods while excluding another mod or version
sections.text: Use a condition array to separate positive requirements from negated requirements: conditions: - hasMod: - KAPI - KLib - hasMod: IncompatibleMod ifNotMatch: true This applies only when KAPI and KLib are both loaded and IncompatibleMod is absent. The two objects are AND-combined by default. ifNotMatch defaults to false and negates only the object where it is written. Add an inline range to exclude only matching versions: conditions: - hasMod: - KAPI - KLib - hasMod: 'OptionalIntegration@^2.0.0' ifNotMatch: true The inverted object passes when OptionalIntegration is absent or when its loaded version does not match ^2.0.0. It fails only when a matching 2.x version is loaded. The explicit map form works too: conditions: - modVersion: OptionalIntegration: '^2.0.0' ifNotMatch: true ifNotMatch negates the entire object's AND result. For example, this passes unless both mods are loaded: conditions: - hasMod: - ModA - ModB ifNotMatch: true To require that neither ModA nor ModB is loaded, use two independently inverted objects instead. Unknown keys, malformed value types, invalid ranges, and a non-boolean ifNotMatch remain configuration errors; inversion never turns them into a match.

sections.heading: Choosing AND or OR across condition objects
sections.text: conditionBehaivor sits beside conditions: and accepts AND or OR case-insensitively. It defaults to AND, preserving packs written before this option existed. Correctly spelled conditionBehavior is also accepted as an alias. conditionBehaivor: OR conditions: - hasMod: RefinedPower - hasMod: FicsitFarming This document applies when either mod is loaded. With AND, both would be required. KDataForge evaluates each object's internal keys, applies its ifNotMatch, then combines final object results. That makes mixed positive/negative alternatives possible: conditionBehaivor: OR conditions: - hasMod: RefinedPower - hasMod: LegacyPowerBridge ifNotMatch: true This applies when RefinedPower is loaded or LegacyPowerBridge is absent. Invalid behavior values, unknown keys, malformed objects, and invalid ranges always fail closed; a matching OR branch cannot hide them. An empty condition array passes under AND and fails under OR.

sections.heading: Difference between `modVersion:` and `hasMod`
sections.text: modVersion: is an explicit map form: conditions: modVersion: SML: '>=3.12.0' KAPI: '>=2026.0.0' Reading the evaluator, modVersion doesn't do anything structurally different from hasMod. For every Ref: range entry it builds the exact string "Ref@range" and calls the same EvaluateHasMod function hasMod uses. There is no separate "this is a hard dependency, so assume it's present and only check the version" code path. Presence is checked every time, for both forms. | | hasMod (with a pin) | modVersion | | Under the hood | EvaluateHasMod("Ref@range", …) | Builds "Ref@range" per map entry, calls the same EvaluateHasMod | | If the mod isn't loaded at all | Document skipped (Info) | Identical, document skipped (Info), not a harder failure | | Idiomatic use | One or two optional integrations, inline | Several version constraints stated together, typically for mods you already expect to be present | Practically, use hasMod (bare or pinned) for content that's genuinely optional: a mod you have not declared anywhere as a dependency of your own plugin. Reach for modVersion when you want to state, in one readable block, the version floor for several mods you already treat as real dependencies, whether declared in your own .uplugin or bundled together in a modpack. It reads better than several separate hasMod entries, but **it will not error louder if one of those mods turns out to be missing.** If a mod is truly required for your pack to make sense at all, that's a job for your .uplugin's own Plugins: dependency list. SML refuses to load your mod if a _real_ dependency is missing. conditions: only ever produces a quiet per-document skip, never a hard failure.

sections.heading: `hasClass:` gating on a class existing, no mod dependency needed
sections.text: conditions: hasClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGBuildableFrackingActivator # scalar one class For several classes, use a sequence; every class must exist: conditions: hasClass: # sequence ALL must exist - /Script/RefinedPower.RPWindTurbine - /Game/FicsitFarming/Buildable/FarmPlot/Build_FarmPlot.Build_FarmPlot_C hasClass resolves each entry with the exact same class-path resolver KDataForge uses for every target:/class:/parent: reference elsewhere (FKDFValueCodec::ResolveClass). It accepts a full /Script/Module.Class or /Game/....Asset_C path, with an automatic _C retry for Blueprint classes written without the suffix. As a last resort, for name-only input with no / or . at all, it falls back to a bare-class-name lookup against whatever's currently loaded in memory. Ambiguous matches log an error and pick the first sorted match, so use full paths in anything you publish. The reason hasClass exists alongside hasMod is what happens when the check **fails silently vs. loudly**. A cdo document whose target: (or allAssetsOfClass:) points at a class that doesn't resolve produces an Error diagnostic: the class was expected to be there and wasn't. Wrap the same patch in a conditions: block with hasClass: and a missing class instead produces the quiet Info-level "skipped by conditions" message, and nothing else happens. That's the whole value of hasClass for optional integration: it turns "this class doesn't exist" from a load error into an expected, silent no-op. It does that without your pack, or its .uplugin if it has one, needing to declare a dependency on the other mod at all, since you're checking for the class directly rather than asking SML whether a specific plugin id is loaded.

sections.heading: Combining conditions in one block (AND)
sections.text: Every key inside one conditions: map is ANDed together, so you can require several independent things at once: type: schematic conditions: hasMod: KAPI gameVersion: '>=416000.0.0' schematics: - id: Schematic_KAPIBonusResearch properties: mDisplayName: KAPI Integration Research # ... unlocks a recipe that only makes sense once KAPI's data assets exist This schematic only applies when both KAPI is loaded and the game build is recent enough. If either one is false, the whole document (research entry, unlock, everything) is skipped as a unit, with one Info diagnostic naming whichever condition failed first.

sections.heading: Worked scenario: base content + two independent optional integrations
sections.text: A pack that always ships a base item, then layers on two independent bonuses: one gated by hasMod, one by hasClass. Neither blocks the other, or the base item, if its target mod is missing.

sections.heading: (a) The base item: always applies, no conditions
sections.text: # file: super-ingot.item.yml (excerpt no conditions: key at all) type: item items: - id: SuperIngot parent: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/Parts/IronIngot/Desc_IronIngot.Desc_IronIngot_C properties: mDisplayName: Super Ingot Every player gets the item, the recipe, and the schematic that unlocks it. See Item + Icon + Recipe + Tier-1 Unlock for that full chain. Nothing about it depends on any other mod.

sections.heading: (b) A KAPI data asset: only if KAPI is loaded
sections.text: # file: super-ingot-cleaner.dataasset.yml type: dataasset conditions: hasMod: KAPI assets: - id: CleanerItem_SuperIngot class: /Script/KAPI.KAPICleanerItemDescription properties: mProductionTime: 6.0 mInFluid: ItemClass: /Game/FactoryGame/Resource/RawResources/Water/Desc_Water.Desc_Water_C Amount: 500 This is the standard shape for KAPI-integrated content. See Data Assets for the full field reference. If KAPI isn't installed, this document is skipped and the base item from (a) is completely unaffected.

sections.heading: (c) A RefinedPower patch: only if the class exists
sections.text: # file: refinedpower-windturbine-boost.cdo.yml type: cdo conditions: hasClass: /Script/RefinedPower.RPWindTurbine patches: - target: /Script/RefinedPower.RPWindTurbine applyToSubclasses: true properties: mMaxTurbinePowerProduction: $op: multiply value: 1.25 This pack never lists RefinedPower as a dependency anywhere. hasClass checks for the actual ARPTurbineBaseActor-derived class at load time and skips cleanly (Info, no error) if it's absent. This follows the same no-hard-dependency philosophy as the RRDA data asset integration pattern. That pattern gates on hasMod: RefinedRDApi because it's patching RRDA's own data assets, whose consumer rescan already runs by reflection. Here, we go one level more direct and gate on the RefinedPower class itself with hasClass. This is useful whenever you want to touch another mod's actual buildable/actor class rather than a data asset built for cross-mod integration. Three independent documents, three independent outcomes: (a) always applies, (b) applies only with KAPI, (c) applies only with RefinedPower present. Any subset, "only (a)", "(a)+(b)", "(a)+(c)", or all three, is a valid, error-free load depending on what is installed.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - A document seems to be silently doing nothing, no errors anywhere. This is very likely a failed condition. Today, /kdf report only prints Warning/Error diagnostics and only counts those two severities in its summary line. A condition failure is Info severity and is filtered out of both, so there's no explicit "Skipped by conditions" line to read in the chat output right now. The indirect tell is the summary's "N document(s) applied" count: a condition-skipped document never gets counted there. So if that number is lower than the number of .yml files you expect to apply, a condition mismatch on one of them is the most likely cause. Temporarily delete the conditions: block to confirm the rest of the document is otherwise correct, then reintroduce it. - A condition that should pass never does. The single most common cause is a typo'd mod reference: hasMod/modVersion match the mod's exact plugin reference, case-sensitive (KAPI, not Kapi or kapi). Double check the spelling against the actual mod's .uplugin SemVersion/reference id, not its display name in the mod list. - hasClass never passes even though the mod is definitely installed. Check for a missing _C on a Blueprint class, or a class that only exists in a newer/older version of that mod than what's installed. hasClass checks the class as it exists right now, not a version range, so pair it with hasMod: OtherMod@>=X.Y.Z in the same block if you need both. - Want the load to hard-fail instead of quietly skipping when a mod is missing? conditions: never does that, by design: diagnostics are never fatal. If a mod is a genuine hard requirement, declare it in your own .uplugin's dependency list instead. SML will refuse to load your mod at all rather than silently skip content. Conditions & Packs is the syntax reference for condition keys, pack.yml, redirects:, and include:. Data Assets documents type: dataasset and the RefinedR&D integration pattern used above.

pages.title: Debug a pack that won't apply
