sections.text: # file: myoverhaul-tag-batch-a.cdo.yml type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Constructor/Recipe_IronPlate.Recipe_IronPlate_C properties: mGameplayTags: $op: append value: - MyOverhaul.Rebalanced - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Constructor/Recipe_IronRod.Recipe_IronRod_C properties: mGameplayTags: $op: append value: - MyOverhaul.Rebalanced # file: myoverhaul-tag-batch-b.cdo.yml type: cdo patches: - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Constructor/Recipe_Wire.Recipe_Wire_C properties: mGameplayTags: $op: append value: - MyOverhaul.Rebalanced - target: /Game/FactoryGame/Recipes/Constructor/Recipe_Screw.Recipe_Screw_C properties: mGameplayTags: $op: append value: - MyOverhaul.Rebalanced That's two files and four recipes, with no coordination between them beyond both existing. This is the point: tagging is additive, and it doesn't care which file or which pack a given target was tagged from.

sections.heading: Your own freshly generated content: tag it in its OWN document, not a separate `cdo` patch
sections.text: If a recipe is one you're generating in this same pack (type: recipe, id: form), put mGameplayTags straight into that document's own properties: instead of writing a follow-up cdo patch for it: # file: my-recipe.recipe.yml type: recipe recipes: - id: Recipe_MyThing properties: mDisplayName: My Thing mGameplayTags: - MyOverhaul.Rebalanced # … mIngredients, mProduct, mManufactoringDuration, mProducedIn … Only this version is guaranteed to work on the first load. See Step 3 and Troubleshooting for why a separate cdo patch targeting a same-pass generated recipe doesn't resolve on that first load.

sections.heading: Step 3: the bulk patch: `matchTag` + `ofClass` + `tagProperty`
sections.text: # file: myoverhaul-rebalance.cdo.yml type: cdo include: - myoverhaul-tag-batch-a.cdo.yml - myoverhaul-tag-batch-b.cdo.yml patches: - matchTag: MyOverhaul.Rebalanced ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGRecipe tagProperty: mGameplayTags properties: mManufactoringDuration: $op: multiply value: 0.8 # 20% faster myoverhaul-tag-batch-a.cdo.yml and myoverhaul-tag-batch-b.cdo.yml are both cdo documents, in the same CDOChanges stage as the bulk patch, so they need explicit include: ordering here. That's different from the gametag file in Step 1. GameTags is a stage that always finishes before CDOChanges even starts, so it never needs an include: entry. Two cdo documents in the same stage need one whenever one depends on the other having already run.

sections.heading: The worked scenario, end to end
sections.text: Four vanilla recipes, tagged from two files, sped up 20% by one bulk patch: myoverhaul-tags.gametag.yml registers MyOverhaul.Rebalanced. myoverhaul-tag-batch-a.cdo.yml tags Recipe_IronPlate and Recipe_IronRod. myoverhaul-tag-batch-b.cdo.yml tags Recipe_Wire and Recipe_Screw. myoverhaul-rebalance.cdo.yml scans FGRecipe with matchTag for the tag and multiplies mManufactoringDuration by 0.8. Add a fifth recipe to the tag next month. That's one more target: line in whichever tagging file makes sense, with zero changes to myoverhaul-rebalance.cdo.yml. The patch keeps applying to "everything tagged MyOverhaul.Rebalanced," not to a fixed list. A self-contained version of this exact pattern uses four real vanilla recipes, one gametag file, and one cdo file. It applies tag-then-matchTag in a single document instead of splitting across files, since ops inside one document's patches: list apply top-to-bottom. It looks like this: rebalance-tags.gametag.yml + rebalance-vanilla-recipes.cdo.yml.

sections.heading: When to reach for a native `KMods.*` tag instead of your own
sections.text: KAPI already registers a set of native tags: KMods.AlternateRecipe, KMods.EventOnly, KMods.Deprecated, KMods.WIP, KMods.Cheat, KMods.Disabled, KMods.ExcludeFromNodeRandomization, KMods.PlannerExclude, and KMods.WikiExclude. See the full list in Data Assets → KMods native gameplay tags, and a worked matchTag example against them in Balancing → Buffing all alternate recipes. | Use a native KMods.* tag when… | Register your own tag when… | | You want content that's ALREADY carrying the tag (e.g. every alternate recipe in the game, tagged by KAPI/other KMods) | You're marking content you're touching: nothing upstream tags it for you | | The category is a general, cross-pack concept (deprecated, WIP, event-only, cheat) | The category is specific to your pack's own balance pass or content set | | You're fine gating the whole document behind hasMod: KAPI | You don't want a KAPI dependency at all | The two aren't mutually exclusive. A single matchTag: list can include both, for example matchTag: with block-sequence entries KMods.AlternateRecipe and MyOverhaul.Rebalanced, remembering that's an AND: "alternates that are ALSO mine." Native tags always require a conditions: block with hasMod: KAPI on the document, since they don't exist without KAPI loaded. Your own tags never need any hasMod gate.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: - Tag not registering / "Invalid tag" at load time. The error includes the engine's own suggested fix, usually a stray space or extra dot in the dotted tag string. Fix the YAML string, not the tag. See Game Tags → Troubleshooting. - matchTag matched no objects: check ofClass first. ofClass has to be the class the tagged content is, or an ancestor of it. ofClass: /Script/FactoryGame.FGSchematic will never match a recipe's tags, even if the tag name is identical. Confirm with /kdf report which classes were scoped. - matchTag matched no objects: check tagProperty next. If a class exposes a tag container under a non-standard name, an unnamed or mis-typed tagProperty silently finds nothing rather than erroring. The lookup fails closed, not loud. - matchTag matched no objects, and the target is content YOU generated in the SAME pack. type: cdo runs before the content-generation stages. A matchTag scan cannot discover a class that this initialization pass has not generated yet. Put the tag and initial property values in the generated entry's properties: block. Do not rely on a later session: short-id and tag discovery still happen before generation. An exact canonical generated-class path can be watched and patched when that class is created, but this is a narrow lazy-resolution mechanism, not general cross-stage ordering. Inline properties are the predictable solution. - **A KMods.* tag "doesn't exist", or the whole document silently skips.** You forgot a conditions: block with hasMod: KAPI. Without KAPI loaded, KAPI's own tags never register, so matchTag: KMods.AlternateRecipe fails with "unknown gameplay tag." If you _did_ gate the document, a missing KAPI install just skips it quietly, an Info diagnostic in /kdf report, not an error, rather than breaking your pack. Game Tags covers registration mechanics, ordering, and session initialization. Targeting catalogs every selector, including matchTag with ofClass, target:, and allAssetsOfClass:. For more bulk-edit examples, including the native KMods.* alternate-recipe buff, see Balancing.
